query_text:
The novel opens in early 1945. Peter Marlowe, a young British RAF Flight Lieutenant, has been a P.O.W. since 1942. Marlowe comes to the attention of the "King" - an American corporal who has become the most successful trader and black marketeer in Changi - when King sees him conversing in Malay. Marlowe's languages, intelligence, honesty, and personality cause King to befriend him and attempt to involve him in black market deals, which bring Marlowe to the attention of Robin Grey, a British officer and Provost Marshal of the camp, who has developed a Javert-like obsession with King and hopes to arrest him for violating camp regulations. Grey is attempting to maintain military discipline among the prisoners and sees King as the antithesis of his beliefs. As the son of a working-class family, Grey follows the rules for their own sake, using his position as Provost Marshal to gain a status otherwise unavailable to him in British society.
Despite being an enlisted man and undistinguished in civilian life, King has become a major power in the closed society of the P.O.W. camp through his charisma and intelligence. Trading with Korean guards, local Malay villagers, and other prisoners for food, clothing, information, and what few luxuries are available, King keeps himself and his fellow American prisoners alive. Senior officers come to him for help in selling their valuables to buy food, and other officers are secretly on his payroll. Marlowe is initially put off by King's perspective and behaviour, which clash with the British upper class ideals he has been taught. He turns down a lucrative business partnership with King because "Marlowes aren't tradesmen. It just isn't done, old boy". Marlowe soon understands that King is not the thief and con artist that Grey would have him believe. Rather, King asks for the best of each man and rewards him accordingly, irrespective of class or position.
Through the experiences of Marlowe, King, and other characters, the novel offers a vivid, often disturbing portrayal of men brought to the edge of survival by a brutal environment. The P.O.W.s are given nothing by the Japanese other than filthy huts to live in and the bare minimum of food. Officers from various parts of Britain's Asian empire, accustomed to having native servants provide them with freshly laundered uniforms daily, are reduced to wearing rags and homemade shoes. For most, the chief concern is obtaining enough food to stay alive from day to day and avoiding disease or injury, since almost no medical care is available. Some are degraded and come close to losing their humanity, while others display levels of courage and compassion beyond expectations. Some literally steal food out the mouths of their comrades, while others give away what they have or take terrible risks to help their friends.
King decides he and his friends should breed rats to sell for food. His comrades, though nearly starving themselves, are repulsed at the idea of eating rat meat, so King comes up with the plan of only selling the meat to officers without telling them the true source. A group of officers who stole money from their underlings are later seen greedily enjoying a meal of what they are told is mouse deer (rusa tikus in Malay), not knowing they are actually eating rat meat. When the camp is ultimately liberated, most of the soldiers have trouble adjusting to freedom. King loses his power and is shunned by the others. Grey ironically thanks King on the grounds that his hatred of King was the only thing keeping him alive. At the end the rats are abandoned in their cages when the camp is abandoned. The final scene has the rats consuming each other one by one, with the final survivor becoming "king of the rats".
option_0_text:
Roger Brown (Aksel Hennie), Norway's most successful headhunter, supports his lavish lifestyle by stealing paintings from his clients; his partner, Ove (Eivind Sander), works at a surveillance company and deactivates security at the victims' homes, allowing Roger to swap the art for a counterfeit. Asked to dinner by his mistress, Lotte (Julie Ølgaard), Roger declines and ends their relationship. Roger's wife and art gallery owner, Diana (Synnøve Macody Lund), introduces him to Clas Greve (Nikolaj Coster-Waldau), a former executive for GPS tech company HOTE. Roger, currently seeking to recruit the next CEO of rival firm Pathfinder, recognizes Clas may be a suitable candidate. Diana reveals that Clas has asked her to authenticate a lost Rubens painting he inherited that is believed to be worth millions.
Roger convinces Clas to meet with him over lunch to discuss the job, and soon learns Clas used to be a member of TRACK, a special forces unit that specialized in tracking people, and winner of the European Military pentathlon. He also learns that Clas helped HOTE develop a nanotechnology GPS tracking gel that is difficult to remove. Despite his misgivings, Roger meets with Ove to work out details on stealing the painting. Roger manages to steal it from Clas' home, but he discovers Diana's cellphone beside Clas' bed, implying the two of them are having an affair due to Roger's refusal to have children with Diana. In retaliation, after a seemingly successful meeting with Pathfinder executives, an upset Roger flippantly informs Clas that the company may be looking for someone else to fill the position.
The next morning, Roger finds Ove in his (Roger's) car, apparently dead from a poison syringe embedded in the car seat; just as Roger dumps Ove in a lake, Ove recovers, as he did not get a full dose of the poison. Driving Ove to his cabin, Roger puts him in bed and ignores his demands for medical attention, as he does not want the police involved. Ove pulls a gun in response, causing a shoot-out where Roger accidentally kills Ove. Finding Clas has followed him to Ove's cabin, Roger narrowly escapes after a scuffle. After realising Clas may have used HOTE's GPS gel technology on him, Roger switches his car for Ove's and throws his clothes in a lake, changing into Ove's spare uniform and fleeing to a farm where Ove used to stay. Nevertheless, Clas tails Roger to the farm with his dog and murders the farmer, but Roger evades them. Trying to escape on a tractor, Roger is attacked by Clas' dog, which he kills by impaling it on the tractor's forks. Roger, believing Clas is still chasing him, drives erratically and falls from the tractor, only to find his pursuer is a stranger wanting to help.
Waking in a hospital, Roger learns the police think he is Ove, and arrest him for the farmer's murder when he tries to escape. Driving to the station, the officers pull over to block a truck reported stolen. Roger realizes that Clas is driving the truck, and that Diana may have helped Clas by rubbing the GPS gel into Roger's hair. With Clas approaching, the officers ignore Roger's protests, allowing Clas to ram the car off a cliff. Playing dead until Clas leaves the scene, Roger shaves his head and hides his hair on a deceased officer's body, then swaps clothes with a detective's disfigured body to fake his death.
Roger turns to Lotte for help, only to discover she is working for Clas. Clas, who is still secretly employed by HOTE, was planning to use Roger to get the Pathfinder job and steal their secret technologies. Lotte admits that she put the GPS gel in Roger's hair, absolving Diana, and that she suggested dinner so she could introduce him to Clas; since Roger ended their affair, Clas used a counterfeit Rubens painting to meet Roger through Diana. When Roger lets his guard down, Lotte attacks him with a knife, causing Roger to shoot and kill her in self-defense. Roger returns home and admits everything to Diana, who apologizes for her affair with Clas. The next morning, Roger goes to a morgue to retrieve the remaining evidence linking him to the murders (his cut hair), while Diana contacts Clas to ostensibly resume their affair.
While cleaning Ove's cabin of evidence, Roger is confronted by Clas, who was able to track the GPS gel in the cut hair. Clas gloats that Diana has returned to him, and tries to shoot Roger but fails. Roger fatally wounds Clas with a hidden gun, explaining that Diana only resumed their affair so she could load Clas' gun with blanks. Ove's home security records Clas involved in a shootout, though Roger stays in a camera blind spot near Ove. The footage, combined with evidence doctored by Roger, suggests Ove and Clas were art thieves who killed the farmer, Lotte, then finally each other after a dispute. The police, including star detective Brede Sperre, ignore the minor inconsistencies (Ove's time of death being days earlier than what is implied by the video footage) because Brede knows that leaving the case unsolved would harm his growing reputation. Later, Roger and a visibly pregnant Diana are shown selling their house, and Roger returns to work, giving the Pathfinder job to the client he rejected and robbed at the beginning of the film.
option_1_text: Set during World War II, the novel describes the struggle for survival of a group of Western POWs - Americans, Australians, Dutch and New Zealanders - in a Japanese camp in Singapore. The story is based on Clavell's own autobiographical experience of the three years of imprisonment in the Changi camp: one of the protagonists, Peter Marlowe, is inspired by the young Clavell. While it's possible that the character of "the king" is based on a real-life prisoner named Theodore "Ted" Lewin, whose exploits are very similar to those of the king.
option_2_text:
On July 2, 1937, Amelia Earhart (Hilary Swank) and her navigator, Fred Noonan (Christopher Eccleston), are on the last leg of an around-the-world flight. Moving in vignettes from her early years when Earhart was captivated by the sight of an aircraft flying overhead on the Kansas prairie where she grew up, her life over the preceding decade gradually unfolds.
As a young woman, Earhart is recruited by publishing tycoon and eventual husband, George Putnam (Richard Gere) to become the first woman to cross the Atlantic Ocean, albeit as a passenger. Taking command of the flight results in success and she is thrust into the limelight as the most famous woman pilot of her time. Putnam helps Earhart write a book chronicling the flight, much like his earlier triumph with Charles Lindbergh's We. She gradually falls in love with him and they eventually marry, although she enacts a "cruel" pledge as her wedding contract.
Embarrassed that her fame was not earned, Earhart commences to set myriad aviation records, and in 1932, recreates her earlier transatlantic flight, becoming the first female pilot to fly solo across the Atlantic. Throughout a decade of notoriety, Earhart falls into an awkward love affair with pilot and future Federal Aviation administrator Gene Vidal (Ewan McGregor). In a display of romantic jealousy, Putnam quietly tells Amelia that he does not want Vidal in his house. Annoyed by the seemingly endless agenda of celebrity appearances and endorsements, Putnam reminds her it funds her flying.
Earhart returns to her husband on the eve of her last momentous flight, her biggest and most dangerous adventure to date, to fly around the world. Earhart's first attempt ends in a runway crash in Hawaii, due to a collapsed landing gear, and her aircraft requires extensive repairs before the flight can be attempted again. Eventually, she takes the repaired Lockheed Model 10 Electra, sponsored by Purdue University, in a reverse direction, leaving the lengthy trans-Pacific crossing for the end.
Setting out to refuel at tiny Howland Island, radio transmissions between USCGC Itasca, a Coast Guard picket ship, and Earhart's aircraft reveal a rising crisis; the Coast Guard radio operators realize they do not have sufficient length to provide a "fix". Itasca has a directional finder with a dead battery, and weak radio communications prevent Earhart and USCGC Itasca from making contact. Running low on fuel, Earhart and Noonan fly on. They disappear. A massive search effort is unsuccessful, but solidifies Earhart as an aviation icon.
option_3_text:
Notorious womanizer Michael James (Peter O' Toole) wants to be faithful to his fiancée Carole Werner (Romy Schneider), but every woman he meets seems to fall in love with him, including neurotic exotic dancer Liz Bien (Paula Prentiss) and parachutist Rita (Ursula Andress), who accidentally lands in his car. His psychoanalyst, Dr. Fritz Fassbender (Peter Sellers), cannot help, since he is stalking patient Renée Lefebvre (Capucine), who in turn longs for Michael. Carole, meanwhile, decides to make Michael jealous by flirting with his nervous wreck of a friend, Victor Shakapopulis (Woody Allen). Victor struggles to be romantic but Carole nevertheless feigns interest.
Fassbender continues to have group meetings with his neurotics and obsessives and cannot understand why everyone falls for Michael. The group sessions get stranger—including an indoor cricket match. Michael dreams that all his sexual conquests simultaneously bombard him for attention, listing where they made love.
Fassbender goes to the River Seine and fills a rowing boat with kerosene and wraps himself in the Norwegian flag - preparing to commit suicide in the style of a Viking funeral. Victor appears and sets up a small dining table nearby and asks what he is doing. Distracted, Fassbender forgets his idea of suicide and starts giving Victor advice. Despite his attempts to womanise, Fassbender is revealed to be married with three children.
Meanwhile, Carole's plan seems to work and Michael asks to marry her. She agrees and they settle on marrying within the week. She moves in but Michael finds fidelity impossible.
When a second "fiancée" arrives, she knows the worst. Simultaneously, a woman parachutes into Michael's open-top sports car and he ends up sleeping with her, also meeting other conquests at the bar. This takes place at a small country hotel, where all parties materialise in the format of a typical French farce. Some are checked in, but most just appear. This includes Carole's parents who wander the corridors, causing Michael to jump from room to room. A rumour has also started locally that an orgy is taking place so side characters such as the petrol station attendant also start to appear. Carole appears and wishes to see Michael's room. As they speak, all the other participants chase each other around in the background. Fassbender's wife tracks him down.
Everyone ends in Michael's room with most of the women half-naked. The police arrive and form a line. Anna—Dr. Fassbender's wife, played by Eddra Gale—charges in operatic Valkyrie costume, complete with a spear. They all escape to a go-kart circuit. They leave the circuit and go first to a farmyard then through narrow village streets still on the go-karts then back to the circuit.
After a mayor marries Michael and Carole in a civil marriage ceremony, the couple are signing the marriage certificate when Michael calls the young female registrar "Pussycat", infuriating Carole. They leave and Fassbender attempts to court her instead.
option_4_text: Three friends, in their senior year of college, decide to go to the Mardi Gras party, a typical New Orleans carnival party, where for each necklace of pearls, a girl is required to show her breasts.

query_text: End of the 17th century. A proud nobleman refuses to kiss the hand of the despotic King James II of England, who orders his buffoon Barkilphedro to get rid of him, for which he will be cruelly executed and his son surgically disfigured.
option_0_text:
The film is set in a small town with the fictitious name of Châteauneuf. In the opening scene, we see about 15-year-old schoolgirl Catherine Roussel walking home from school crying. At the request of her parents, she explains that her teacher Jean Doucet sexually abused her. He vehemently denies the charge. However, when other students in the class are questioned, the girl's statement is confirmed, as two other students make similar accusations, including Helène Arnaud, the best in class and the daughter of a construction contractor. The mayor, wanting to avoid a scandal, advises Doucet to leave the place, but he refuses, as it would be tantamount to an admission of guilt. Eventually, he is arrested and sent to prison for further investigation. He faces life imprisonment in a penal colony.
Doucet's wife Suzanne, who is convinced of her husband's innocence and knows the inhabitants of the village well, now interrogates them in detail and discovers the true backgrounds and connections.
In the end, Jean Doucet is released, but declares that he no longer wants to live in the village. His wife, who had long wanted to leave the small town anyway, is delighted.
option_1_text:
It's 1977. After a difficult childhood and adolescence, eighteen-year-old Scott Thorson travels to Los Angeles to look for work as a veterinarian; here, in a gay bar, he meets theater producer Bob Black, who invites him to Las Vegas to attend a show of his friend, the famous pianist Liberace, at the time at the peak of his fame. Scott is introduced to the pianist, who is immediately fascinated by him; offering him to care for his elderly dog, the young man begins to frequent his sumptuous residence: soon the two will begin to exchange confidences and intimacy, until they begin a real relationship.
Scott declares to Liberace that he is bisexual, while Liberace replies that he has always been homosexual, despite hiding it from the public; the pianist is also a fervent Catholic despite the fact that the Church does not approve of homosexual relationships: he tells him of the meeting he had years earlier with a messenger of God, after which he was convinced that God loves him as he is. Liberace is very fond of Scott, takes him to live with him and covers him with jewelry and other precious gifts; later he will make him perform in his show and will even propose to adopt him, without success.
Little by little, however, the dark side of Liberace emerges, obsessed with his public image to the point of paying his manager Seymour profusely to invent any excuse to justify the absence of a woman at his side. The pianist is also morbidly jealous of his physical appearance, so much so that he undergoes drastic diets and continuous plastic surgery, forcing Scott to do the same to become a "younger version" of him; however, this will create a gradual fracture in the couple as Scott, to lose weight, begins to use amphetamines in increasing doses. The boy will end up paying for his doses by selling the jewels given to him by Liberace, and having frequent bouts of nervousness because of which Liberace will gradually distance himself from him.
The couple's crisis lasts until 1982: Scott is now totally addicted to drugs and, although he continues to live in Liberace's house, there is no longer any relationship between the two. When the pianist becomes infatuated with the young singer Cary-James, he begins to regularly cheat on Scott, even on the day he is in Los Angeles for his adoptive mother's funeral. This causes a violent reaction from Scott, following which the two separate. In 1984 a bitter legal battle takes place in which Scott sues Liberace for defamation, demanding the conversion into money of the properties titled to him in the years of their relationship; all he gets is a decent sum of money and some gifts offered in exchange for silence on his relationship with Liberace.
Scott returns to live a much more modest and secluded life than he did with Liberace. In December 1986 he receives a call from the latter, who, knowing that he is dying due to AIDS contracted some time ago, asks him to see him one last time. The two ex-lovers manage to say a final goodbye before Liberace dies, on February 4, 1987; despite Seymour's efforts to keep the illness hidden, the true cause of his death soon emerges. At the funeral, Scott imagines Liberace performing in his final, lavish show before soaring off to heaven.
option_2_text:
In England in the late 17th century, King James II got rid of his enemy, Lord Clancharlie, and sold his young son, Gwynplaine, to child traffickers who disfigured him. The boy runs away and rescues a blind baby, Dea, from the cold.
Both are taken in by Ursus, an outsider. Gwynplaine, nicknamed  The Laughing Man, became a famous travelling comedian. His destiny will change when he later discovers, during the reign of Queen Anne, his noble origins.
option_3_text: Roger Brown is leading a double life. Norway's most talented bounty hunter, he's also a painting thief. When his wife introduces him to senior executive and former mercenary Clas Greve, Roger sees an opportunity to steal a valuable canvas from him. But the latter will prove to be a more than dangerous adversary.
option_4_text: When tragedy strikes three families, their destiny forces them on a converging path to discover God's love, grace and mercy as the challenges of their fate could also resurrect their beliefs.

The man eventually manages to free himself, but is warned that the politician is gravely afflicted with a brain tumor and needs immediate surgery. Meanwhile, the rebel Gonzales kidnaps Ferguson's wife, threatening to kill her if her husband performs the operation.
option_0_text: Dr. Ferguson and his wife, Helen, were on vacation in a Latin American country when they were dragged by the military to the Presidential Palace. The head of state, Raoul Farrago, is a dictator. He's on short-term disability from a brain tumor, unless Ferguson attempts a last-chance surgery. The surgeon hesitates, but his sense of duty compels him to accept. That's when opponents of the regime abduct Helen and inform Ferguson that she will be executed if the President survives this operation...
option_1_text: In 1951, Marcus left his native New Jersey to study at a conservative university in Ohio, where he faced sexual repression and anti-Semitism.
option_2_text:
Pather Panchali is primarily a depiction of life in India during the 1920s. The focus of this film is the lives of Apu (name and surname: Apurba Kumar Raj) and his family members.
The story narrates the life of a poor Brahmin family. The father, Hariharan, is a priest who cannot earn enough money to support his family. The mother, Sarbajaya, has the primary responsibility of raising her mischievous daughter Durga and caring for her elderly sister-in-law named Indir, whose independent spirit sometimes irritates her. With Apu's arrival, scenes of joy and games enrich their daily life, occasionally interrupted by tragedy (e.g. Indir's death). However, life is a struggle, and that's why Harihar must find a new job and leave. Sarbajaya is alone, stressed and has to fight for the survival of her family. In addition, the life of this family is marked by the turbulence of the monsoon. The final disaster, Durga's death, results in the family's departure from the village in search of a new life in Benares.
The film suggests an intimate relationship between loss and development, or between destruction and creation. Another theme of Pather Panchali will be the pursuit of progress (e.g. arrival of the train to the village, wishes for a happy wedding).
option_3_text:
During the Mexican-American War, Captain John Boyd (Guy Pearce) is transferred to an isolated fort in California by General Slauson after committing an ambiguous act of bravery: he seized an enemy command post but only after faking his own death because he was terrified. Arriving at his new assignment, Boyd and the dwindling garrison are picked up from the fort by a strange, traumatized individual, Colqhoun (Robert Carlyle), who recounts the cannibalistic acts he and his fellow travelers had to resort to while trapped in a cave for several weeks. Colonel Hart, commander of the fort, decided to lead an expedition to the cave to rescue any survivors. George, the Indian scout, warns them of the curse of the wendigo that befalls those who have eaten human flesh.
Arriving on the scene, Boyd and Private Reich descend into the cave and as Colqhoun's behaviour grows increasingly strange. Boyd and Reich discover that Colqhoun has murdered all his fellow travelers and led them into a trap. Colqhoun kills one by one all the members of the expedition (George, Colonel Hart and soldiers Toffler and Reich) except Boyd, who manages to escape him by jumping off a cliff. Boyd, who broke his leg, must feed on Reich's corpse to survive. He manages to return to the fort after regaining his strength but no one believes his story. A new commander arrives, and that new commander, Colonel Ives, is none other than Colqhoun. Ives tells Boyd his story: as a tuberculosis patient, he learned the legend of the wendigo and attempted cannibalism. He felt refreshed and healed.
Private Cleaves and Major Knox are killed and it turns out that Ives had only seriously wounded Hart before saving him by having him consume the flesh of his soldiers. Boyd, Ives and Hart are now the only three occupants of the fort as George's sister Martha has gone to fetch General Slauson. Ives now wants to convert Boyd to his cause and stabs him in the abdomen leaving him the choice of eating or dying. Boyd eventually relents and heals from his wound but still refuses to become a cannibal permanently and is locked up. He frees himself with the help of Hart, who can't stand his condition, and kills him at his request. He then fights Ives and the two men inflict serious injuries on each other. They end up nailed to the ground by a bear trap and bleeding to death. Ives warns Boyd that he'll eat it if Boyd dies first. But it is Ives who takes the last breath and Boyd, who refuses to engage in cannibalism again, in turn expires on the corpse of his opponent. The epilogue shows General Slauson smelling with delight the stew of human flesh left on the fire, while Martha, who discovered the bodies of Boyd and Ives, flees the fort.
option_4_text:
Cold War, late '40s, early '50s. A Soviet defector has flown his jet fighter from his base in the far east of Siberia across the Bering Strait and landed on an American airfield. The commander of the air base in Alaska, Air Force Colonel Jim Shannon, is very surprised when he faces the pilot: It's a woman! Her name is Anna Marladovna, she's an air force lieutenant, and she's very pretty. Although Anna is seeking political asylum, she is not prepared to betray her old home and divulge military secrets. Shannon should therefore, on behalf of Washington, treat the Russian woman courteously, indulge her with capitalist conquests such as steaks and champagne, and beyond that, try to seduce her. In fact, the unequal couple fall in love. Fearing that Anna might be deported by the American authorities due to her unwillingness to cooperate, Shannon suddenly decides to marry the beautiful defector without the necessary approval from the Air Force. Then the two lovebirds go on their honeymoon to Palm Springs.
When Shannon returns to the air base, his superior, Major General Black, informs him that his wife is most likely a Soviet spy who is spying on him and the military base. You decide to play Anna's game and give her false information. When Shannon returns home to his wife one day to tell her that the American side plans to throw her behind bars for several years and then deport her to the Soviet Union, he presents her with an alternative plan (quite obviously agreed with Shannon's superiors): Jim and his wife drive to the base, steal a jet fighter and take off for Siberia until they are safe from their American pursuers over Soviet territory and land on Anna's home airfield. Anna's superiors welcome Lieutenant Marladovna and take good care of her American "companion" Shannon. Both will be housed in shabby barracks. Anna makes it clear to her people that Jim Shannon is worth a thousand times more than the U.S. military plane that crashed on landing, because he has a wealth of expertise that could be of great use to Soviet designers.
During their stay in the USSR, Jim discovers that his wife is pregnant by him. Shannon is commissioned by the Soviets to test-fly their new machine to detect any flaws. But what they really want to do is drug him to get all the information about the technological advances in American jets. Through the nature of the questions, Jim learns how much the Soviets already know and what they are technically capable of. However, the Russians are only getting outdated information from him. When Anna discovers her husband's intentions, she fears for him, because she must realize that she truly loves Jim and, moreover, she lacks the capitalist comforts with which Jim had obviously successfully "infected" her. She fears that if she stays in the U.S.S.R., the drugs will one day damage Jim's head so badly that he will no longer be the man she fell in love with. Their personal feelings begin to trump the sense of patriotic duty and love for the fatherland. The Soviet apparatchiks sensed this ambivalence and assigned her an agent loyal to the party to make sure that she did not do "stupid things". Anna then grabs her husband, steals a Soviet fighter jet, and flies back to the United States in a breathtaking chase through the clouds of Soviet pursuers.

query_text:
Fisheries expert Alfred Jones receives an email from financial adviser Harriet Chetwode-Talbot, seeking advice on a project to bring salmon fishing to the Yemen—a project being bankrolled by a wealthy Yemeni sheikh and supported by the Foreign and Commonwealth Office. Alfred dismisses the project as "fundamentally unfeasible" because the Yemen cannot provide the necessary environment for salmon. Meanwhile, the British Prime Minister's press secretary, Patricia Maxwell, suggests the salmon fishing story to the Prime Minister's office as a positive story to help improve relations between Britain and the Islamic world.
Alfred meets Harriet to discuss the project, but despite Harriet correcting his misconceptions of the Yemen environment, Alfred is convinced that the project is foolhardy. Alfred's boss, under pressure from Patricia, forces Alfred to accept a position on the project. Alfred considers resigning rather than ruin his reputation in the scientific community, but is convinced by his wife that they need his income and pension.
Harriet arranges for Alfred to meet the Sheikh at his estate in the Scottish Highlands. The Sheikh is excited to meet Alfred as he is the inventor of the "Woolly Jones" fishing fly. While the Sheikh acknowledges that the project might sound crazy, he still believes that fishing is a noble pursuit that promotes harmony and requires immense faith.
After his wife accepts a position in Geneva, Alfred devotes himself to the salmon project. Although painfully shy, he enjoys working with Harriet and they begin to make progress. Their enthusiasm is interrupted, however, when Harriet learns that her new boyfriend, British special forces Captain Robert Meyers, is missing in action. Devastated, Harriet withdraws to her apartment. When Alfred visits her, she gets upset, thinking he just wants her to return to work, but then she realises he has come to comfort her, and the two embrace.
Meanwhile, the Sheikh continues his work, despite radicals who accuse him of introducing Western ways to their region. Patricia informs the Sheikh that because of opposition to removing salmon from British rivers they will need to use farmed salmon. The Sheikh does not believe that salmon bred in captivity will survive and rejects Patricia's offer, ending the British Government's involvement in the project. Alfred resigns his government job to continue with the project.
After a confrontation with his wife in which he realises that their marriage is over and that he is in love with Harriet, Alfred convinces the Sheikh to give the farmed salmon a try. As the two are fishing, a Yemeni radical attempts to assassinate the Sheikh, who is saved by Alfred casting his fishing line towards the assassin. Soon after, they return to the Yemen, where Harriet and Alfred continue to grow closer. After a moonlight swim, he asks her if there was a "theoretical possibility" of the two of them ending up together. She accepts with a kiss on his cheek, but says she will need some time.
At a press conference in the Yemen, with the Foreign Secretary, Patricia reunites Harriet with her boyfriend Robert who has survived the counter-terrorism operation. The PR stunt leaves Alfred heartbroken. That night, Harriet realises her feelings for Robert have changed, and when Alfred gets a text message from his wife asking him to return, he declines.
The following day the fish are released from their holding tanks. The fish swim upstream, and everyone celebrates the success of the project. While Robert and the Foreign Secretary fly-fish for the photographers, terrorists break into the dam upstream and open the flood gates. Although most people survive the resulting flash flood, the valley is left in ruins. The Sheikh blames himself for the tragedy, and vows to rebuild—this time with the support of the local community.
The next day, as Harriet prepares to leave with Robert, the latter says while she was the one thing on his mind that kept him alive during his mission, she doesn't owe him anything. She approaches Alfred to say goodbye, where he tearfully wishes her luck as he ponders what to do next. Just then, they see a salmon jumping from the water, indicating that some fish survived. Alfred tells Harriet he will indeed stay and help them rebuild. Harriet asks if he will need a partner—and Alfred realises that she is talking about herself. They embrace, and then hold hands whilst looking out over the river.
option_0_text: In 1809, in the Tyrol occupied by Bavarian and French troops, Severin Anderlan, a Tyrolean medical student, returns to his homeland and discovers that the French troops, allies of Bavaria, have destroyed his native country and killed his family members. After killing some French soldiers, he flees to Innsbruck as captain of the Bavarian dragons. Here, at a court dance, he learns that Napoleon's troops are about to invade his land again, where the Tyrolean insurrection broke out. Severin then organizes the armed resistance of his people.
option_1_text: Recruiter Anne and pediatrician Eric Calder live on the shores of Lake Geneva in Switzerland. While Anne is often absent for work, Éric makes his first doctor's appointments in the newly opened office. One evening, he receives another call from one of his patients, the painter and neighbor Linda Benson, who is addicted to hallucinogenic mushrooms. He accepts her offer to take drugs with her. Then Linda Benson is dead.
option_2_text: The film takes place during the Cristero War in Mexico. An American priest (Henry Fonda) confronts the Mexican government over its refusal to close his church. Amidst the outrages against the priests, the priest decides to undertake a dangerous journey to Veracruz to return to the United States. The man has the help of an indigenous woman (Dolores del Río). However, the priest has become an obsession for a police chief (Pedro Armendáriz), who will do his best to prevent him from reaching his destination.
option_3_text: Fred Jones (Ewan McGregor) is an expert member of the National Center for Fish Farming Promotion and has Asperger's syndrome. When consultant Harriet Chetwode-Talbot (Emily Blunt), who represents a wealthy Yemeni sheikh (Amr Waked), asks for help in fulfilling the sheikh's vision of introducing salmon fishing in the desert country of Yemen, Fred rejects the idea as unfeasible. However, the Prime Minister's press secretary, Patricia Maxwell (Kristin Scott Thomas), welcomes it as a story of "goodwill" Anglo-Arab cooperation to distract voters from the developing bad news about Afghanistan and presses Fred to work with Harriet and the sheikh to get the project off the ground. Little by little he's starting to believe in finding the sheik. Away from his wife for whom his career is everything, Fred falls in love with Harriet, whose boyfriend, Robert (Tom Mison), has just disappeared in combat. After Fred declares his love for Harriet, Robert returns alive, so he must choose between the two men. The fish are released and the project seems to yield good results, but is sabotaged by local militants, who destroy the salmon. But when Fred sees that some fish have survived, his faith is restored and Harriet joins him in fulfilling the sheik's vision.
option_4_text:
Virginia is a woman who has always displayed powers of clairvoyance since childhood when she had the vision of her mother's suicide in Dover, while she was in boarding school in Florence. As an adult, the woman married Francesco Ducci, a Tuscan businessman.
One day, after escorting her husband to the airport, Virginia, driving home, has another vision in which she sees an elderly woman murdered and beaten by a lame man. Immediately afterwards, she tells the episode to her friend and psychologist Luca Fattori, an expert in parapsychology, who, however, does not give much weight to the friend's vision.
Virginia begins to devote herself to the renovation of a villa outside Siena owned by Francesco's family. As she enters the building she is escorted by the guard, who finds the room she saw in the vision and where the crime seems to have taken place. Curious, he begins digging with a pickaxe in the supposed niche where the woman was walled up and finds a skeleton. The police are alerted and discover that the body belongs to a certain Agnese Bignardi, a girl missing since 1972. The woman was also Francesco's lover, who thus becomes the first suspect in the murder. Meanwhile, Virginia's starting her own investigation.
Meanwhile, Virginia finds on her answering machine a phone call from a woman who claims to have conclusive proof of Francis' innocence, but she does not leave an address where she can be traced.
In the vision there was also a yellow taxi; Virginia manages to track down a taxi driver who recognizes Agnese and who claims to have accompanied her along with a man with a lame beard near the art gallery. Virginia decides to go to the art gallery, because, always in the vision, there was also a painting on which something was written. In fact, in the museum he finds the photo of a painting by Vermeer, Love Letter, stolen in March 1972. Doing some research in the library, Virginia recovers a newspaper in which there is talk of the theft; in the article there is also a photo of a man with a beard, Emilio Rospini, the director of the art gallery. Suspecting that he may be the man identified by the taxi driver, Virginia enters Rospini's home and meets his wife, who tells her how her husband was left crippled in his left leg for a few months. At that point Rospini himself enters the house having shaved off his beard, resembling in every way the man in Virginia's vision. The woman takes the opportunity to ask him about his relations with Agnese, but Rospini refuses to answer.
Virginia finds in a newsstand the magazine seen in the vision on which Agnese is depicted; Luca believes that the photo has been recycled from the newspaper by an older service, and Paola notices that on the side a horse's snout stands out. Going to a stable, Virginia and Luca talk to a stable boy who remembers finding the photo in the archives and selling it to the newspaper. Although he does not recognize the girl, the man recognizes the horses in the photo, one of which belongs to Rospini.
Francesco is released and the suspicions then fall on Rospini, suspected of the theft of the painting by Vermeer, for which he was blackmailed by Agnese. Meanwhile, Virginia receives another phone call from the mysterious woman, Mrs. Casazza, who this time arrives in time to leave her the address: via del Lombrone 6. As Virginia is about to leave, Gloria, Francesco's sister, gives her a watch with a very special carillon alarm clock that the woman remembers hearing in her vision as well. After that, Virginia goes to Luke, who points out that the magazine with Agnese's photo is in its first year of publication, and therefore it is impossible that he was present in the room during the murder of the girl; this means that Virginia did not have the vision of something that happened in the past, but a premonition of events that have yet to happen.
Virginia goes to Via del Lombrone, a street near the villa where Agnese's body was found, and finds the mysterious woman dead, just like in the vision, and at some point Rospini appears. Before running away from the man, Virginia retrieves a letter, also present in the vision, and once out of the house, she heads to a nearby church, left open following some renovation work. During the escape, Virginia climbs onto a scaffolding and Rospini, trying to reach her, misses and falls to the ground. Frightened, the girl flees from the church and returns to the nearby villa of the Dukes; from here she calls home and finds Francesco, just released, to whom she asks to come and pick her up.
Meanwhile, Luca receives a call from the stallion who has remembered a very important detail: Rospini's mare that appears in the photo was shot in 1972 and therefore the same photo dates back to that year and refers to the IX horse race and not the tenth, with the horse covering part of the Roman number of the banner, thus misleading.
At the hospital Rospini confesses to the police that he planned the theft of Vermeer's painting together with Francesco and Agnese. Rospini and the Casazza believe that Agnese has escaped with the refurtiva, but after the discovery of the skeleton in the villa, they understand Francesco's deception. Arriving at the house of the Casazza, Rospini had found her already dead and next to him Francesco, who, frightened by the man, had thrown himself out of the window, injuring his left ankle. When Virginia arrives, Rospini chases her only to retrieve the letter.
Meanwhile, Francesco arrives at the villa and Virginia sees that he is limping; the man also finds the letter, and believing that he has read it, first stuns it and then the still agonizing wall. Only then does Virginia realize that she had a premonition of her own death. Meanwhile, Luca, after the call of the stallion, realizes the truth of the facts and drives at full speed to the villa of the Dukes. Stopped by the highway, he offends an officer to be chased to the building, where they find Francesco. The man invites them in by showing them the room where Agnese was found, but in which he has changed the arrangement of the furniture, thus hiding the niche in which Virginia is walled. Despite Luca's suspicions, Francesco does not betray himself, and the group is ready to leave the house, but here he plays the carillon of Virginia's clock, thus exposing her husband's crime.

query_text:
Sangraal, son of Ator, is heir to the peaceful people of the marshes. At birth he was saved by his nurse, while his parents and most of his people were slaughtered by a rebellious neighboring people. As an adult, Sangraal leads a band of brave men in search of a "promised land" in which to settle and live in peace.
During the journey, to defend a colony of quiet shepherds, he clashes with the men of Nantuk, a violent and cruel chief protected by the Fire Goddess. In the clash between Sangraal and Nantuk, Lange, the woman with whom Sangraal was in love, is also killed; Sangraal himself - taken prisoner - is saved in extremis by the beautiful Ati, daughter of the chief of the shepherds. Sangraal, to appease his soul and restore peace, sets out to find the wise Rudak, in the hope that he can restore Lange to life.
After various vicissitudes and having "purified" himself through suffering and overcoming various difficulties, he finally meets the "prophet" who orders him to continue fighting against the forces of evil, but only for the sake of justice, not out of a spirit of vengeance. Sangraal, strengthened in his faith for justice, confronts Nantuk and kills him, destroying with him the goddess who protected him.
option_0_text: Alberto Menichetti (Alberto Sordi) lives with his aunt and her old maid in Rome. He works in the company of Vedova De Ritis (Franca Valeri), a seductive widow who is secretly in love with him. But Alberto is attracted to Marcella (Giovanna Ralli), a young hairdresser in his neighborhood. Unable to make up his mind, he enlisted in the Italian army.
option_1_text:
Paul Armstrong, a liberal Harvard professor and former lawyer opposed to capital punishment, is persuaded by an elderly woman to go to Florida to investigate the conviction of her grandson Bobby Earl Ferguson for murder. Ferguson, a former Cornell University student, was convicted of raping and brutally murdering a young white girl named Joanie Shriver eight years prior. Ferguson tells Armstrong that he was physically and psychologically tortured by two police detectives to get a forced confession, but firmly states he is innocent. Armstrong, believing in his innocence, must save him from being executed in the electric chair. As Armstrong digs deeper into the case, he discovers that Tanny Brown, the chief detective on the case, did indeed coerce Ferguson's confession.
Ferguson tells the professor that the murder was actually committed by Blair Sullivan, a serial killer awaiting execution. According to Ferguson, Sullivan constantly taunts him about his conviction for the crime. Sullivan, through the use of Biblical cryptic clues, later reveals the location of the knife used to kill the girl. Armstrong and Brown go to the place, where Armstrong asks Brown to retrieve the knife as Brown's the actual police officer. Brown tries to threaten Armstrong into abandoning the investigation. Armstrong then discovers why Brown is so passionate to get Ferguson convicted: the murdered girl was Brown's daughter's best friend. With a new testimony and with the murder weapon at hand, Ferguson gets a re-trial and is acquitted and thereafter freed from prison. Subsequently, the governor authorizes Sullivan's execution.
Armstrong receives a call from Sullivan, who says he has a final clue to share, but first wants Armstrong to visit Sullivan's parents and tell them he said goodbye. Arriving at the house, Armstrong sees various religious items before finding their butchered, decaying bodies. Back at the prison, Sullivan gloats that he and Ferguson struck a deal: Ferguson would kill Sullivan's parents in exchange for freedom, while Sullivan would claim responsibility for the girl's murder, which Ferguson did in fact commit. Armstrong asks why he was needed for their scheme, and Sullivan replies that was "Bobby Earl's call", meaning that Armstrong would be much more believable in establishing the verdicts than either Ferguson or Sullivan. Armstrong, in his anger at being manipulated, lies to Sullivan and tells him his parents were alive and that they "forgive him." Sullivan becomes enraged. He is forcibly taken by the guards to the electric chair, where he is executed.
Armstrong suspects that Ferguson has kidnapped his wife and daughter, and Armstrong and Brown pursue him. They learn Ferguson's motive is a desire for revenge on Armstrong's wife Laurie; she was the prosecutor against him in a previous kidnapping case which, while ultimately dropped due to lack of evidence, resulted in him being brutalized and castrated in jail when she had him remanded to make a name for herself, as well as the loss of his Cornell scholarship and educational prospects. Out in the swamps, Armstrong finds his wife and daughter in a small shack, where Ferguson appears. Ferguson's plans include raping and murdering Armstrong's wife and daughter and then disappearing. At a critical moment, Brown reappears (after seemingly being attacked and killed by Ferguson) and he and Armstrong join forces. Armstrong stabs Ferguson to death, and his body is subsequently eaten by an alligator. Armstrong's family is thus saved.
option_2_text:
Adam Jones was the chef at a high-class Parisian restaurant owned by his mentor Jean-Luc, until his drug use and temperamental behavior destroyed his career and the restaurant. In the aftermath, Adam went into self-imposed exile in New Orleans by shucking a million oysters to sober up, planning to head to London to restart his career and attempt to earn a third Michelin star.
In London, Adam searches for old colleagues, beginning with his mentor's former maître d'hôtel, Tony Balerdi, now a hotel manager of The Langham Hotel in London, under the ownership of the Balerdi family. Adam checks into one of The Langham's rooms then visits an old friend, Conti, and notes the talent of his sous-chef Helene, but she dislikes his arrogance and dismisses him immediately. A Paris colleague, Michel, whose restaurant Adam had sabotaged out of jealousy, tracks him down. After a brief fistfight, they talk and Michel forgives Adam then asks to work for him. Adam also visits a cutting-edge eatery run by Reece, with whom he has a long-standing rivalry, and the visit ends poorly. Adam's former drug dealer realizes he has returned to Europe and attempts to collect Adam's outstanding debt.
Adam convinces famed restaurant critic Simone to dine at Tony's hotel. Tony realizes that Adam set this up and is reluctant to let him cook, but his kitchen is in such poor condition it would result in Simone shutting his restaurant down. Seeing no other way, he allows Adam to cook. Simone's favorable review convinces Tony to renovate the hotel's kitchen and hire Adam as head chef permanently. He stipulates that Adam must submit to weekly drug tests with Tony's psychiatrist Dr. Rosshilde. Adam agrees to the tests, although he is uninterested in therapy and throws himself into preparations for the grand opening. Another old friend, Max, joins Adam's team after being released from prison. Helene rebuffs further job offers until Conti fires her and sends her to Adam's kitchen. Helene is irate about being fired, but Adam convinces her to work for him by tripling her salary.
Opening night is a disaster, and Adam furiously closes early, blaming Helene. He publicly humiliates her, escalating from verbal to physical aggression, and she quits. Tony convinces Helene to return with a doubled salary and some insight about Adam's behavior. Adam goes on a talk show that he previously turned down to drum up publicity for the restaurant. At his second opening, a restaurant critic gives a positive review, enraging Reece. Adam improves his attitude, but refuses Helene's request for time off for her daughter Lily's birthday. Later, he notices his kitchen acting in a strange manner. Helene reveals that her daughter is at the restaurant under Tony's supervision, since she did not want to spend her birthday at home. Adam is upset, but relents and bakes Lily a birthday cake, which impresses Helene.
With the restaurant's reputation established, Adam sets his sights on three Michelin stars, still avoiding his drug dealer, even after Tony offers to pay off his debt. Adam takes Helene to the reopening of Reece's restaurant. Adam and Reece are civil, but the night derails when Adam spots his ex-girlfriend Anne Marie, the daughter of Jean-Luc. Adam finds Anne Marie surprisingly forgiving after he abandoned her in Paris and missed her father's funeral. The encounter leaves Adam shaken and introspective about his failure in Paris. Early the next morning, Helene finds him at the fish market where they kiss in the alley behind The Langham on the way back to the restaurant. They are interrupted by the drug dealer's thugs, who take Adam away. He returns that night during dinner service beaten and bruised.
Kaitlin, the front of house host, advises Tony that two Michelin reviewers have arrived, and he cooks for them rather than going to the hospital. They send their meals back as it's too spicy, and Michel reveals he sabotaged the sauce with cayenne pepper as revenge for Adam's past cruelty before walking out. On the verge of a breakdown, Adam leaves the restaurant.
He wanders the city, eventually arriving at Reece's restaurant drunk. Once inside, he begins to break down emotionally. Reece soothes him, and they part on better terms the following morning. Adam attends a group therapy session, then returns to the hotel, where he learns that Anne Marie has paid off his debt. She gives him her father's knives and tells him that she approves of Helene. Tony and Helene find Adam in his hotel room, and Tony tells him that the two men they assumed were Michelin inspectors were actually just businessmen on a trip. Adam rejoices at getting a second chance and kisses Tony out of gratitude.
Adam admits his insecurities to Helene, and she comforts him by telling him that he needs to trust his crew. She tends to his wounds and they share a kiss, their relationship rekindled.
Adam returns to the kitchen to prepare for the Michelin inspectors' meals; when Tony asks him what they will do, Adam says that the whole kitchen will do it together as a team. As a result of increased teamwork in the kitchen and Adam's new attitude, the restaurant receives its third star.
The final scene is of Adam enjoying a family meal with the rest of the crew, which he had refused to do earlier, showing that they are his new family.
option_3_text:
In Stuttgart, a disoriented woman is picked up by the police and handed over to medical care. Since she is not proficient in the German language, has Asian features and speaks in a presumably Tibetan dialect, it is assumed that she is from Tibet. In order to appeal to her, you give her the name Luscha. The doctor from Aldenhoff takes her in and tries to raise her according to European standards. In the further course of the film plot, Luscha accidentally meets and falls in love with the lawyer Robert Lorm.
The two decide to look forward to a future together and build their own home. To have a memory of this time, a plaster cast of Lusha's face is created. As she takes off her hardened form, she seems to have transformed into a completely different woman. It is believed that Luscha was temporarily under a form of hypnosis, which not only banished her language from her memory, but also temporarily altered her facial features.
As Johanna Stegen, she can no longer remember the time of her transformation and becomes engaged to the doctor Dr. Thomas Martin. Attorney Lorm tries to win her back by all means and using his hypnotic powers, but to no avail.
option_4_text:
The movie introduces Sangraal, son of king Ator, whose realm and people are destroyed by evil warlord Nantuk.  Sangraal and the remainder of his people flee his wrath and begin searching for a new home. After defending some villagers from an attack by Nantuk's troops, the villagers gladly accept the newcomers as part of their community. Their leader, Belem, even offers Sangraal co-rulership.  Meanwhile, the warlord - who has assumed kinghood after Ator's fall - has angered the Goddess of Fire and Death, to whom he owes his power and whose cult he leads.  She demands that Sangraal be sacrificed or Nantuk will lose his power, his kingdom, and his life.
Nantuk sends out more men to destroy the village sheltering Sangraal, and has his troops murder everyone while the captured and crucified protagonist must watch.  He witnesses his wife's death at the hands of the Goddess of Fire and Death and falls unconscious before being freed by Belem's daughter, Ati, and Li Wo Twan, a travelling archer.
After Ati and Li Wo Twan patch the barbarian up, Sangraal decides to visit the powerful wizard Rudak, who might have the power to bring his wife back to life.  Meanwhile, Nantuk promises his Goddess to torture Sangraal and cast him into her fiery altar with his own hands.
The trio narrowly manages to escape several ambushes and finally makes it to the mountain where Rudak dwells. Rudak, however, convinces Sangraal to finally let go of his dead wife, as no one has the power to bring back the dead. Instead, Sangraal must face his destiny and fight evil: he must seek out a shrine which contains everything he needs to win this battle.
The journey ahead is dangerous, even without Nantuk's servants and their ambushes, but the trio is able to overcome all the obstacles and escape the traps set up for them. Despite getting captured several times, Sangraal finally manages to find the shrine Rudak had mentioned, which contains a powerful, magical crossbow.  However, Ati and Li Wo Twan are ambushed once more, leaving the archer dead and Ati captured.
Sangraal then pursues Ati and her capturers all the way to Nantuk's headquarters, which contains the Goddesses' altar.  He challenges the evil king to a duel, and prevails over him, impaling him on his own dagger.
Afterwards, the protagonist returns to the late king's cave, to find Ati abandoned by Nantuk's servants.  Before they can leave, the Goddess reappears and threatens to take both Sangraal and Ati's life, laughing at the blade Sangraal considers swinging at her and burning it, but her laughter ends when the barbarian loads his magical crossbow and kills her with a shot in the gut.
The movie ends with a shot of Sangraal and Ati riding into freedom.

query_text:
Hando and Davey are part of a gang of neo-Nazi skinheads who are ramping up acts of gratuitous violence or in reaction to the growing Vietnamese community in their Melbourne suburb of Footscray. The situation remains unchanged until the day when their enemies organize themselves and decide to fight them directly. Gabe, a young woman with epilepsy, joins the group and helps them escape justice.
One day, when they see the Vietnamese breaking into the pub they frequent, Hando and his gang lash out at them relentlessly, only to see the situation turn against them. Their nest is ransacked and burned, and they have to retreat to a new area.
But dissension arises in the group: Davey, who has fallen under the spell of Gabe, excluded from the group by Hando, decides to leave the group and live with the young woman.
option_0_text:
The tyrannical village priest Bhuvan Panda considers himself a god and bends religion to his will. As the "tool" of the goddess Kali, he imposes his archaic rules on the town of Rangpur in northern India. For him, women can only exist in three forms: goddesses, mothers and prostitutes. The latter he always visits at night in the Lalbatti quarter, where the maids of love are at home. He prefers to take the beautiful Basanti, whom he humiliates and mistreats. One day, the young Chandan Mishra arrives in Rangpur to take over the post of the old local postman. His tour soon takes him to Lalbatti, where the innocent man becomes the plaything of the whores. Especially Basanti likes him and when Chandan realizes that she has a good heart and only works here to provide her daughter Titali with a better future, he falls in love with her. This arouses the wrath of Bhuvan Panda and he does not approve of the impending marriage of the two. Bhuvan Panda even plans to kill Basanti and when Chandan challenges him to stop him, he is killed. Meanwhile, Basanti waits for her lover at the altar. When he doesn't come, Basanti's heart breaks and in her desperation she returns to her life as a prostitute.
When Basanti receives the news of Chandan's daily death, she and all the villagers attack the temple and rise up against the years of tyranny. In an escalating confrontation between the prostitute and the priest, Bhuvan Panda is beaten down by Basanti and driven from the village. She then embraces her daughter, and a new, liberated life returns to the village.
option_1_text:
In Melbourne's working-class neighbourhood of Footscray, there's a skinhead gang led by the swaggering, charismatic Hando and his best friend Davey. The life of the entire entourage, however, undergoes an abrupt change from the meeting in a pub between Hando and Gabrielle, a girl who has just escaped from her unstable ex.
A few days later, some Skin88s from Canberra join the gang. After organizing a party, the young people discover that the bar in their neighborhood, for years run by an Australian family and their usual meeting place, has been sold to Vietnamese: armed with springs, chains and various white weapons, the gang carries out a raid, seriously injuring two children of the immigrant entrepreneur. Towards the end of the punitive mission, however, the third brother calls some of his friends and, shortly after, it is the Asians who, armed with clubs and sticks, force Hando's men to flee. Escaping the worst, the skinheads take refuge in their hideout, but are soon overtaken by the Vietnamese youths, who set the place on fire and some of the boys in the group. The next day, the neo-Nazis begin planning a decisive counterattack.
Hando, meanwhile, has started a relationship with Gabrielle, but when she is struck by an epileptic seizure, the young man interrupts their relationship, while Davey begins to show an ever-growing interest in the girl. The group, embittered by the events and eager for revenge, are incited by Gabrielle to rob the villa of Martin, a wealthy man of her acquaintance, so as to get the money to buy firearms. The following night the villa is then vandalized and the girl reveals that the man is her father, justifying the vandalism as revenge for the years of violence suffered by him.
The plan however fails, as the man manages to free himself from the captivity in which the group had forced him and to arm himself with a gun, forcing them to a rocambolesque escape and moreover without any refutation. Back at the warehouse Hando and Gabrielle argue furiously and Davey gives her his home address and leaves the group as well. Gabrielle, one time, gives a tip to the police, reveals the gang's hideout, then goes to Davey, makes love to him and reveals her love to him in return.
At the warehouse, the police arrest all the neo-Nazis, killing even the very young Bubs; Hando, who cannot help but cry for his friend and run away in panic. The next morning he shows up at Davey's house, who finds him in bed with Gabrielle, but the two provide an alibi that Hando can't counter. The three, therefore, decide to leave for Adelaide.
The three rob the prearranged place and Hando kills the cashier for no apparent reason, taking all the money in the register.
Driving through the night, the three finally decide to stop at a beach, where Hando discusses with his friend the possibility of abandoning Gabrielle and fleeing Australia. The girl overhears the conversation and, in a fit of rage, sets Hando's car on fire, screaming in anger that she called the police.
Skin88, also furious, begins to strangle the girl, but at this point Davey intervenes, who to defend her stabs his friend with a Nazi dagger that he had bought with Hando's own contribution. He dies shortly afterwards, bleeding to death, while Davey leans over Gabrielle to comfort her and a group of Japanese tourists witness the scene.
option_2_text:
Germany at the end of the First World War: "The fuel that war and need created in people" is portrayed as a "nervous epidemic", "which has affected people and drives them to all kinds of deeds and guilt".
The fates of various people from different social strata are described: the manufacturer Roloff, who has lost his belief in technological progress, the teacher Johannes, who calls for social reform in popular assemblies, and Marja, who turns into a revolutionary to fight against the armed forces.
“Young Marja is about to get married to Richard, but has actually loved Johannes since childhood, who has become a kind of mouthpiece for the branded people and demands social reform; when he rejects her love, which he replies but cannot reconcile with his biblical code, she takes revenge by accusing him of rape. Her brother, the factory owner Roloff, who has long since given up his belief in technological progress, swears in court that he has observed the attack: his psyche has long been marked by war and destruction, and soon he will be completely mad. Marja later withdraws the accusation and becomes the leader of a revolutionary group: she wants to build on Johannes' ideology, replaces his pacifist approaches with gun violence. In the end, even Roloff's wife, until then the only person who was perceived to be untouched, goes mad: she sets fire to Johannes' house and kills his blind sister, and then goes to the monastery to do penance. ”
option_3_text: Two years after the murder of Count Dracula, history tells of his resurrection. To bring him back to life, three thrill-seeking nobles want to use the blood collected at the scene of death, but the three men during the ritual back off and kill their ceremonial master, Lord Courtley, Dracula's servant. Dracula's revenge (already awakened) involves the three men and their children. One of them will oppose it.
option_4_text:
In Paris in 1890, Dr. Georges Bonnet, a physician and amateur sculptor, abruptly ended a fashion show he had organized in his home. He's hiding a secret because although he appears to be in his 30s, he's actually 104 years old and has retained his youth and vitality thanks to the transplantation of parathyroid glands every 10 years. Professor Ludwig Weiss of Vienna, co-discoverer of this anti-aging process, arrives three weeks late at George's house to perform the final transplant. As a result, George must drink a smoking green elixir every six hours to stay young, although the elixir only gives him four weeks without a transplant. When Georges' last model, Margo Philippe, meets Georges while he is drinking the liquid, he hits her. When 89-year-old Ludwig finally arrives, he reveals that he cannot operate on George because a stroke has left his right hand disabled. Ludwig instructed Georges to find another surgeon.
Sureté Inspector LeGris begins investigating Margo's disappearance and arrives at a dinner arranged by Georges for Janine Du Bois, a former lover, and Dr Pierre Gerrard. Georges denies knowing where Margo is and, when LeGris asks to see Margo's bust, tells him that he accidentally destroyed it that morning. LeGris leaves and Georges confesses to his surprised guests that he lied, as the police would probably damage the bust if he handed it to them. Ludwig secretly convinces Pierre to perform the transplant surgery, claiming that Georges is terminally ill and needs urgent treatment.
After Janine and Pierre leave, Ludwig tells Georges that Pierre is going to operate. However, Ludwig was suspicious of George and said it was strange that this was the third of George's models to have disappeared at the time of his transplants. Ludwig discovers that the most recent parathyroid gland comes from a living person, instead of being "revitalized" from a corpse. When Ludwig confronts George that his actions are unjustified, George retorts that he revived four cadaver glands but they all died because Ludwig was late, adding to George's hatred of being alone in the world. Ludwig destroys the elixir to prevent George from continuing; George strangles Ludwig to death.
Pierre arrived the next morning to perform the operation, but George informed him that Ludwig had been unexpectedly recalled to Vienna. Pierre refuses to continue and suggests that Georges find another surgeon. Georges visits other surgeons in Paris to no avail. Meanwhile, LeGris tells Pierre about the disappearances of three young women 10 years apart - in London, San Francisco and Bern, Switzerland - and that each modeled for a sculptor who was also a doctor but disappeared at the same time as the models. With Margo also missing, LeGris thinks Georges is responsible for all the disappearances, but Pierre doubts him, as that would place the suspect in his 60s.
Georges takes Janine to a cellar containing his sculptures and proudly shows her the first figurine he made when he was a boy at the age of 12. The figurine is dated 1798. Janine says with a laugh that the date must be wrong because if it wasn't, George would be 104 years old. George leaves abruptly, locking Janine in the cellar. He then goes to Peter and tells him that he and Ludwig had discovered the secret of "everlasting life" decades earlier, but he cannot reveal the secret to the world because if everyone could live forever, paradoxically, everyone would eventually die without a new supply of new parathyroid glands. Pierre again refuses to perform the transplant but gives in when Georges threatens Janine's life. Janine finds a mentally deranged Margo imprisoned on the reservation.
That night, Pierre simulated the operation by making the incision at George's waist but without transplanting the gland. Georges rushes to the cellar while Pierre and LeGris follow him. Georges tells Janine that the same operation will allow her to live forever, always young and beautiful and in love by his side. She refuses. Suddenly, George is aging rapidly and realizes that Peter has not operated. As he cries out that he is dying, Margo throws an oil lamp at him, setting the cellar on fire. Pierre and LeGris save Janine while Georges and Margo die in the consuming flames.

query_text:
The film is an ensemble piece in which the five protagonists plan, enjoy and come down from a weekend out in Cardiff; all motivated at least in part by the need for a weekend escape from the banality and misery of their daily lives. Jip is suffering from sexual anxiety brought on by a series of unsuccessful liaisons. Koop, Jip's best friend, is jealous of his girlfriend Nina's happy and care-free nature. Nina is being sexually harassed in a job she had no choice but to take after having failed a college interview. Lulu, Jip's best female friend and "dropping partner", has suffered infidelity in her last 3 relationships. Moff, the newest member of the group having met Jip at a warehouse party after moving from London to Cardiff, is an unemployed slacker who works as a small-time dealer, despite his father being a senior policeman. The five friends become very close, take drugs such as cannabis, ecstasy and cocaine, and "live for the weekend".
The film follows the antics of the five friends as well as various characters they meet along the way. They go to pubs and clubs on Friday, taking along Nina's 17-year-old brother Lee whose waning enthusiasm for his first drugs experience is played out in a debate between Jip and a doctor. Jip gives up his ticket to Lulu, whom he has talked into coming out and is forced to talk his way into the club as the group are a ticket short. The club scene is then examined through a series of cameos including two attempts by older journalists to understand the club scene. The ensemble then joins a house party, where Lulu and Jip finally kiss and attempt unsuccessfully to make love; whereas the established couple, Koop and Nina, fight over Koop's perceptions about her behaviour. Later, as expected by the group, "what goes up must come down" sets in as the effects of their drug use begin to hit home leaving them coping with feelings of anxiety and paranoia. They recover Lee from a group of younger partygoers he has spent the night with and make their way home.
On returning home, some of the group's issues are mended whilst some are thrown into sharper relief. Jip makes love with Lulu, overcoming his sexual problems. Koop and Nina's argument is resolved. Lee has made it through the weekend without any of his concerns being realised.  Moff, however, is still caught up in the paranoia caused by his extensive drug use. He argues with his parents again and is seen walking alone around Cardiff feeling depressed. However, Moff joins his friends for an end of the weekend drink and having raged about his obsession with drugs is soon joking about his addiction with his friends. The film finishes with Jip and Lulu kissing in the street.

Self-narrator Rabo Karabekian tells that before the Armenian Genocide, his parents fled from their Armenian homeland to the United States, where he was born in 1916 in San Ignacio, California. Now he lives in a 19-room beachfront home in East Hampton, Long Island, left to him by his second wife when she died two years ago. He was inspired to write his autobiography by a woman named Circe Berman, 43 years old, who showed up one day in his self-chosen solitude.
Karabekian met many abstract expressionist artists during his lifetime. Since he himself had too little talent to become a painter, he decided to become an art collector. In the meantime, he has lost all his former friends, but he has one last secret, which he carefully keeps hidden from the public, like once Knight Bluebeard the riddle of the secret chamber.
option_1_text: Journalist Blair Maynard investigates the mysterious disappearances of boats in the famous Bermuda Triangle. Taking care of his son on a weekend, with whom he has a complicated relationship, he travels aboard an old cuckoo to the island of Navidad, a place close to the last signs of life of the disappeared ships. They meet Dr. Windsor, who offers them hospitality. They are soon attacked by pirates and taken to their island, where the population, cut off from the rest of the world, still lives as in the 17th century.
option_2_text: Jip lives in Cardiff, works in a clothing store, and suffers from sexual failure anxiety. He is dissatisfied with the gray everyday life, his family background also gives little hope: his father is in prison and his mother earns her money with prostitution. The same is true of his friends. Jip's only glimpses are the weekends he spends with them under the influence of drugs. The film focuses on one such weekend. Jip, Koop, Nina (Koop's girlfriend), Lulu and policeman's son Moff want to go to the asylum, a hip Cardiff club. However, they only got four tickets to the club. Lulu wants to stay home voluntarily, which is not right at all for Jip, who's got his eye on her. In a rather daring way, he procures the missing card so that they can all still come in and celebrate.
option_3_text:
A former novelist named  Eliza Welsh  has turned into a mommy blogger. Her daughter is about to turn six and Eliza wants to throw a birthday party for her child. The task would have been easier if Eliza Welsh's list of things to do was shorter!
Between her very young son, the tyrannical mothers of the playground, the lack of parking space and the apology to her best friend for posting her secrets on her blog... Eliza doesn't know where to turn anymore. In addition, she is eager to enter a contest organized by a well-known magazine. But here's the problem. How do you answer, in exactly 500 words, the question What does "being a mother" mean to you?
option_4_text:
After the territory of Laramie, Wyoming has had law and order restored by men known as the Frontiersman, sheriff Sam Barrett has a peaceful town. At least until a fight breaks out between his grown son, Logan, and a man named Kearney who has been wounded by one of Logan's bullets.
Newspaper editor Larrabee explains to the sheriff what happened. Larrabee was accused of cheating at cards by Kearney, who drew a gun on him. But because the editor was unarmed, Logan stepped in and shot the gun from Kearney's hand.
Sam believes the fair thing is to give Logan and Kearney each 10 days in jail. Kearney is livid, though, accusing the sheriff of favorable bias toward his son. Later that day at Kearney's ranch, Ryan, a ranch hand, sees Logan standing over Kearney's dead body.
A posse is formed. Logan runs into a doctor's daughter, Janie Martin, and explains his situation. A bank is robbed and the banker shot by a man fitting Logan's description, riding off on a pinto, which is what Logan rides. Larrabee helps him get away.
Janie spots a man in similar garb on a pinto and realizes Logan's been telling the truth about being innocent. Sam goes to help his son and discovers Larrabee is behind the killing and robbery. Janie is held hostage, but Logan and his father, fighting side by side, save the day.

query_text: The Sorceress Queen, after a dream, remembers Adora, the eldest daughter of the rulers of Eternia, who was kidnapped by Hordak, once master and now enemy of Skeletor. He will reveal the truth to Prince Adam, who will have to discover on his own with a magic sword who is the person who will also possess the same powers as He-Man. On his journey to Etheria, Adam meets the brave rebels and Hordak's new army, among them Adora who belongs to that army. After his transformation into He-Man, the sword will tell him that Adora is the one who will possess his same powers. The Queen Sorceress, through telepathic communication will reveal to Adora the truth: that Prince Adam (He-Man) is her true blood brother and that she herself will discover his transformation with the sword to become She-Ra, the Princess of Power. Both brothers, He-Man and She-Ra, will unite as the new Masters of the Universe to fight for freedom, equality, rights and justice, against the evil forces of Skeletor and Hordak on their respective planets.
