The story is set in 1790 in the countryside around the Dutch settlement of Tarry Town (historical Tarrytown, New York), in a secluded glen known as Sleepy Hollow. Sleepy Hollow is renowned for its ghosts and the haunting atmosphere that pervades the imaginations of its inhabitants and visitors. Some residents say this town was bewitched during the early days of the Dutch settlement, while others claim that the mysterious atmosphere was caused by an old Native American chief, the "wizard of his tribe ... before the country was discovered by Master Hendrik Hudson." Residents of the town are seemingly subjected to various supernatural and mysterious occurrences. They are subjected to trance-like visions and frequented by strange sights, music, and voices "in the air." The inhabitants of Sleepy Hollow are fascinated by the "local tales, haunted spots, and twilight superstitions" on account of the mysterious occurrences and haunting atmosphere. The most infamous specter in the Hollow is the Headless Horseman, the "commander-in-chief of all the powers of the air," (an attribute also of the Devil, according to Ephesians 2:2). He is supposedly the restless ghost of a Hessian trooper whose head had been shot off by a stray cannonball during "some nameless battle" of the Revolution, and who "rides forth to the scene of battle in nightly quest of his head".
The "Legend" relates the tale of Ichabod Crane, a lean, lanky and extremely superstitious schoolmaster from Connecticut. Throughout his stay at Sleepy Hollow, Crane is able to make himself both "useful and agreeable" to the families that he lodges with. He occasionally assists with light farm work, helping to make hay, mending fences, caring for numerous farm animals, and cutting firewood. Besides his more dominant role as the schoolmaster, Ichabod Crane also assists the various mothers of the town by helping to take care of their young children, taking on a more "gentle and ingratiating" role. Crane is also quite popular among the women of the town for his education and his talent for "carrying the whole budget of local gossip," which makes him a welcomed sight within female circles. As a firm believer in witchcraft and the like, Crane has an unequaled "appetite for the marvelous," which is only increased by his stay in "the spell-bound region" of Sleepy Hollow. A source of "fearful pleasure" for Crane is to visit the Old Dutch wives and listen to their "marvelous tales of ghosts and goblins," haunted locations, and the tales of the Headless Horseman, or the "Galloping Hessian of the Hollow, as they sometimes called him."
Throughout the story, Ichabod Crane competes with Abraham "Brom Bones" Van Brunt, the town rowdy and local hero, for the hand of 18-year-old Katrina Van Tassel, the daughter and sole child of wealthy farmer Baltus Van Tassel. Ichabod Crane, an outsider, sees marriage to Katrina as a means of procuring Van Tassel's extravagant wealth. Brom, unable to force Ichabod into a physical showdown to settle things, plays a series of pranks on the superstitious schoolmaster. The tension among the three continues for some time, and is soon brought to a head. On a placid autumn night, the ambitious Crane attends a harvest party at the Van Tassels' homestead. He dances, partakes in the feast, and listens to ghostly legends told by Brom and the locals, but his true aim is to propose to Katrina after the guests leave. His intentions, however, are ill-fated, as he fails to secure Katrina's hand.
Following his rejected suit, Ichabod rides home on his temperamental plough horse named Gunpowder, "heavy-hearted and crestfallen" through the woods between Van Tassel's farmstead and the farmhouse in Sleepy Hollow where he is quartered at the time. As he passes several purportedly haunted spots, his active imagination is engorged by the ghost stories told at Baltus' harvest party. After nervously passing a lightning-stricken tulip tree purportedly haunted by the ghost of British spy Major André, Ichabod encounters a cloaked rider at an intersection in a menacing swamp. Unsettled by his fellow traveler's eerie size and silence, the teacher is horrified to discover that his companion's head is not on his shoulders, but on his saddle. In a frenzied race to the bridge adjacent to the Old Dutch Burying Ground, where the Hessian is said to "vanish, according to rule, in a flash of fire and brimstone" before crossing it, Ichabod rides for his life, desperately goading Gunpowder down the Hollow. However, while Crane and Gunpowder are able to cross the bridge ahead of the ghoul, Ichabod turns back in horror to see the monster rear his horse and hurl his severed head directly at him with a fierce motion. The schoolmaster attempts to dodge, but is too late; the missile strikes his head and sends him tumbling headlong into the dust from his horse.
The next morning, Gunpowder is found eating the grass at his master's gate, but Ichabod has mysteriously disappeared from the area, leaving Katrina to later marry Brom Bones, who was said "to look exceedingly knowing whenever the story of Ichabod was related". Indeed, the only relics of the schoolmaster's flight are his discarded hat, Gunpowder's trampled saddle, and a mysterious shattered pumpkin. Although the true nature of both the Headless Horseman and Ichabod's disappearance that night are left open to interpretation, the story implies that the Horseman was really Brom (an extremely agile rider) in disguise, using a Jack-o'-lantern as a false head, and suggests that Crane survived the fall from Gunpowder and immediately fled Sleepy Hollow in horror of both the legends and having to deal with his landlord, never to return but to prosper elsewhere, or was killed by Brom (which may be unlikely, since Brom was said to have "more mischief than ill-will in his composition"). Irving's narrator concludes the story, however, by stating that the old Dutch wives continue to promote the belief that Ichabod was "spirited away by supernatural means", and a legend develops around his disappearance and sightings of his melancholy spirit.
In a Postscript (sometimes unused in certain editions), the narrator states the circumstances in which he heard the story from an old gentleman "at a Corporation meeting at the ancient city of Manhattoes", who didn't "believe one-half of it [himself]."
option_1_text:
Bank robber Zeki Müller has just been released from prison. Upon his release, he's going to get back the money he stole to pay off a debt, but his friend buried it on a construction site. During Zeki's time in prison, the construction project was completed and his money is now buried under the new gymnasium at the Goethe Gesamtschule. To get the money, Zeki infiltrates the school and applies for the vacant position of a deceased janitor. However, due to a misunderstanding, he is given a job as a substitute teacher.
Elisabeth "Lisi" Schnabelstedt is a teacher at the Goethe Gesamtschule, her former high school, which is under the tutelage of her younger sister, Laura. Lisi does not impose the authority necessary to handle students successfully.
When Ingrid Leimbach-Knorr, head teacher of class 10 B, attempts suicide, the handling of the difficult class goes to Lisi Schnabelstedt, though the class's brutal jokes about the new teacher quickly reduce her to tears. Zeki assumes the position of substitute teacher for Lisi's old seventh grade class. To get his money back, Zeki works through the night in the school basement in a tunnel that leads to the buried money. She also copies Lisi's diploma as she does not have a high school or college education, which is eventually discovered by Lisi. After blackmailing Zeki, Lisi regains her old seventh grade class, while Zeki assumes responsibility over class 10B.
Zeki is kicked out of the strip club where he lived, and tries to sleep in Lisi's garage. When she finds out, Lisi allows him to live in her basement as long as he teaches class 10B correctly instead of watching movies at every class period.
Through unconventional methods and Lisi's gentle leadership, Zeki gains the respect of the class. Although Zeki begins his time as a teacher with draconian methods, which include shooting students with a paintball gun and holding a student underwater, he eventually takes a softer approach and convinces the students that they don't want to become drug dealers and depend on welfare. To do this, he organizes a field trip to visit Zeki's acquaintances who live this lifestyle. He also becomes more involved in the school by assuming leadership of the Drama Club, which performs a modern version of Romeo and Juliet, and helps with the Jugend forscht competition. Zeki, concerned about Lisi's image among the class, leads his students on a graffiti-painting excursion on a train, during which one student paints the title 'Fack ju Göhte'. As a result of this increased respect, Lisi passes her practical teaching exam with class 10B. In addition, Zeki arranges a love affair for Lisi's younger sister, Laura, with her crush Danger, and ensures the continuity of Lisi's legal guardianship of Laura by pretending to be Lisi's serious boyfriend when Laura's social worker comes to visit.
Eventually, Zeki finds the money in the tunnel, but the tunnel under the gym causes the floor to break and allows Lisi to discover Zeki. When Lisi learns of Zeki's criminal past, she threatens to call the police if he does not leave his job and home immediately. Zeki, with no options, agrees to drive his car for a bank robbery. When Zeki's class is about to take their final exam in German, everyone takes out their motivational photos. A student informs Lisi that the photo of Zeki's motivation is on her desk. When Lisi opens the desk, she discovers that her motivation to become a better person is her. A friend of Zeki is able to convince Lisi that the ex-criminal wants to change his way of being for her.
Zeki does not continue with the robbery because three students stop him to ask him if he will be their class teacher next year and he sees the train with the graffiti 'Fack ju Göthe'. Send Lisi a dress and an invitation to the graduation party and report to the school principal. She wants to keep him and even gives him a forged high school diploma. He informs Zeki that class 10B has improved dramatically and that if they continue to work toward their high school diplomas, the school will become the best in the city. His grades in German, previously 5 and 6, are now better than 3.
option_2_text:
When her friend Gary is hit by a taxi outside a Tiffany's store, Rachel mistakenly assumes he was proposing to her because she finds a jewelry box among his belongings. What she doesn't know is that the box was switched with another man named Ethan, who provided first aid to her friend Gary.
In gratitude for saving her friend, Rachel invites sympathetic Ethan, who with his daughter Daisy even visits the accident victim Gary in the hospital, to her small cafe where she makes her own Italian pastries, with the two getting close to each other. While Gary is recovering from his mild concussion, Rachel opens her bakery at the Christmas market and picks up Ethan and his girlfriend Vanessa at the airport. It is not until Christmas Eve, when both couples open their respective jewelry boxes, that the two men realize that the jewelry gifts have been exchanged. But while Gary gives the surprised Rachel the wonderful emerald ring with a big gesture, as if he had bought it for her, Ethan is completely speechless, instead of the precious ring, only finding relatively simple earrings in it, which his girlfriend Vanessa is still happy about, and does not say a word about it.
The next day, Ethan visits Rachel and asks her if Gary can be trusted, if he's honest, if he accidentally took something somewhere. Because Gary's not coming because he got held up at work, Rachel and Ethan are spending another night together.
The next morning, Ethan visits Gary at his tattoo parlor and asks him to return the ring immediately so Vanessa can finally propose to him. But Gary refuses to give up the ring. Meanwhile, Rachel was at Tiffany's and learned from the salesgirl that it was actually Ethan who bought the ring. She then confronts Gary, who does not deny his retention of the ring, but also tells her that he loves her and wants to marry her, which Rachel hardly accepts, as she is very surprised by his brazen stealing of the ring. Later, when Ethan arrives at the cafe, Rachel tells him that she knows everything and that he will soon get the ring back.
At a New Year's Eve party at Rachel's Cafe Restaurant, it becomes increasingly clear that she and Gary aren't a match at all. She learns that he was already on his way to another date when they first met, which eventually leads to a rift between the two. That's when Ethan and Vanessa arrive to celebrate their engagement at the cafe. But now all the lies of the last few days are flying, until finally Vanessa storms out. Already in the last few days, it was clear that their life plans were about to fall apart, as Ethan wants to move to New York and Vanessa wants to return to Los Angeles as soon as possible. It's the breakup of the longest-running relationship in the round.
Ethan and Rachel have thus become a couple who can envision a future together, in which Ethan's daughter Daisy has a place as well, having lost her mother as an infant, and can now share this fate with her "new mother" Rachel, who also lost her mother as a child.
A year later, we meet the three again, happy and busy working in the café-restaurant, all three dressed in funny sweaters. At the height of the evening, Ethan begins to give a speech about Rachel, culminating in a marriage proposal, which she gladly accepts, so there's a happy ending.
option_3_text: A barber shop owner travels to Vienna to receive his inheritance from his late aunt. However, it appears all she has left him are thirteen old chairs. Needing to raise enough money to pay for his ticket back home, he sells them to a second-hand dealer. Only then does he discover a letter from his aunt telling him she has left 100,000 ℛ︁ℳ︁ sewn into one of the chairs. He now sets out to track down the various new owners of the chairs to find the hidden money.
option_4_text:
On Eternia, the Sorceress of Castle Grayskull is awakened by a mysterious magic sword that leads her to a glowing portal known as a 'Time Gate'. Recognizing the sword as the 'Sword of Protection', the Sorceress summons Prince Adam and Cringer to Castle Grayskull and sends them through the portal to find the person destined to possess the sword.
Arriving in the other dimensional world of Etheria, Adam and Cringer stop at an inn for lunch and discover that Etheria is ruled by an evil intergalactic army known as the Horde. When some Hordesmen soldiers cause trouble in the inn, Adam stands up to them and defeats them with the help of an archer named Bow, who tells Adam that he and his friend Kowl are members of the 'Great Rebellion'.
As word of the fight reaches the Horde's leader Hordak, Bow and Kowl take Adam and Cringer to the Rebellion's base in the Whispering Woods. They meet the other Rebels, including their leader Princess Glimmer, tree people called the Twiggetts, and Madame Razz, the comically inept witch, who arrives on her talking Broom to reveal that the Horde are threatening to enslave the villagers unless the Rebels responsible for the fight in the inn give themselves up, and that some of the Horde's worst villains, including Catra, Mantenna, Leech and Scorpia are there, stacking the odds almost insurmountably against the rebels. Bow is willing to surrender to save the village, but Adam and Glimmer convince the group that they should fight back to save the villagers instead.
As the Horde, led by Force Captain Adora, start taking away the villagers, they are attacked by the Rebels, aided by Adam and Cringer in their secret identities as He-Man and Battle Cat. He-Man confronts Adora and the Sword of Protection glows in her presence, revealing that she is the one he's looking for. This distraction allows the Horde to knock He-Man out and capture him.
Madame Razz divines that the Horde have taken He-Man to their prison complex on Beast Island, and the Rebels head there to attempt a rescue. In the prison, Adora interrogates He-Man and agrees that the sword seems to be meant for her, to which He-Man retorts that he is to give it to someone who serves good rather than evil. Adora believes the Rebels are evil and the Horde the rightful, benevolent rulers of Etheria, although she admits to not knowing much about life outside the Horde's base. When He-Man dares her to see for herself what life on Etheria is really like, Adora says she'll think about it. The Rebels arrive on Beast Island and manage to get into the prison to find He-Man, only to get captured and imprisoned themselves. Kowl manages to elude capture and frees He-Man, who then frees the others and destroys the prison. Meanwhile, Adora has ventured into the towns outside the Fright Zone and sees first-hand the cruelties Etheria's citizens are forced to endure at the hands of the Horde.
As Hordak and Shadow Weaver discuss how He-Man is a threat too powerful to ignore, they are confronted by Adora wielding the Sword of Protection. However, Shadow Weaver casts Adora into a mystic sleep that will make her forget what she learned about the Horde and takes the sword, planning to learn its secrets.
Later, Hordak shows the Horde his latest weapon: the Magna-Beam, a willpower-fueled transporter that will allow him to send the entire Rebel base into exile forever. However, none of the Horde's captives have sufficient willpower to fully charge the machine. He-Man sneaks into the Horde base looking for Adora, but Adora once again thinks he's the villain and arrests him. Hordak then confines He-Man in the Magna-Beam's energy chamber to charge it overnight.
Later that night, Adora has nightmares about He-Man's fate and hears a voice calling her name. She discovers the Sorceress talking to her through the Sword of Protection and asking her to help He-Man, whom the Sorceress reveals is Adora's twin brother. After reflecting upon the Sorceress's words, Adora breaks Shadow Weaver's spell then follows the Sorceress's instructions to hold the sword aloft and say "For the Honour of Grayskull!" She then transforms into the superpowered She-Ra, Princess of Power. After she rescues and revives He-Man, the pair destroy the Magna-Beam and make their getaway on Adora's horse Spirit, who in She-Ra's presence is transformed into a talking winged unicorn named Swift Wind.
She-Ra reveals that she is He-Man's sister, but He-Man is skeptical. When She-Ra explains that she was told by the 'woman in the sword', He-Man uses the Sword of Protection to contact the Sorceress, who confirms and explains their relationship. When Adam and Adora were born to King Randor and Queen Marlena, Eternia was invaded by the Horde. Unable to defeat the combined might of the Eternian army and the magic of Castle Grayskull, Hordak plotted to demoralize them by kidnapping the newborn royals, aided by his favorite pupil (and He-Man's future archenemy) Skeletor. Although the kidnapping was interrupted by Man-At-Arms, Hordak escaped with Adora and ultimately fled through a Time Gate. The Sorceress was unable to discover which dimension Hordak fled to, so she cast a spell that wiped all memory of Adora from the people of Eternia except for herself, Man-At-Arms, King Randor and Queen Marlena. Thus Adam was raised unaware of his sister's existence. Convinced by the Sorceress's story, He-Man happily accepts She-Ra as his sister.
Returning to the Rebel camp as Adam and Adora, the Rebellion accept Adora into their ranks after learning that she was mind-controlled into serving the Horde. The Rebels also discover that Queen Angella, rightful ruler of the kingdom of Bright Moon, is being held prisoner on nearby Talon Mountain, so Adam and Adora volunteer to rescue her. As He-Man and She-Ra, they defeat Queen Angella's jailer Hunga the Harpy, free Queen Angella, and reunite her with her people (including her daughter Glimmer).
Adam takes Adora back to Eternia to reunite with their parents, but Hordak discovers that Adora is with the Rebels and pursues them through the Time Gate. Finding himself back on Eternia, Hordak goes to his old base on Snake Mountain and discovers that Skeletor is now the principal villain of Eternia. Skeletor is not pleased to see his old mentor and engages him in a magical duel. Upon learning that Hordak is after Adora, Skeletor agrees to help him to be rid of him. Magically disguised as cooks and with Hordak hidden inside a giant cake, Skeletor and his henchmen manage to infiltrate the royal palace and kidnap Adora.
As Man-At-Arms, Teela and He-Man reassure the distraught king and queen that they will save Adora, Skeletor betrays Hordak and forces him back to Etheria, planning to ransom Adora himself. However, Adora manages to outwit her captors and, reclaiming her sword, deals with the villains as She-Ra before running into the rescue party. As He-Man introduces She-Ra to the others and helps her to convince them that Adora is safe, Skeletor is left bemoaning "A female He-Man! This is the worst day of my life!"
Adora decides to return to Etheria to aid the Rebellion, a decision accepted by her family, and the Sorceress sends Adora and Spirit back to Etheria, telling them they can use the Sword of Protection to summon aid from Eternia should they ever need it. Adam and Cringer tag along, offering to "help Adora get the Rebellion off to a big start".
As He-Man and She-Ra, the twins help the Rebels liberate Bright Moon, learning more about She-Ra's powers in the process (including using empathy to communicate with the wild animals of the Whispering Woods and healing Swift Wind when he is injured by the Horde). He-Man and Battle Cat then return to Eternia, while She-Ra and Swift Wind resolve to stay until all of Etheria is free.

query_text:
In 1949, former United States Army Air Forces officer Harvey Stovall spots a familiar Toby Jug in the window of a London antique shop and learns that it came from Archbury, an airfield where Stovall served during World War II. Convinced that it is the same jug which used to stand on the mantel of the airfield's officers' club, he buys it and journeys to the derelict airfield, where he reflects on his wartime experiences.
In a flashback, the setting shifts to 1942, when the 918th Bomb Group at Archbury has gained a reputation as the "hard luck group". After a particularly disastrous mission, group commander Colonel Keith Davenport appears exhausted and demoralized. His defeatist attitude spreads to other senior leaders of the group, including his Air Exec, Lieutenant Colonel Ben Gately. Ordered to fly another mission the next day, at a dangerously low altitude, Davenport protests to his friend, Brigadier General Frank Savage, the Assistant Chief of Staff for Operations at VIII Bomber Command. Later, Savage reluctantly shares with Major General Pritchard, the commanding general of VIII Bomber Command, his belief that Davenport has become emotionally too close to his men and may no longer be fit to command. That night, Pritchard and Savage visit the group headquarters to investigate the cause of the mission's heavy losses. Pritchard realizes that Savage is right: Davenport has become over-protective and is unwilling to discipline his men, even for costly mistakes. Davenport is relieved of command and Savage is asked to take over.
Savage takes a harsh approach to restoring the group's discipline and morale. He begins by reprimanding Gately, demoting him to aircraft commander and insisting that he henceforth fly every mission. Savage assigns Gately only the most incompetent crewmen, ordering him to paint the name "Leper Colony" on his airplane. Rough-and-ready Major Cobb impresses Savage with his independent spirit and replaces Gately as Air Exec. Savage conducts a series of training missions and waits for an opportunity to restore the group's pride in its abilities. Upset by the contrast of Savage's stern leadership with Davenport's easygoing ways, all of the group's pilots apply for transfers. Savage asks the Group Adjutant, Major Stovall, to delay processing their applications to buy him some time. An attorney in civilian life, Stovall knows how to use bureaucratic red tape to his advantage.
When the group returns to combat, all the groups are ordered to abort their mission due to heavy weather. Savage ignores the recall order. The 918th successfully bombs the target and is the only group to do so. All of its crews return safely. Though Pritchard is furious, Savage claims that he did not hear the recall due to a radio malfunction and instead persuades Pritchard to recommend the group for a Distinguished Unit Citation. Savage also acquires a surrogate son in Lieutenant Jesse Bishop, a Medal of Honor recipient who is Savage's eyes and ears among the combat aircrews.
When the Inspector General arrives to investigate the pilots' transfer requests, Savage packs his belongings, expecting to be relieved of command and possibly court-martialed. But, led by Bishop, the pilots withdraw their requests. Savage also softens his attitude towards the men as he becomes more closely involved with them. Gately goes on to win Savage's respect and admiration by demonstrating extraordinary leadership and courage in combat.
With enemy resistance intensifying as the air war advances deeper into Germany, missions become longer and riskier and many of Savage's best men are shot down or killed. Pritchard tries to get Savage to return to a staff job at VIII Bomber Command, but Savage feels that the 918th is not yet ready to do without him. Reluctantly, Pritchard leaves him in command. Ordered to return to the same target after a particularly brutal raid on a ball bearing factory, Savage finds himself physically unable to haul himself up into his B-17. Gately takes his place as lead pilot and strike commander for the mission. While waiting for the group's return, Savage becomes catatonic. Only as they return to Archbury does he regain his composure and fall asleep.

Dr. Eleanor  Ellie  Arroway (Jodie Foster) is a talented scientist, who was encouraged to pursue her passions for radio-telecommunication and astronomy by her father Theodore (David Morse). The latter died when she was only nine years old. She now works for the SETI program at the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico. She and her colleagues search for radio signals of extraterrestrial origin. However, government scientist David Drumlin (Tom Skerritt) cuts off funding for the SETI program, which he deems futile. Arroway gets funding from billionaire Mr. R. Hadden (John Hurt) to continue his research work at the Very Large Array in New Mexico.
Four years later, the project is still threatened with closure but Arroway discovers an important signal that reproduces a sequence of prime numbers, originating from a sector around the star Vega 26 light-years from Earth. The announcement of the discovery prompted Drumlin and the National Security Council headed by Michael Kitz (James Woods) to take control of the center. The project team discovered animated images in the signal, taken during a speech by Adolf Hitler during the opening ceremony of the 1936 Summer Olympics in Berlin. After the astonishment, Arroway and his team argued that this was the first television transmission likely to have left Earth's atmosphere, and that it was simply sent back from Vega to Earth to signal its reception.

For his film, Morgan Spurlock experimented on himself by eating nothing but McDonald's products for 30 days. His rules were: to eat exclusively at McDonald's (three complete meals a day), to eat every product on the menu at least once during the 30 days, to never walk more than 5,000 steps a day, and to always order a Supersize menu when it was offered to him (which was only the case a total of nine times).
The film shows Spurlock's preparation for the experiment and its aftermath, including examinations by three doctors and his conversations with a nutritionist. After 30 days, Spurlock had gained 11.1 kg, or 13% of his body weight. After completing the project, it took him five months to lose nine kilograms, and another nine months to lose the rest. Doctors noted altered liver values (however, in 2017, Spurlock admitted to being an alcoholic and "never been sober for more than a week in 30 years").
Further, Spurlock reports on the general health and social consequences of excessive fast-food consumption by comparing the supply situation of American schools: on the one hand, those supplied by private corporations, on the other hand, schools participating in the public health program. It also identifies some of the tricks used by advertisers to target children, such as edible cigarettes, which are later designed to reproduce the pleasurable feelings felt by children when they access the brand. Fast food chains are trying to do this with toys or something.
The film begins with a (later unsuccessful) lawsuit filed by two obese American girls against McDonald's, claiming that the company was responsible for their overweight and health consequences. In this context, Spurlock interviews U.S. consumers, physicians and nutritionists.

Medical student Nelson Wright is trying to get several of his classmates to participate in an experiment involving artificially induced near-death experiences. He is interested in scientific achievement and the fame that comes with it. In addition to Dave, who's just been suspended for four months for unauthorized emergency surgery, Joe and Randy, he's also asking Rachel for support. Rachel is interested in near-death experiences and uses every opportunity to interview affected patients about their experiences.
First, Nelson allows himself to be put into a state of clinical death for one minute and then resuscitated. Impressed by the success, Rachel wants to be put in this condition. But Joe wins the race by the length of the time: 1:30 minutes. The next night, the experiment is repeated, and again the arrest and resuscitation are successful.
The experiments have unexpected side effects for those involved. Nelson experiences frightening daydreams and injuries to his face. A small boy attacks him with hands and objects; during the attacks, Nelson recognizes that it is Billy Mahoney, with whom he himself played badly years ago. Joe is also haunted by apparitions. He sees on every screen accusing girls and women whom he lured into his bed with false promises and filmed there without their knowledge. Nelson and Joe don't talk about their negative experiences, but only talk about the positive experiences during clinical death.
After Joe, Rachel wants to be put in a state of clinical death. But Dave wants to last 2:20 minutes, so he's supposed to be next. As an atheist, for Dave, it's less a belief in a divine encounter than a desire to keep Rachel out of harm's way. He's starting to develop feelings for her and wants to protect her. Nelson observes this and reacts jealously. Dave's resuscitation almost fails, and it takes over 3:50 minutes for his heart to return to normal. Shortly thereafter, he too begins to daydream. He's being stalked by a former classmate he teased in the schoolyard years ago.
Now Rachel is enforcing her wish and wants to be put into clinical death for five minutes. But Dave wants to quit when he realizes the side effect of her experiments. He blames Joe and Nelson because they haven't said a word about their negative experiences. In Rachel's near-death experience, her father appears. He shot himself when she was five. Since then, Rachel feels guilty about her father's suicide. Having so far seen the afterlife as positive and desirable through the narratives of the near-death experiences, a world collapses for her when she is also haunted by the appearance of her dead father and she sees the afterlife as very dark.
When Joe returns home that evening, he is surprised to find his fiancée in his apartment. She discovered the videos and broke off her engagement. Dave tries to confront his visions, and eventually finds the girl he teased as a child. On the way to see her, Nelson joins him, because out of fear and desperation for Billy Mahoney, he doesn't want to be alone anymore. Dave approaches the girl from back then; she is now a mother herself and grows flowers. After a lengthy conversation, she accepts Dave's apology and thanks him for this late clarification.
Nelson begins to injure himself more and more violently during his daydreams. Which is why Dave is giving Joe and Randy custody of Nelson. You're supposed to help him get rid of his guilt by finding Billy Mahoney. Nelson takes them to the cemetery and shows them Billy's grave. In desperation, he tells her that Mahoney died because of him and therefore he has no way to apologize. After confessing and announcing that he would make amends, Nelson flees his two friends by car. They communicate with Dave, and together they set off in search of him.
Rachel will be left alone. She remembers in a daydream that her father used drugs. She realizes her unfounded self-condemnation and comes to terms with her father in a dream. Shortly thereafter, Nelson calls Rachel's house and announces his reconciliation with Billy Mahoney. He's planning on putting himself to clinical death to pay off his debt to Billy.
Rachel, Joe, Dave and Randy rush to Nelson and try to resuscitate him. On the verge of absolute death, Nelson makes peace with Billy Mahoney in a vision. At the last second, he's picked up by his friends and awakened.

Kate Mosley is trying to make a career as an advertising executive in New York City, confident in her talent, but failing to make headway. When she is offered a promotion, her boss decides not to give it to her because she is not stable enough emotionally. Her colleague Darcy then discovers that Kate is engaged to a boy named Nick who lives in Boston, Massachusetts, and works as a videographer for weddings and christenings, with whom Kate actually only took a picture during a wedding.
Everything seems to work out for Kate, in fact she gets the attention of her colleague, Sam Mayfair, who she has always liked. But events take an unexpected turn when she's forced to bring her fake boyfriend to a dinner with her boss after Nick saves a little girl from a fire and ends up in the papers. So Kate tracks down Nick and the two try to get to know each other to prove they're engaged, but as they get to know each other, they begin to be attracted to each other. During dinner, Kate tries to break the farce by asking Nick for an excuse to leave her; he does not want to but agrees to please Kate and so the two break up. Meanwhile, she breaks up with Sam too, realizing he's not the right man for her.
A week later, Kate, feeling guilty, tells her employers the truth about the cover-up and so her boss orders her to take a few days off to reflect on the situation with Nick. Kate realizes that she is truly in love with Nick and therefore goes to him while he is filming a wedding in a church; here she declares her love to him and kisses him while Nick invites her as a guest to the wedding.

After completing their education at an upscale boarding school on the East Coast, two young McIntire brothers, John and George, return diligently to their father's ranch in the Wild West. They soon realize that life is not quite the same as in New England. Upon arrival, they are attacked by bandits but are saved by a mysterious, mute stranger dressed in black.
At their father's ranch, as the brothers visit their mother's grave, their father tells them that a gang of gangsters has been terrorizing the town for some time. But also the story of the occupants of the tomb next door. Years earlier, a mother and her young son were murdered by outlaws, and the husband was seriously injured and nursed by their mother. He recovered, became a formidable marksman, nicknamed "Cemetery", and became close to the widower. That same evening, the father's reception to celebrate his sons' return is disrupted by the arrival of the "collector", the leader of the gang that blackmails all the ranchers in town. But the McIntires can rely on Samaritan Cemetery, who's watching over them and determined to fight the gang of racketeers.
option_3_text: Nelson convinces his group of university friends to help him in a controversial science experiment. The idea is simple, cause death by strong doses of medicine and resurrect, thanks to science, and then tell others about your experience in the afterlife. Everyone in the group participates out of a desire to experiment, and little by little it becomes a kind of bet on who will stay dead the longest. But soon the group find themselves dealing with dark, sometimes violent presences, as in Nelson's case, who seem to want to punish them for events in their past.

DJ Andrey Pushkaryov wakes up in his Moscow apartment, packs his records into his suitcase, and makes his way to Domodedovo Airport to fly to Zurich. Upon his arrival, he is greeted by the promoter of the Supermarket Club. After a short nap in his hotel room, he is awakened by his alarm clock in the middle of the night, packs up his things and leaves for his performance. After the gig, he gets on the train to Geneva and falls back asleep.
After a brief visit to a friend in Geneva, he takes a flight back to Moscow.
This "story line" is the first loop of the film, which Pushkaryov repeats again and again with minor deviations in the following film.
Arriving at his Moscow apartment, he first processes his booking requests before choosing from his collection of vinyl the discs for his next gig. He takes a taxi to the Leningrad railway station and gets on the train to St. Petersburg.
Once there, he listens to new tracks on Beatport. In the evening, he will be driven to the Barakobamabar, where his next performance is scheduled. At dawn, he and a friend take the subway to the station.
Back in Moscow  and back to a new action Loop, he sits down with friends and talks about his dream of wearing  only during the day  and pushing the techno club industry to put people in a healthier situation by doing so.
After a short trip on the subway, he stops at Club Mir and flies back to Geneva. From Geneva, he takes the train to Olten via Bern, where the promoter picks him up and drives him to Club Terminus. There are technical problems: the Technics SL-1210 turntables do not want to downgrade from 45 to 33 rpm. In addition, a technician from the club later applies his hand to the tonearm. Tired, Andrey takes a taxi to his hotel, where he works on the computer to process further booking requests.
The next morning, he takes the train to Lausanne and then a high-speed train to Paris. After a performance at the Club 4 Éléments, he travels to the SWISS hub in Zurich, where he books a flight to Budapest.
The club crew takes him from Budapest to Kecel, where he puts on at Club Korona in front of a large crowd. On the way back to Budapest, he falls asleep in the car and misses the skyline of the capital. Once at the hotel, he again has only a limited number of free hours before heading back to the airport, ending another "loop".
Arriving in Zurich, he booked a flight to Bucharest. Once there, he'll be driven to Craiova, where he'll stop at Club Krypton without sleep or rest.
The next day, he misses the return trip because of one of the worst snowstorms in Romania. He arrives at a club called Midi in Cluj-Napoca, stops for an ecstatic crowd, and then finds himself back in the car on the way back.
Finally, you see Andrey on the beach, where he watches the waves and disappears after a short time. His suitcase with the plates is the last one in the picture.

Seattle Medical Examiner Dr. David Krane (Ray Liotta) arrives at a crime scene, an apparent drug store robbery. He finds a matchbook that reminds him of a similar matchbook found at the scene of his wife Mary's murder. Krane is convinced that the killer is the same man who killed his wife. He approaches Detective Don Bresler (Peter Coyote), insisting that, should he find a suspect, to interrogate them about his wife's murder.
Later, Krane goes to a dinner where Dr. Martha Briggs (Linda Fiorentino) gives a lecture on her experiment to transfer memories. She tells Krane that neuro-peptides are used in forming memories and can be retrieved from Cerebral Spinal Fluid (CSF). She has created a serum designed to facilitate the memory transfer process but an external stimulus similar to the memory must also be present for the memories to successfully imprint on the recipient. When Dr. Krane learns human trials are many years away, he says he would volunteer to try the serum, but Dr. Briggs refuses.
Later that evening Krane retrieves the sample of CSF from his wife's autopsy, and then breaks into Dr. Briggs' office. He then goes back to his house which is filled with crime scene photos. Krane injects himself with the serum, and has a memory flash of the night of his wife's murder, but is unable to see the killer's face. Krane then returns to the lab, retrieves the CSF from the female victim at the drug store. Krane drives to the drug store where he then injects himself, again, with the serum. Krane is finally able to see the killer's face. He then meets with a police sketch artist and tries to create a sketch of the killer. Krane and his friend and colleague, Curtis Avery (David Paymer), enter the sketch into a computer program that generates a searchable photo of the killer.
Dr. Briggs then confronts Krane about the break in and the theft of her serum. He explains that it works and that you experience the memory as if it were happening to you. Dr. Briggs is worried about side effects and gives Krane a physical, noting that there has been "significant" damage to Krane's heart. Curtis says they got a hit on the photo, identifying the suspect as Eddie Dutton.  Dutton has a long criminal history, including drugs and several murders for hire. Curtis gives Krane Eddie's last known address.
Krane and Dr. Briggs travel to the seedy motel where Eddie Dutton resides.  He soon sees Eddie in the elevator, and has an overreaction to seeing him. Krane runs down the stairs after Eddie. Dr. Briggs yells at Krane to stop as he is straining his heart. Krane pursues Eddie, who pulls out a gun and starts to fire at Krane. Eddie runs into an alley, where the two struggle and Krane ends up with Eddie's gun. Eddie runs into a Catholic church, and grabs a young boy, holding him hostage with a knife. Dr Krane tries to talk Eddie down when the police arrive. Eventually Det. Bresler fatally shoots Eddie, and Dr. Krane is upset because he did not get to question Eddie.
Dr. Krane is confronted about his erratic behavior by his supervisor who fires him. Krane and Dr. Briggs go to the Police station, where Krane sneaks into the autopsy room and steals a sample of Eddie's CSF.
Back at his house, Krane injects himself with the serum, using Eddie's CSF. Krane has a flash of what appears to be Eddie having rough sex with a woman, who may be Mary. In the midst of the memory flashback Krane inadvertently begins to choke Dr. Briggs. During the flashback Dr. Krane sees that Eddie notices Krane returning to the house and Eddie flees, apparently before Mary is actually dead. Dr. Briggs finds Krane at the bottom of the porch stairs and administers the nitroglycerin to him. He explains that Eddie did not kill his wife, and that he had come home drunk that night and passed out in the front yard while his wife was being murdered. Krane opens up about how he was a drunk and the marriage was on the rocks. He mentions that when his wife died she was 5 weeks pregnant.
The next morning Dr. Briggs goes to Curtis and asks him to get a DNA sample from Krane. As Dr. Briggs is running the DNA for a paternity test, Krane walks in and is angry that she would test the paternity without consulting him. The paternity test shows the baby was not Krane's child.
Krane rushes over and confronts Mary's sister Kelly (Kim Cattrall). They argue, and Kelly says that Mary was having an affair with a police detective. While talking to Det. Bresler about this new information, Krane begins to have flashbacks of an interrogation of Eddie. These flashbacks cause a heart attack and Krane is rushed to the hospital. Krane has flashbacks of the night and subsequent events of Mary's murder. While Krane and Dr. Briggs are at the hospital, an explosive device destroys Dr. Briggs office.
After Krane recovers, Detective Stewart Gleick (Christopher McDonald) the original detective on Mary's case, approaches Krane in the hospital saying that a detective named Joseph Bodner may be the man with whom Mary was involved, thus making him the likely father of her unborn child. Detective Bodner tried to commit suicide on the same day Mary was killed, but ended up in a coma instead. Krane and Dr. Briggs go to the hospice where Det. Bodner is, and take a sample of his CSF. Krane and Dr. Briggs argue about who should take the injection. Krane says he is not taking any chances and he tapes Dr. Briggs to the seat and injects himself. He confirms that his wife was in fact having an affair with Bodner. Mary met Detective Bodner who was a witness against Detective Bresler, who is revealed to have been quite corrupt.
As Krane is reliving these memories, Detective Bresler arrives at the house and begins to set the scene to kill Krane and Dr. Briggs by lighting a fire. Kelly arrives at the house with Krane's kids, just as Bresler is about to kill them. Krane fights Bresler, beating him unconscious. Krane then pulls Dr. Briggs out of the house, and then rushes in to save Bresler. He then goes back into the burning house to retrieve the microcassette recorder that recorded Bresler's confession.
The movie ends with Krane in a coma. He imagines he is with his wife. Dr. Briggs explains that his wounds should heal, but he is not responding mentally. Det. Gleick tells Krane that they got Bresler. Dr. Briggs says he could snap out of his coma at any time. The scene then shifts to Krane imagining playing with his kids, he looks back over his shoulder and his wife turns and fades away.

His desire is to be able to stop stealing and get out of the business, but he does not succeed, until he meets Elyse, an actress and con artist, with whom he organizes a last trick that will set them free.

The story is set in rural Denmark in the late 1960s. One day, a 13-year-old boy named Frits Johansen (Janus Dissing Rathke), also known as Martin, returns home, but finds his father under the table in the dining room, where he tells him that he must hide so that no one sees them.
He suffers the tyranny of his teacher, who refuses to see his evolution in the classroom. During all the summer holidays Frits sees everything on TV. He is particularly interested in news from the USA: Martin Luther King's "I have a dream" and his dream of a better world without oppression and racial discrimination, as well as demonstrations in the big cities. The seeds of rebellion are sown and it is only necessary to wait for the return to school for the new ideas to become facts.
At home everything is in disarray, his father has fallen into a depression and at school boredom alternates with pulling ears in the principal's office. But things are about to change: the father regains his courage and a new teacher arrives who listens to rock music at school, has posters of Che Guevara and above all questions the principal and his cruel methods of education.

query_text: Tom Ripley (Matt Damon), a young employee of a Manhattan service company, borrows a Princeton jacket to play the piano at an outdoor party. When the rich owner of the house chats with him upon seeing his jacket, Ripley hints that he is a friend and college buddy of his son Dickie (Jude Law); then, the father offers him a thousand dollars if he goes to Italy and convinces Dickie to return home to run the family business and spend his last moments with his sick mother. When he meets Dickie, who is a playboy, he is fascinated by the lifestyle he and his girlfriend Marge (Gwyneth Paltrow) lead. She quickly becomes accustomed to this way of life and Dickie's company, for which she begins to feel something more than friendship. When he is finally forced to reveal his feelings, he is faced with a decision that will change his whole life.
