When Tun decided to end their brief affair, the girl fell into a deep depression, attempted suicide, and eventually - the boy says - disappeared and he knew nothing more about her fate.
Tun and Jane then decide to go to the girl's village to find out what happened to her. During the journey Natre appears several times thrown at the pursuit of their car. When they arrive in the girl's hometown, they discover that she had committed suicide and that her mother still keeps her body at home. The two boys convince Natre's mother to have her cremated after a proper religious ceremony, hoping this will appease the dead girl's wrath, but it does not produce the desired results.
In fact, Natre's spirit is still wandering around waiting for justice and scattering clues to help Jane find out what really happened to her. In this way Jane finds pictures taken by Tun in which his friends are seen raping Natre. Strangled, the boy says that his friends convinced him to go to her in a group to harass her, in order to free him from the torment of the girl he was in love with. The incident tragically turned into group sexual violence, in which Tun did not actively participate despite being involved by taking photos, at the urging of his friends, to prevent the girl from talking later.
It is understood that shocked by the event and filled with shame for what happened the girl would then return to her native country to commit suicide. Jane quarrels and leaves, leaving only Tun, who, enraged, starts taking pictures of her apartment to find out where Natre is hiding. He finds out only when, after slamming his Polaroid against the bulletin board on which he posted the photos, it bounces and falls to the ground and automatically takes a picture.
Natre's ghost is clinging to his back, never to let go of his one true love. The spirit covers Tun's eyes, who, staggering blindly, falls backwards from the window. Wounded, committed to an asylum, you can still see him hunched over under the weight of the ghost of his lover.
option_3_text:
After the Battle of Sekigahara, a samurai is hired by the Tokugawa shogun to raise a group of young boys and turn them into assassins to finish off Toyotomi's allies and prevent another civil war.
Azumi (Aya Ueto) is a young girl about 7-8 years old, selected because of the coldness shown in the face of her mother's death at the hands of samurai master Gessai (Yoshio Harada). Azumi is raised as an expert in martial arts and a master of sword fighting. Azumi and his nine companions grow up with the goal of an unidentified "mission" that they must complete when the time comes.
When they are little more than teenagers, the master Gessai gathers his ten disciples and instructs them to form pairs, choosing their own best friend. After which Gessai gives the order to fight to the death, since of the ten boys only five will have to complete the mission. Azumi and his companions are perplexed and fight, but eventually they proceed to execute Gessai's order and each kill their own best friend, including Azumi.
Internal conflicts and questions begin to arise in Azumi and the others, when they realize that the "mission" does not provide that they can help women and children slaughtered by a group of bandits, as this would be outside of their main task of killing the "warlords" Asano Nagamasa, Masayuki Sanada and Kiyomasa Kato.
But more than warlords, Azumi will have to deal with the unstoppable mercenary Bijomaru Mogami. Despite the effeminate and unthreatening appearance, Bijomaru will prove to be a crazy and terrible fighter, responsible for the death of one of Azumi's comrades and penultimate enemy that Azumi will have to face in the course of the film.
option_4_text: Joe is a gangster who ended up in jail for tax evasion (remember Al Capone). His wife always thought he was innocent, but when a reporter tells her the truth, she leaves him. She falls in love with the journalist and when Joe gets out of prison after serving his sentence, the two lovers become prey to the gangster's revenge.

query_text: In the gynaecology department of a German hospital, the events that mark the stay of some women as well as the daily lives of the main members of the medical staff are followed for a few weeks.
option_0_text: Mystic Pizza follows the lives of three young waitresses in a small American town called Mystic, Connecticut, in the late 1980s. For Daisy Arújo, her sensitive sister Kat, and their friend Jojo Barbosa, the last summer after high school will be a summer they'll never forget. The three friends work at the local pizzeria and there they will share their desires, their dreams and their plans to escape from the small town. When Daisy falls in love with a young man named Charles, everyone thinks she's found a way to leave town. But when the girls discover that Charles is not the man he appears to be, they realize that with friendship and self-respect they will find themselves and a way out of Mystic.
option_1_text:
Starting at a party in Los Angeles near Christmas, Harry Lockhart (Robert Downey Jr.) narrates the events of the film in the first person. After escaping a botched toy store robbery, Harry's friend is found dead, forcing him to hide in a building where they were conducting an audition. Seeing that the script was similar to the events of that night, Harry impresses the producers with his performance.
After Harry flies to Hollywood for a screen test, he is introduced to "Gay" Perry Van Shrike (Val Kilmer), who offers to help Harry in his preparation for the role. At the beginning of the party, Harry meets his friend and childhood sweetheart Harmony Lane (Michelle Monaghan). Because her sister was sexually abused by her father, Harmony traveled to Los Angeles to become an actress and help her sister. At the same time Harry meets Harlan Dexter (Corbin Bernsen), a retired millionaire actor who has recently resolved a ten-year standoff over his wife's inheritance with his daughter Veronica.
The next day while investigating, Harry and Perry witness a vehicle and a body being thrown into a lake, only to be detected by the killers; as Perry accidentally shoots the body, they cannot call the police. As they return to the hotel, Harry receives a call warning him of Harmony's suicide, only for her to appear at his bedroom door moments later informing him that his sister had flown to Los Angeles, stolen his wallet and papers and then committed suicide.
Believing Harry to be a detective, Harmony asks him to investigate Jenna's death because she thinks it's a murder. After Harmony leaves, Harry discovers in his bathroom the body that was in the lake along with a gun that had been planted on him. After he and Perry dispose of the body, it is found and identified as Veronica Dexter, whom they had seen at the party. Perry tells Harry to leave Los Angeles because the killers had identified and targeted him. However, Harry discovers that Perry had been hired by Harmony's deceased sister, revealing the connection between the two cases.
Attending a party where Harmony is working, the three discover that Harmony had told her late sister that her father was the character played by Harlan Dexter and that that was what prompted her to travel to Los Angeles. As Perry retreats to monitor another case, Harry is confronted by the Lake Killers (Dash Mihok and Rockmond Dunbard) who threaten and beat him. While taking Harry to the hospital, Harmony realizes that the killers are headed towards where Perry is guarding, and decides to go rescue him. While Harry is unconscious in Harmony's car, a pink-haired girl accomplice to the killers (Shannyn Sossamon) inadvertently takes Harry to his lair; when Harry sees her being killed by one of the Lake's killers, he kills him in a fit of rage.
After Harmony disappears following a lead, Harry and Perry investigate a private clinic owned by Harlan Dexter; there they discover that Veronica Dexter was killed and her body supplanted by another which dismissed the charges against Harlan and put him in possession of his wife's entire inheritance. After being captured by Harlan, he reveals to them that his plan is to burn his daughter's real body to destroy the evidence only for Harmony to steal and crash the van leaving Veronica's body hanging from a bridge on the highway. After Harmony escapes and crashes after a fall, a shootout ensues that leaves Harry and Perry injured. Harry in an attempt to save Harmony, falls off the bridge clinging to Veronica's body. After a shootout with Harlan and his henchmen, Harry finds Harmony and collapses from his injuries.
When Harry wakes up in the hospital he finds that Harmony and Perry are fine, and he reveals that Harmony's sister was not murdered but had effectively committed suicide. After Jenna escaped abuse in Indiana, she searched for Harlan believing he was her real father only to find him having sex with the pink-haired girl who played the impostor daughter. Faced with this, Jenna believed that Harlan was an abuser like his real father, and after hiring Perry with Harmony's credit card to investigate, ended his life.
The film contains an epilogue where Perry confronts Harmony and Jenna's father, and then gives way to a monologue where Harry tells how he currently works for Perry.
option_2_text: 1939, shortly before the outbreak of World War II. Carl Ehrlich, captain of the German freighter Ergenstrass, whose avowed anti-Naziism had deprived him of his military command, bet his childhood friend Commander Jeff Napier that he would break out of Sydney Harbour by forcing the blockade. However, the German consul demands that Ehrlich take on board Elsa von Schwepp, an adventurer who occasionally works for the German secret services and who happens to be Napier's fiancée. The captain of the Ergenstrass was ordered to drop off her passenger in a neutral port.
option_3_text:
In episodic form, everyday stories from the gynaecological department of a clinic are told, combined with the private and marital problems of the two male protagonists, a chief physician and his superior, the chief physician.
Among the patients faced with important decisions by both doctors is a young woman with cancer who is faced with the choice between accepting treatment that could endanger her child's life or putting her child's welfare first. In the case of Angelika Schneider, who was accompanied by her mother, there is more than just the question 'child or not child' in the room. Her own life is in the highest, most acute danger, because the 15-year-old girl is pregnant and, in desperation, tried to abort the fetus herself with a needle. She's been bleeding profusely from the abdomen ever since.
Private problems, in turn, are driving Chief Physician Prof. Overhoff and his chief physician, Dr. Schumann. Overhoff had a traumatic experience: his wife died of a pulmonary embolism while giving birth to their second child. He blames himself. Now, as a single father, Overhoff must care for his adolescent daughter Eva and an infant. Schumann, on the other hand, is married to a woman who is equally as demanding as she is beautiful, young and a bit over-excited, who is about 20 years younger than him and prefers to act and act exalted. Claudia Schumann even brings unrest to the hospital operation and thereby strains Schumann's relationship with his boss. Because she accuses prof. Overhoff, to have been responsible for the death of his wife, having impregnated her at an advanced age.
This tragic event leads to the fact that now Claudia Schumann does not want to have children for fear that she might end up like Mrs. Overhoff, which in turn leads to tensions with her husband. In fact, her neuroses go so far as to hide and hoard medication, including birth control pills, in her doll collection. When Eva Overhoff discovers this, she immediately shares her knowledge with her father, who in turn informs his chief physician. Schumann's attempt to reason with his wife fails. When Claudia assumes that her husband, who occasionally has fun with the attractive nurse from the nursery, has messed up her cycle and therefore she has become pregnant, she makes a suicide attempt using sleeping pills.
option_4_text:
In the prologue, the armies of the Westlands assemble in preparation for Tarmon Gai'don, as do the forces of the Shadow.  The Forsaken Demandred stages a raid on the city of Caemlyn, sending Trollocs to capture the cannons, developed jointly by Matrim Cauthon, Queen Elayne Trakand, and the Illuminator Aludra. Talmanes Delovinde and the Band of the Red Hand launch their own counter-attack and successfully exfiltrate the cannons out of the city, but Caemlyn is lost.
The Light is bolstered by people coming from all over the world to fight, sensing the end of all things, while the Shadow welcomes a new Forsaken: Mazrim Taim, now called "M'Hael".
# The Field of Merrilor
Rand al'Thor prepares a meeting of all the nations on the Field of Merrilor, to persuade them to fight in Tarmon Gai'don. Mat returns to Ebou Dar to locate Tuon, only to find the city crawling with assassins sent by one of her generals. At the Black Tower, Logain Ablar is missing and Mazrim Taim is forcibly "Turning" people to the Shadow. The Asha'man still loyal to Logain, led by Androl Genhald and aided by Aes Sedai ambassador Pevara Tazanovni rescue Logain, defeating Taim and driving his Dreadlords from the Tower. Rand's "price" of allegiance—a treaty called "The Dragon's Peace", in which borders are fixed and war is outlawed—and his plan to shatter the remaining seals of the Dark One's prison, lead to widespread argument; the latter resolved only when Moiraine Damodred quotes from the Prophecies of the Dragon, and convinces Egwene to break the seals herself. The Aiel, persuaded by Aviendha's post-apocalyptic visions during Towers of Midnight, demand to be subject to the treaty, as arbiters of any dispute.  When Elayne Trakand remarks that peace cannot be maintained if the Seanchan are exempt, Rand agrees to persuade their cooperation, and appoints Elayne commander-in-chief of the armies formerly under himself.
# The War
Elayne dispatches her forces to four different campaigns, whereof Caemlyn is to be retaken by Andoran and Cairhienin troops; Egwene commands an army of Aes Sedai to reinforce Kandor, while Lan Mandragoran and the resurrected nation of Malkier hold Tarwin's Gap. Rand himself will lead the Aiel to face the Dark One. The four remaining "Great Captains" are attached to each campaign: Gareth Bryne in Kandor, Agelmar Jagad at Tarwin's Gap, Rodel Ituralde to Shayol Ghul, and Davram Bashere to serve Elayne directly. The campaigns turn to disaster when Graendal, now renamed Hessalam, Compels the commanders to err. Rand gains the support of the Seanchan by persuading Tuon in Ebou Dar that his authority, as the reincarnation of Lews Therin, supersedes hers. The Seanchan march to battle with Mat as one of their generals. Taking only Moiraine, Nynaeve al'Meara, and the sa'angreal Callandor, Rand confronts the Dark One's champion, Moridin; interrupted only when Rand makes contact with the Dark One. Meanwhile, Perrin Aybara enters Tel'aran'rhiod to protect Rand from Slayer. In this he is assisted by Lanfear; but wounded by Slayer and forced to retreat. Rand and Egwene learn that enemy agents have seized some of the Dark One's seals. Elayne's forces burn Caemlyn to force the Trollocs to pursue; but they are pursued also by a new force from the north, and saved by Logain and his loyal Asha'man. At Tarwin's Gap, the defenders are forced into a rout; while in Kandor, Egwene and the Aes Sedai are unexpectedly outflanked by the nation of Shara, under Demandred. Realizing that Mat's foxhead medallion makes him the only competent general immune to hostile 'Compulsion', Egwene gives him command of their forces, and Mat rallies the survivors at the Field of Merrilor.
# The Last Battle
To lure Demandred into risking his resources, Mat stages a public quarrel with Tuon, and the Seanchan depart the field. Perrin continues pursuit of Slayer. At Shayol Ghul, Graendal opposes the Aiel. When Demandred challenges the absent Rand, Gawyn Trakand attacks him directly and is mortally wounded. Later, his elder half-brother Galad Damodred is severely wounded in the same effort; but wounds Demandred before retreat. Mat's command post is attacked directly by Sharan forces, and Siuan Sanche is killed in the defense. Gareth Bryne loses reason and dies soon after. Elayne is waylaid by several Darkfriend Guardsmen including Doilin Mellar, who arrange a duplicate of Elayne to be seen dead. Faile's contingent arrive at Merrilor, but are almost immediately betrayed. Faile seizes the Horn of Valere (capable of recruiting deceased heroes), which she gives to Olver.
Androl and Pevara track down M'Hael and steal the remaining seals on the Dark One's prison. Egwene then asks Leilwin Shipless to be her warder and attacks M'Hael. M'Hael uses balefire to destroy a number of Aes Sedai. In the midst of her fight with M'Hael, Egwene creates a new weave, the "Flame of Tar Valon", capable of counteracting balefire, and sacrifices her own life to destroy M'Hael and his followers. Galad passes  Mat's foxhead medallion to Lan, and Lan attacks Demandred, killing him in single combat by letting Demandred stab him, then decapitating the Forsaken while his blade is thus engaged. Olver sounds the Horn of Valere, summoning legendary heroes to rescue Elayne. Mat uses the Heroes and reinforcements from the Seanchan to sweep the field.
# Shayol Ghul
Outside the Pattern, Shai'tan and Rand duel by constructing their visions of what reality could be after Tarmon Gai'don, and ultimately achieve stalemate on the premise that the Pattern is incomplete in case of either's defeat. Perrin kills Slayer at the Pit of Doom, and later kills Lanfear before she can kill Moiraine (later revealed by Brandon Sanderson to be a faked death by Lanfear) Mat kills Padan Fain with his own dagger. Olver and the resurrected heroes win the battle, while Aviendha mentally enslaves Graendal. Rand resumes his duel with Moridin, during which Rand, Moiraine, and Nynaeve take control of Moridin and use his power to create a huge weave of saidar, saidin, and True Power combined. Seeing this, Logain breaks open the Dark One's prison, and Rand uses the huge weave of three powers, first to capture the Dark One, and later to re-create his prison without flaw.
# Epilogue
Bereft of the Dark One's influence, the Blight dissolves. Mat reunites with Tuon, who reveals that she is pregnant by him; whereas Perrin locates Faile buried under Trolloc corpses, but alive, and inherits the throne of Saldaea. King Alsalam of Arad Doman is revealed to be dead, and Ituralde succeeds him. Cadsuane Melaidhrin is elected the new Amyrlin Seat, while Moghedien is captured by a sul'dam. Thom and Moiraine, Lan and Nynaeve, wait attendance on Rand, who is slowly dying of his wounds. A funeral pyre is held; but it is revealed that Rand had exchanged psyches with Moridin, and is therefore alive. No longer able to channel the One Power, Rand now has the ability to manipulate the Pattern directly, though it is unclear to what extent. He demonstrates this ability by lighting his pipe without the use of the One Power.

query_text: In 1940, the young Lady Diana Broughton and her husband (thirty years her senior), Sir Henry 'Jock' Broughton, settled in the British colony of Kenya, caring little  as much as the small British community they joined  about the ongoing war. Colonial life is divided between worldliness, horse racing, sentimental intrigue, women are nymphomaniacs, men runners of petticoats and heavy drinkers. Diana then meets Josslyn 'Joss' Hay, Earl of Erroll, a member of this community, and becomes his mistress...thinking she can count on her old husband's indulgence and understanding. His miscalculation will lead to tragedy.
option_0_text: Despite her family's traditions, Mary Magdalene decides to accompany a social movement that is built around Jesus of Nazareth.
option_1_text:
Philadelphia-based child psychologist Malcolm Crowe returns home with his wife, Anna, after having been honored for his work. Vincent Grey, a former patient Malcolm had treated for hallucinations, breaks into their house and accuses Malcolm of failing him before shooting Malcolm and then himself.
Months later, Malcolm begins working with Cole Sear, a 9-year-old boy who reminds him of Vincent. He feels he must help Cole to rectify his failure to help Vincent and reconcile with Anna, who has become distant and cold. Cole's mother, Lynn, worries about his social skills, especially after seeing signs of physical harm. At a birthday party, Cole is cornered by bullies who lock him in a cupboard, causing him to scream in terror before passing out. Following this incident, Cole finally confides to Malcolm that he sees ghosts walking around like the living, but they only see what they want to see and are unaware that they are dead.
Malcolm thinks Cole is delusional and considers dropping his case, but after listening to an audiotape from a session with Vincent, he hears a man tearfully begging for help in Spanish and realizes that the ghosts Cole sees are real. He suggests that Cole try to communicate with the ghosts and help them finish their business, to which Cole hesitantly agrees.
Cole awakens one night to discover a ghost girl vomiting. He finds out who she is and goes with Malcolm to the funeral reception at her home. Cole sneaks into the girl's room, where she crawls out from under her bed and gives him a box containing a videotape, which he gives to her father. The tape reveals the girl's mother poisoning her food, alerting her father to this and saving her younger sister from the same fate.
Before parting ways with Malcolm, Cole suggests that he try speaking to Anna while she is asleep to communicate better with her.
While stuck in traffic, Cole tells his mother his secret and says that someone died in an accident down the road. When Lynn does not believe him, Cole tells her his late grandmother visits him and describes how she saw Lynn in a dance performance when she was a child, giving details that he could not have known. Cole's mother finally accepts the fact that her son has a special ability and tearfully embraces him.
Malcolm returns home to find Anna talking in her sleep, asking Malcolm why he left her, much to his confusion. When she suddenly drops Malcolm's wedding ring, he notices that it is not on his finger. Recalling what Cole told him about dead people only seeing what they want to see and not knowing they are dead, Malcolm finally realizes he did not survive being shot by Vincent and has been dead while working with Cole. He quickly comes to terms with his death and tells Anna that he loves her. She bids him goodnight, indicating that she is now at peace and can move on. With his business finally complete, Malcolm's spirit departs in a flash of light.
option_2_text:
As King Arthur prepares for battle against his former friend, Sir Lancelot, he reflects on the sad circumstances which have led him to this situation.
He recalls the night of his marriage to Guenevere. It is an arranged marriage, and he is afraid of what lies ahead ("I Wonder What the King is Doing Tonight"). Guenevere herself is worried about marrying a man she has never met and longs for the romantic life of a fought-over maiden ("The Simple Joys of Maidenhood"). They converse, and as she does not know his true identity, she fantasizes about escaping with him. Arthur tells her what a wonderful place his kingdom is ("Camelot"). She finds herself drawn to him, but they are interrupted by his men and her entourage. Arthur's identity is revealed, and Guenevere gladly goes with him to be married.
Four years later, Arthur explores with Guenevere his idea for a Round Table that would seat all the noble knights of the realm, reflecting not only a crude type of democratic ideal, but also the political unification of England. Inspired by Arthur's ideas, the French Knight Lancelot makes his way to England with his squire Dap, boasting of his superior virtues ("C'est Moi"). Lancelot's prowess impresses Arthur, and they become friends; however, many of the knights instantly despise Lancelot for his self-righteousness and boastfulness. Back in Camelot, Guinevere and the women frolic and gather flowers to celebrate the coming of spring ("The Lusty Month of May").
Guenevere, who initially dislikes Lancelot, incites three of the best knights to challenge him to a joust ("Then You May Take Me To The Fair"). Arthur ponders how distant Guenevere has become ("How to Handle a Woman"). Guenevere's plan goes awry as Lancelot easily defeats all three, critically wounding Sir Dinadan. A horrified Lancelot pleads for Sir Dinadan to live, and as he lays hands on him, Dinadan miraculously recovers. Guenevere is so overwhelmed and humbled that her feelings for Lancelot begin to change. Despite his vows of celibacy, Lancelot falls in love with Guenevere.
Guinevere and Lancelot meet in secret to discuss their future. Lancelot vows that he should leave and never come back, but finds it impossible to consider leaving Guenevere ("If Ever I Would Leave You"). Arthur decides to rise above the scandal. Mordred, Arthur's illegitimate son, arrives at Camelot determined to bring down the fellowship of the Round Table by stirring up trouble. All this takes its toll on Arthur's disposition, and Guenevere tries to cheer him up ("What Do the Simple Folk Do?") despite her conflicted emotions.
Mordred persuades Arthur to stay out hunting all night as a test, knowing that Lancelot will visit Guenevere in her bedchamber. Lancelot and Guenevere sing of their forbidden love and how wrong it has all gone ("I Loved You Once In Silence"). Mordred and several knights catch the lovers together. Lancelot escapes, but Guenevere is arrested. Thanks to Arthur's new civil court and trial by jury, she is sentenced to die by burning at the stake. Bound by his own law, Arthur cannot spare her. Preparations are made for Guenevere's burning ("Guenevere"), but Lancelot rescues her at the last minute, much to Arthur's relief.
On the battlefield, Arthur receives a surprise visit from Lancelot and Guenevere, at the edge of the woods, where she has taken residence at a convent. The three share an emotional farewell.
Prior to the battle, Arthur stumbles across a young boy named Tom, who espouses his commitment to Arthur's original ideal of "Not might 'makes' right, but might 'for' right." Arthur realizes that, although most of his plans have fallen through, the ideals of Camelot live on in this simple boy. He knights Tom and gives him his orders: run behind the lines and survive the battle, so that he can tell future generations about the legend of Camelot. Watching Tom leave, Arthur regains his hope for the future ("Camelot (reprise)").
option_3_text:
The work consists of a dialogue between two people, in the dialogue called He (Lui) and I (Moi).
The "literary" Diderot or moi takes his evening promenade to the Palais Royal. Here he meets Jean-François Rameau or lui, whom he has known for some time, and after a short conversation invites him to the Café de la Régence. It is Jean-François Rameau, the nephew of the famous composer Jean-Philippe Rameau. With this acquaintance, the lui, he will have an extended conversation along the way. From this person, the moi feels both attracted and repulsed. Because the nephew is not just a cynic who is eloquent, rich in gestures, charming and without shame reveals his parasitic existence and immorality and thus reveals that the staged mask game of inferiority in real society pays off. Thus the contradictions between bourgeois virtues and real society are revealed. The "literary" Diderot or moi, who initially appears from a position of moral superiority, is increasingly embroiled in contradictions by Rameau's nephew.
What begins as a light-hearted chat, spiced with jokes and anecdotes, turns into an increasingly serious conversation. It ultimately leads to fundamental moral, artistic, and philosophical questions.
Rameau criticizes the cultural establishment, but at the same time shows himself to be dependent on it. Rameau's nephew is just a pulcinella of rich society, but considers himself a neglected genius.
With "Rameau's Nephew", Diderot reveals the soul of a failed artist: arrogant and immoderate in his passion, he is at the same time dependent on the favor of his patrons. The desperate scorn of society is countered by the subtle narrator of the self, a philosopher of the Enlightenment. The cynic's disillusioned view of the world is met by the philosopher's enlightened love of humanity. Diderot's thoughts can be seen in both figures. Diderot chose dialogue, as it were, as a form of design to play through philosophical thought processes and cultural-critical reflections.
option_4_text:
With much of the rest of the world at war, several bored British aristocrats live dissolute, hedonistic lives in a region of Kenya's Colony known as the Happy Valley, drinking, drugging and consenting to decadent sex to pass the time.
On 24 January 1941, Josslyn Hay, the Earl of Erroll, was found dead in his car in a remote location. The Count has a noble pedigree but a somewhat sordid past and a well-deserved reputation for having affairs with married women.
Diana Delves Broughton is one of those women. She is the beautiful wife of Sir John Henry Delves Broughton, known to most as "Jock", a man 30 years her senior. Diana has a prenuptial agreement with her husband that if either of them falls in love with someone else, the other will do nothing to prevent the romance.
Diana has succumbed to the charms of the rogue Earl of Erroll, whose other lovers also include the drug-addicted American heiress Alice de Janze and the somewhat more reserved Nina Soames. The Count is more serious in this matter than in any of his previous flirtations, and he wants Diana to marry him. She is reluctant to leave what she believes is the financial security of her marriage to formalize her relationship with Erroll (who has no funds or prospects), not knowing that Delves Broughton is heavily in debt. Humiliated in private but appearing to honor his agreement, Delves Broughton publicly toasts the couple's adventure at the Nairobi club, asking Erroll to bring Diana home at a set time. Delves Broughton appears to be extremely intoxicated for the rest of the evening; once he is alone it is clear that he was pretending to be drunk. After dropping off Diana, Erroll is shot dead in his car not far from the home of Delves Broughton who is soon accused of Errol's murder.
Diana is distressed by the loss of her lover, as is Alice, who openly masturbates next to his corpse in the morgue. The owner of a local plantation, Gilbert Colvile, whose only friend is Delves Broughton, calmly offers Diana advice and comfort and eventually surprises her by proposing marriage.
Delves Broughton is on trial. There are no witnesses to the crime and the physical evidence that seems incriminating is also circumstantial. He obviously had the motive and the means, but he is found innocent and the scandal comes to an end. De Janze is dying of a drug overdose, and Diana discovers more evidence implicating her husband in the death of her lover. After threatening her with a shotgun, Broughton shoots himself in front of her. The film ends with a Diana running away, stained with blood, discovering the rest of the Happy Valley scene partying around De Janze's grave.

query_text:
In 1983, near the Shadow Mountains, recovering alcoholic Red Miller lives a solitary life with his girlfriend, artist and author Mandy Bloom. He works as a logger, while she has a day job as a gas station cashier. In their cabin by a lake, Mandy creates elaborate fantasy art, which Red admires greatly.
On her way to work one day, Mandy walks past a van carrying the Children of the New Dawn, a religious cult led by Jeremiah Sand. Sand is struck by Mandy's beauty and orders one of his disciples, Brother Swan, to kidnap Mandy with the help of the Black Skulls, a cannibalistic, demonic biker gang who regularly use a highly potent form of LSD.
That night, Swan drives out to the lake and summons the Black Skulls by blowing a mystical ocarina known as the Horn of Abraxas. After Swan offers them a low-ranking member of the cult as a sacrifice, they break into the couple's home and subdue Mandy and Red. Afterwards, cultists Mother Marlene and Sister Lucy drug Mandy before presenting her to Sand. Sand, a failed musician, attempts to seduce Mandy with his psychedelic folk music, telling her that God had told him to take anything he wanted, but she instead laughs at Sand, infuriating him. In retaliation, he stabs Red, who is bound and gagged with barbed wire, before burning Mandy alive. After Sand and his followers leave, Red frees himself, mourns over Mandy's ashes, goes back inside, and falls asleep. After waking up from a nightmare, he consumes a bottle of vodka, tends to his wounds, and shrieks in agony, grief, and rage.
The next morning, Red fetches his crossbow from his friend Caruthers, who also provides him with freshly crafted bolts and information on the Black Skulls. Caruthers explains that the Black Skulls were former drug couriers who became sadomasochists after they consumed a bad batch of LSD. Before Red leaves, Caruthers warns him that his odds of survival are poor, but Red strives to hunt down the bikers after forging a battle axe. option_1_text: Russian trafficker and criminal Dirk Cross travels to Egypt where three archaeologists have unearthed an ancient Egyptian artifact of great value, the breastplate of Aaron. On the orders of ex-Nazi Colonel Speerman, Dirk kills the three and steals the breastplate, along with the two diamonds of equal value attached to it. Liz and Shepherd, now a private investigator, begin to investigate Isaac's disappearance to find out what Speerman and Dirk are up to. Somewhere near the Shadow Mountains in the year 1983, Red Miller lives with his girlfriend, artist Mandy Bloom, in a cabin near the lake. Red works as a lumberjack, while Mandy has a day job as a cashier at a nearby gas station in the woods. She creates elaborate fantasy art, and Red greatly admires her work. They lead quiet, solitary lives, and their conversations and behaviors point to a troubled past and psychological difficulties. Red appears to be a recovering alcoholic and a possible veteran, and Mandy relates traumatic experiences from her childhood.
On her way to work, Mandy passes a van carrying The Children of the New Dawn, a Manson-style hippie cult led by Jeremiah Sand. Sand is impressed by Mandy's beauty and orders one of his disciples, Brother Swan, to kidnap Mandy with the help of the Black Skulls, a demonic motorcycle gang with a taste for human flesh and a highly potent liquid form of LSD.
At night, Swan drives to the lake and summons the Black Skulls by sounding a mystical horn. After Swan offers them a low-ranking member of the cult as a sacrifice, they break into the couple's home and subdue Mandy and Red. The two female cult members, mother Marlene and sister Lucy, drug Mandy with LSD and giant black wasp venom before introducing her to Sand. Sand, a failed musician, tries to seduce Mandy with his psychedelic music, telling her that God had told him to take whatever he wanted. Mandy ridicules him, leaving him confused and enraged. Seeking revenge, Sand stabs Red, who is bound and gagged with barbed wire and then burns Mandy alive in front of him. After nothing but remains of Mandy's ashes, Sand and his followers leave. Red breaks free, mourns Mandy's ashes, walks back in and falls asleep, exhausted and in shock. After waking up from a nightmare, he consumes a bottle of vodka, tends to his wounds and screams in agony, pain and rage.
In the morning, Red searches for "the reaper", his crossbow, from his friend Caruthers. Caruthers provides him with newly created arrows and information about the Black Skulls. According to Caruthers, the Black Skulls were drug couriers who became dangerously sadomasochistic after consuming a bad batch of LSD. Before Red leaves, Caruthers warns him that his chances of survival are low. Red forges a battle axe and goes out in search of the bikers. Tracking down the gang, he attempts to run over a motorcyclist who is crawling, but is captured in the process. In his hiding place, Red manages to break free and kill the Black Skulls. While rummaging through his hiding place, he ingests some of his contaminated cocaine and LSD, causing him to experience instantaneous and severe hallucinations.
Searching for a radio tower he envisioned earlier, Red encounters The Chemist, a mysterious drug manufacturer, who tells him where to find The Children of the New Dawn. In his makeshift wooden church in a quarry, Red kills Brothers Swan and Hanker with his axe and kills Brother Klopek in a chainsaw duel, sparing only Sister Lucy's life. Crossing the tunnels under the church, Red finds Mother Marlene and beheads her. Then he finds Sand, mocking him as he pulls out Marlene's severed head. Sand pleads for clemency, but Red kills him by crushing his skull. He sets the church on fire and watches Sand's body burn before leaving, imagining Mandy in the passenger seat of his car, while the landscape behind him now seems fantastic and otherworldly.

After the United States enters World War I in 1917, the limousine carrying Daisy Heath (Margaret Sullavan), a sophisticated Broadway musical theatre star, knocks down Bill Pettigrew (James Stewart), a naive young soldier from Texas. A policeman orders the chauffeur to take Bill back to camp. During the ride, he becomes slightly acquainted with the cynical, but not cold-hearted Daisy.
Upon their arrival at the army camp, Bill lets his buddies assume that Daisy is the date he had lied about. In fact, he has no one. When they find out the truth, they decide to get even. On their next leave, they take Bill to Daisy's show, so he can introduce them. However, Daisy pretends that she is Bill's girl. As they spend more time together, she begins to warm to him, much to the increasing jealousy of her wealthy real boyfriend, Sam Bailey (Walter Pidgeon), who is financing Daisy's show.
When Sam takes Daisy out for an afternoon at his Connecticut estate for the first time, she tells him that Bill has shown her what true love looks like and made her realize she actually does love Sam. She also believes that the rivalry has also given new depth to Sam's love for her.
That same day, Bill learns that his unit is finally going to ship out for the fighting in Europe. When he cannot get a leave, he goes AWOL so he can propose marriage. Daisy opts to accept so that he can sail for France with something to look forward to. Sam objects to the odd arrangement privately to Daisy, but kindly refrains from telling Bill the truth. The two marry; then Bill has to leave immediately.
He sends her cheerful letters every day. Then, a letter comes from the War Department. As Daisy is in the middle of a performance, her maid Martha takes it to Sam, sitting in the audience. When Sam opens the letter, Bill's ID tag falls out. Daisy sees it, tears fill her eyes as she realizes that Bill has been killed, but she bravely finishes singing "Pack Up Your Troubles in Your Old Kit-Bag and Smile, Smile, Smile".

Barber Benjamin Barker is unjustly arrested, sentenced and forced into a life of hard labour in Australia by Judge Turpin, who covets his beautiful and virtuous wife Lucy.
Returning after 15 years on the run from the penal colony, Barker takes the name Sweeney Todd, bids farewell to his friend, the young sailor Anthony Hope, who rescued him when he was adrift, and returns to his old flat in Fleet Street above Mrs. Lovett's meat loaf shop. Following the discovery of the man's true identity, the woman tells him that, after his arrest, Turpin raped his wife, who decided to poison herself due to the humiliation suffered, to which Turpin kidnapped her daughter Johanna and became her guardian. Upon hearing this news, Todd matures his desire for revenge and as the beginning of the plan decides to reopen his old barber shop upstairs. Anthony, meanwhile, wanders the streets of London, and upon seeing Johanna at the window, instantly falls in love with her; his attraction causes a confrontation with Turpin and the Bamford Messo, who beats Anthony and threatens him with even greater violence if he returns.
Meanwhile, in the market square, Todd denounces an advertising fraud by Italian "street barber" Adolfo Pirelli and his young assistant Tobias "Toby" Ragg, claiming that the elixir they sell is just "a concoction of piss and ink". Todd challenges Pirelli, who is mortally offended by the insult received, to test his finesse in shaving in the shortest time. Bamford then comes as a witness to the challenge between the two rivals, which ends with Todd's victory; when the dealer congratulates the winner, the latter takes the opportunity to invite him to his shop for a free shave. When Mrs. Lovett and Todd return to Fleet Street, they see Pirelli arrive, who after revealing to Todd that he is not Italian but English and that he is his old assistant Davey Collins, tries to blackmail Todd by asking for half of his earnings, so that he does not reveal his true identity. Todd thinks back to those words, and in a fit of rage hits the Pirelli repeatedly in the head with a boiling teapot, then locks him in a trunk and, seeing that he is still alive, ends up brutally strangling him. Mrs. Lovett takes Toby, unaware of his master's murder, under her care and hires him as a waiter in her shop, which the boy reluctantly accepts.
When Judge Turpin is disappointed by Johanna's refusal of his advances, the Bamford messenger encourages him to visit Mr. Todd for a shave that would improve his appearance. Todd realizes that this is the perfect opportunity to kill Turpin and get revenge, but during the judge's shave, Anthony bursts inside the store accidentally revealing to Turpin Johanna's plan to run away with him. Enraged, Turpin leaves saying that he will not set foot in Todd's shop again until he meets people like Hope, and when he returns home he locks Johanna in an asylum until she agrees to marry him. Furious at not being able to complete his revenge, Todd takes out his frustration on his innocent customers who, at Mrs. Lovett's suggestion, can become delicious pies in his oven. Enthusiastically, Todd accepts her suggestion by installing a machine in his chair to dump the bodies of the victims through a hatch into Mrs. Lovett's oven room. Both Todd's barber shop and Mrs. Lovett's pastry shop receive much revenue in this way, and Lovett comes to express her desire to marry Todd; exactly a moment later, Anthony arrives and claims to have found Johanna. Hearing this, Todd advises him to disguise himself as an apprentice hairdresser and take Johanna away from the asylum; he then writes a letter informing Turpin of Anthony's plan to take Johanna away so as to lure the judge, and sends Toby to deliver her into the hands of the judge himself.
Toby returns and expresses his distrust of Todd to Mrs. Lovett, who, frightened by the idea of the boy running to tell the police of his suspicions, comforts him and lures him into the oven room by locking him inside. As Lovett warns Todd of Toby's suspicions, they are surprised by Bamford, sent to investigate the "strange smells" coming from the store's chimney. As Todd lures Bamford inside his shop, Toby (in the baking room) finds a human toe in a mess, and discovers a pile of human corpses just as the doorman's body falls down the slide; he flees through the sewers, hiding from Todd and Mrs. Lovett.
Meanwhile, Anthony and Johanna return to Todd's shop where the boy tells her to wait for him. Dressed in men's clothing, Johanna glances around the shop where she finds an image, unaware that it depicts her in her mother's arms. The moment a beggar enters the room looking for Bamford, Johanna quickly hides in a crate in the corner of the room. Shortly afterwards, Todd returns to the store and is surprised to see that the beggar seems to know him. Hearing that Turpin is about to enter, the barber in a state of panic cuts the beggar's throat and drops the body down the slide. Turpin bursts into the store a few seconds later and accepts the offer to have his beard shaved: waving his sharp razors over Turpin, Todd reveals his identity to the judge and stabs him in the neck repeatedly, before slashing his throat.
The barber then finds Johanna hidden in the trunk and, mistaking her for a man because of the clothes, offers her a shave to kill her. He is, however, interrupted by Mrs. Lovett's screams and heads for the baking room, leaving his daughter warning him to forget his face. Mrs. Lovett had cried because the judge, with his last remaining strength, had grabbed her skirt before she died; then recognizing the beggar's body as Lucy's, Mrs. Lovett tries to get rid of the corpse, but when she opens the oven door the light illuminates the woman's face and Todd recognizes her as the wife he thought was dead. Lovett then reveals that Lucy survived the suicide attempt but that the poison made her mad, so she tries to convince Todd that she lied out of love for him, saying that she was "just thinking about him". Todd calms her down and, incredibly, but with a look full of blind fury, begins to dance with her falsely declaring his love for her and for life, then suddenly throws her through the open oven door, staring motionless as the woman burns alive. With a broken heart, the barber then returns to Lucy, takes her in his arms in tears with the knowledge that he has lost her again and that he is responsible for her death and sings one last time; just at the end, Toby reemerges from the sewers, picks up one of Todd's razors from the ground (who despite noticing his presence decides not to react and lifts his neck), cuts his throat from behind and walks away from the macabre scene.

Lemuel Gulliver works as a delivery man for a major New York newspaper. Gulliver is in love with Darcy Silverman, editor-in-chief of the travel section, but he doesn't have the courage to come out and barely manages to talk to her. The arrival of the new assistant Dan, just twenty years old, whom Gulliver claims to give life lessons, highlights his inadequacy: in fact Dan, after only one day of work, is promoted to post office manager, becoming Gulliver's new superior and brutally telling him that he will never make a career and will never reach high summits.
Bitter and more distrustful than ever, Gulliver decides to go to Darcy to ask her out, but for the umpteenth time he gets stuck and, as an excuse, takes random papers from the desk as soon as the application to become a travel agent is submitted. Darcy is stunned and Gulliver lies, posing as a great traveler and writer; Darcy takes him at his word and asks him to bring her a piece the next morning. Not knowing how to get out of it, Gulliver writes an article scouring the Internet and tourist guides.
Increasingly amazed by Gulliver's unsuspected literary skills, Darcy entrusts him with a report on the Bermuda Triangle. Gulliver sets off for Bermuda and finds the local contact, who hands him a speedboat and gives him instructions to reach the appointed place. While sailing, Gulliver finds himself in the middle of a storm and is sucked into an "upside down" vortex, which rises to the sky instead of descending. Crushed by the hurricane, he loses consciousness and, upon awakening, finds himself lying on a beach and immobilized on the ground by numerous ropes.
The whirlwind took Gulliver to the land of Lilliput, ruled by King Theodore and populated by tiny human beings. Initially the Lilliputians, believing him to be a ferocious beast, lock him in a cave; here Gulliver befriends Horace, imprisoned for daring to court Princess Mary, the fiancée of General Edward. During an attack by the Blefuschian enemies, who set fire to the royal palace, Gulliver manages to save the king and princess by urinating on the fire and extinguishing it. From that moment on, he is considered a hero and is showered with honors.
Gulliver, however, lies to the Lilliputians, making them believe that he is a hero, that he has been president of the United States and showing them theatrical representations of famous films making them believe that he has been living these experiences (for example, Star Wars or Titanic).
Gulliver helps Horatio capture the princess, is treated like a hero, and the townspeople build him a huge mansion.
General Edward, however, does not see him in a good light, also because the latter is downgraded to vice general and replaced by Gulliver who then becomes general. Edward lowers all defenses and the Blefuschians begin to attack.
Gulliver enters the water and at first proposes to the enemies to disguise themselves, but then he realizes that he must do something: the bullets that reach his stomach bounce on it and hit the enemies, then he takes all the boats and throws them away.
At this point Gulliver's success is at its peak, everyone loves him and he hangs posters in the city that portray him: such as Gulliver himself with a device in his hand, reminiscent of today's iPads, called "G-pad", or a poster of him that refers to the movie Avatar ("Gavatar").
Although his boat has been found, Gulliver has no intention of leaving, especially since he received messages from Darcy, who had discovered that he had lied to her and told him not to return. Edward does not accept this and is also left by the princess who had been urged by Gulliver to confess her love for Horatio.
Edward, allied with the Blefuschians, after building a robot (thanks to instructions on a magazine found on Gulliver's boat) attacks Lilliput. Gulliver then surrenders and reveals his true identity, being exiled by Edward to the island to which the tiny inhabitants do not dare to go, and, at this point, it is he who finds himself to be tiny. A giant child kidnaps him and uses him as a doll, but Horatio saves him by calling him his best friend and telling him that no matter what job he does, he saved the princess and Lilliput, so he's a hero.
Meanwhile, Darcy, who had to go reluctantly to do the Bermuda Triangle story, finds herself in the same situation as Gulliver, in Lilliput (which has been occupied by the Blefuschians). Everyone calls her "Gulliver's princess" and locks her in the cave (where the king and queen are also imprisoned). Gulliver saves her, and in freeing her, he finally reveals his feelings for her.
Shortly afterwards, Gulliver challenges Edward's robot, thanks to Horace manages to defeat him and Lilliput gets rid of his enemy.
Gulliver also manages to quell the desire for war and violence between the two peoples, singing Edwin Starr's War.
Overcome with enthusiasm, Darcy and Gulliver kiss (as do Horace and the princess).
The two return to New York and, a year later, you see Gulliver working in the travel office just back from Papua New Guinea, going into Darcy's office and Dan coming in with the mail. Dan has a new employee who tells Gulliver he's "just a postal worker". Gulliver contradicts him: "There are no small roles, everyone is great! Remember, there are only little little people!"
The film ends with Darcy and Gulliver having lunch and the framing of an article hanging on the wall, in which it is noted that next to the name Darcy Silverman is written Gulliver, so it is evident that the two have married.

Todd discovers that Lovett knew Lucy was alive, and she tries to convince Sweeney that she cheated on him for his own good, confessing that she loves him and would make a better wife than Lucy ever was. But the love story provokes the maneuvers of minority leader Senator Bob Rumson, who discovers that 10 years earlier Sydney Ellen Wade during a protest march had burned the American flag and uses this fact to discredit her image.
The idyll reaches a breaking point when the scope of the environmental treaty is halved, for which Sydney fought with her staff to reach the quorum for Shepherd's re-election.
Rumson's increasingly heavy attacks and the abandonment of the woman he loves unleash the pride of the man who reacts on live television, bringing the decree back to the original draft and promoting the disarmament he had promised. May the 10th, 1916. British spy Edgar Brodie is dead, according to the press. In fact, he's assuming a different identity, as he's to be deployed as a secret agent in Switzerland. As Richard Ashenden, he's there to kill an unknown spy before he can deploy into enemy territory. This was necessary to safeguard British interests in a Middle East crisis. A colleague from Mexico, known as "the General", is to accompany Ashenden.
In his hotel room, Ashenden meets with the spy disguised as his wife Elsa, who is being visited by her admirer Marvin. Elsa is initially fire and flame for the assassination mission and thinks the whole thing is a great adventure.
When Ashenden and the General find one of their informants murdered in a church, a jacket button in the dead man's hand leads them to a clue. The agents identify the alleged owner of the button (an Englishman with a German wife). They're trying to lure him into a trap. To this end, the espionage-driven "couple" seeks to get acquainted with the already elderly English-German couple. In the meantime, Mrs. Ashenden frequents Marvin, but rejects his advances.
Meanwhile, Elsa has scruples about her assignment, as she becomes more and more convinced that even a political murder is morally reprehensible. Adding to her changed attitude is her burgeoning love for Edgar/Richard. "The General", on the other hand, is increasingly turning out to be a murderous driving force on behalf of the British government.
The elimination of the enemy by the General and Ashenden, whose sense of duty to his country compels him to act as the "ultimate" espionage mission, is now to be accomplished on a mountain hike. Eventually, Ashenden shuns direct involvement and leaves it to the "General" to throw the old man into the deep while Ashenden watches with a telescope.
Tragically, however, it turns out that the victim was merely a harmless tourist. Horrified by the senseless murder, Elsa and Ashenden decide to abort the mission.
However, a new clue shakes Ashenden's resolve again: through an acquaintance, the General has found out that a nearby chocolate factory is used by the German opponents as a conspiratorial cell. The two men spy on the scene, but then have to flee from the police. But they were able to find out that Marvin is the man they're looking for.
Believing that Elsa, who is really clinging to Marvin out of disappointment in her lover, would have also exposed him, they catch the train that Marvin wants to get off on at the last minute. Marvin reveals his identity to Elsa, but at the same time, he sees through her disguise. Ashenden and his Mexican colleague find the two and set out to liquidate Marvin. Elsa, however, foils the act at gunpoint, and responds to Ashenden's patriotic warnings with a reference to the primacy of their moral integrity.
At this very moment, the train is derailed by an air attack by British pilots. Marvin is mortally pinned, but just before he dies, he still manages to shoot the murderous "General". Elsa and Ashenden sink into each other's arms, free from the ultimately unbearable decisions of life and death. Back in England, they both quit the service.
option_0_text:
14th century, present-day Afghanistan: While the ambitious general Jalaluddin Khilji plans to seize the throne of Delhi and become sultan, his grandson Alauddin, far more ambitious and cruel than him, gets his daughter, Mehrunisa, as his wife. He then indulges his uncle's plans, allowing him to become sultan, and gains his trust by returning victorious from a battle against the Mongols; when the opportunity arises, however, he kills him with the help of the slave Malik Kafur, and becomes the new sultan of Delhi.
Meanwhile, in the kingdom of Singhal, the beautiful princess Padmavati accidentally wounds the king of Mewar Ratan Singh during a hunting trip. The man, who came there to look for some rare pearls to give to his wife Nagmati, falls in love with the girl during her convalescence and takes her as his second wife, taking her to the capital of his kingdom, Chittor, in Rajasthan. There he introduces her to the entire court, including the priest Raghav Chetan, who however dares to spy on the two in a moment of intimacy, coming for this outlaw. Eager for revenge, he travels to Alauddin's court and convinces him to besiege Chittor, telling him of the beauty of Padmavati.
The siege remains unsuccessful for 6 months, and finally Alauddin, increasingly obsessed with the desire to see the queen, proposes to Ratan Singh a peace agreement: he will withdraw the army in exchange for a meeting with Padmavati. However, the sultan is only allowed to glimpse the woman for a moment, reflected in a mirror: then, enraged, he takes the king hostage and brings him to Delhi, hoping that Padmavati will come to his rescue so he can see her.
At court, Alauddin is attacked by his nephew Itat Khan, but survives and kills the traitor. Meanwhile, Padmavati devises a ruse to deceive him and free Ratan Singh: first she demands and obtains the killing of the conspirator Raghav Chetan; then she goes to Delhi along with many soldiers disguised as women, and commanded by the brave Gora and Badal. She is unexpectedly helped by Mehrunisa, who frees the king and helps them escape, while Gora and Badal die covering their backs.
Alauddin, after imprisoning Mehrunisa, returns to Chittor determined to destroy everything and finally see Padmavati, whom he is increasingly obsessed with. He and Ratan Singh clash in a duel, and it is the sultan who gets the worst of it; but just as he is about to be killed, the king is shot in the back by Malik Kafur and dies reprimanding the enemy for his cowardice. Padmavati, now certain of defeat, makes the extreme decision: she will throw herself into the fire, committing suicide along with Nagmati and all the women of the city.
The enemy army enters Chittor: Alauddin, aware of what is about to be accomplished, runs forward in a desperate attempt to see the queen at least once. But the gate is shut in front of him just as he reaches a few steps from the bonfire; Padmavati immolates herself on the fire, and the sultan screams in madness in front of the closed door. The suicide of the queen and the women marked Chittor's greatest victory, and Alauddin's bitterest defeat.

Hans Hoffmann likes to perform homosexual acts in public toilets. Sometimes he masturbates with others, sometimes he has oral or anal intercourse. In 1968, Hans is sent to prison for 24 months, and it is not the first time that he is in prison for a violation of the then applicable § 175 StGB in Germany, which prohibits homosexual intercourse between men. Although he had been rescued from a concentration camp in 1945, he was thrown straight into prison. There he first met Viktor Bix, who made no secret of his abhorrence for Hans and his inclinations. And then Hans went to prison again in the 1950s after being caught with his great love.
Twenty years after his first acquaintance with Viktor, Hans must now help his former cellmate. He has become addicted to drugs during his long imprisonment, is about to have his third hearing, and hopes that perhaps he will finally be released.
option_2_text:
On 10 May 1916, during World War I, British Captain and novelist Edgar Brodie returns home on leave, only to discover his obituary in the newspaper. He is brought to a man identifying himself only as "R", who asks him to undertake a secret mission: to identify and eliminate a German agent on his way to Arabia to stir up trouble in the Middle East. Upon agreeing, Brodie is given a new identity—Richard Ashenden—a fake death, and the assistance of a killer known variously as "the Hairless Mexican" and "the General", though he is neither bald, Mexican, nor a general.
Brodie's late "predecessor" thought that the enemy agent was staying at the Hotel Excelsior in neutral Switzerland. When "Ashenden" arrives there, he is surprised to find that "R" has also provided him with an attractive wife, Elsa Carrington. Entering their suite, he also encounters her new admirer, fellow hotel guest Robert Marvin, who is only slightly deterred by the arrival of her husband (and continues to flirt with Elsa). When they are alone, Ashenden is displeased when Elsa reveals she insisted upon the assignment for the thrill of it.
Ashenden and the General go to contact a double agent, the church organist, only to find him dead. In his hand, however, they find a button, evidently torn off in the struggle with his killer. When they go to the casino to meet Elsa, the button is accidentally dropped onto a gambling table. Since it looks the same as his own buttons, an experienced mountaineer named Caypor assumes it is his.
The agents persuade Caypor to help them settle a concocted bet: which one of them can climb higher on a nearby mountain. As the moment approaches, Ashenden finds he is unable to commit cold-blooded murder, but the General has no such qualms and pushes the unsuspecting Caypor off a cliff.
However, a coded telegram informs them that Caypor is not their target. The General finds it very funny, but Elsa becomes terribly distraught when they are told. She decides to quit, despite having told Ashenden that she fell in love with him at first sight. In the lobby, she encounters Marvin. With no destination in mind, she persuades him to take her along with him. Meanwhile, the other two bribe a worker at a chocolate factory (the secret "German spy post office") to show them a very important message received the day before. They discover that it is addressed to none other than Marvin.
Ashenden and the General set out in pursuit, taking the same train as Marvin and Elsa. Before they can arrange anything, the train crosses the border into Turkey – enemy territory – and a large number of soldiers board. Despite this, they manage to get Marvin alone in his compartment. Objecting to cold-blooded murder, Elsa draws a pistol. Before Ashenden can do anything, one way or the other, the train is attacked and derailed by airplanes sent by "R". Marvin is pinned in the wreckage, but manages to shoot the General fatally before dying. The "Ashendens" quit the spy business.
option_3_text: This is Valparaiso. Ema, a young dancer, divorces Gastón, the director of the company for which she performs, unable to overcome the sense of guilt towards Polo, the child they had adopted to compensate for Gastón's sterility and who they then brought back to the orphanage following a tragedy caused by the child's pyromania.
option_4_text:
Bored writer Jean (Carl Parker) meets his old acquaintance Claire (Marilyn Roberts) and her attractive blonde friend Anne (Mary Mendum, also known as Rebecca Brooke) at a Parisian society party. Claire very quickly recognizes Jean's interest in her friend and invites him to accompany her on a walk in the rose gardens of the Château de Bagatelle. Jean quickly realizes that the two women have much more in common than a conventional friendship.
After Jean realizes in another chance meeting with Anne that she can be extremely assertive in a sales negotiation with a bookseller and also appears to him without Claire's presence absolutely resolute, he seeks the conversation with Claire. Claire subsequently demonstrates to him her relationship with her sub and makes it available to Jean. He accepts the gift, and in the days that follow, he becomes more and more absorbed in his new role as Annes Dom, exploring the limits of his new playmate.
In the days that follow, Jean leads Anne into new situations and discovers his own pleasure in the constellation that is completely new to him. Among other things, he introduces Anne to a fashion saleswoman, who subsequently seduces the two together. Other scenes include floggings, public displays, urophilia, and other sadomasochistic practices. The plot culminates in the ninth act in a scene in which Claire and Jean, in Claire's home, put Anne in chains together in a replica "Gothic dungeon" and play in a drastic scene. Claire suddenly goes after Jean and is supported by Anne; Jean flees. Anne then puts down her gag and says goodbye to Claire.
In the final act, there's a surprising twist. The previously dominant Claire visits Jean in his penthouse, dressed as Anne, and follows his instructions to undress; with the words "You can do with me whatever you want" she reveals herself as Switch. They love each other passionately.

query_text:
In German-occupied France, Lucile Angellier and her domineering mother-in-law Madame Angellier await news of her husband Gaston, who was serving in the French Army. While visiting tenants, Lucile and Madame Angellier escape an air raid by German Ju 87 stuka bombers. Following the French surrender, a regiment of German soldiers arrives, and promptly moves into the homes of the villagers.
Wehrmacht Oberleutnant Bruno von Falk is billeted at the Angelliers' household. Lucile tries to ignore Bruno but is charmed by his kind demeanor and his piano music. He gives her a piece of the sheet music. Lucile later learns that her husband Gaston's unit has been imprisoned at a German labor camp. Elsewhere, the farmer Benoit and his wife Madeleine chafe under the German officer Kurt Bonnet, who harasses Madeleine. Benoit, who was denied the chance to fight because of his leg wound, hides a rifle. As an act of resistance, he steals the German soldiers' clothes while they are bathing.
When Lucile discovers that one of her mother-in-law's tenants Celine is having sex with a German soldier, Celine reveals that Gaston has been having an extramarital affair and has fathered a girl named Simone. Angry with Madame Angellier for withholding her son's affair, Lucile allows herself to develop romantic feelings for Bruno. At Lucile's request, Bruno confronts Kurt over his harassment. Lucile's relationship with Bruno draws the hostility of many of the townfolk.
The Viscountess de Monfort later catches Benoit stealing a chicken from her coop. When Benoit points a gun at her, she tells her husband, the collaborationist Viscount de Monfort, who sends German soldiers after Benoit. While hiding in a barn, Benoit kills Kurt with his gun and flees into the forest.
The Germans launch a manhunt and give the townsfolk 48 hours to surrender Benoit. The German Major takes the Viscount hostage and threatens to execute him if Benoit is not found. At Madeleine's request, Lucile hides Benoit in the attic of the Angellier mansion with the help of the reluctant Madame Angellier. Despite a massive manhunt, the Germans fail to capture Benoit and the Viscount is executed by firing squad.
With the Germans planning to withdraw from the town, Lucile takes part in a plan to smuggle Benoit into Paris, where the French Resistance is gathering. She manages to convince Bruno to issue her a travel pass to Paris. However, Bruno's suspicious orderly suspects that Lucile is harboring Benoit and issues special instructions for the checkpoint guards to search her car.
At the checkpoint, Benoit manages to shoot the German soldiers dead with his pistol but is wounded in the shoulder. Bruno arrives on a motorcycle. Lucile faces him with her pistol but is unable to kill him. To Lucile's relief, Bruno helps her lift the wounded Benoit into the car and allows them to escape to Paris. As she drives away, Lucile smiles at Bruno in gratitude. Lucile and Benoit later join the French resistance and help drive out the Germans. While Lucile later learns that Bruno perished during the war, she treasures the memory of his musical score Suite Française.

option_1_text:
The story is set in the court of King Snofru, the founder of the Fourth Dynasty. It begins with the meeting of the civil servants in front of Snofru. He instructs his officials to look for a wise man among them who will please him with "lovely speech". Then Neferti, a high priest of the goddess Bastet, is brought before the king. He first asks Snofru if he wants to hear something from the past or something from the future. The ruler chooses the latter.
Neferti now reports of hard times ahead for Egypt: the Nile River drying up, foreigners settling in the north of the country, and the sun god Re turning away from humans. To this extent, these complaints are similar to those contained in the Ipuwer's exhortations. In contrast, however, Neferti brings about a positive change by announcing a savior who will restore order to the land. He is described as the son of a Nubian woman and is called Ameni, which is to be understood as a clear reference to Amenemhet I.

option_3_text:
During the German occupation of France in the early summer of 1940, many people fled Paris for the countryside. When a German regiment is stationed in Lucile Angellier's village, Officer Bruno von Falk takes refuge in the house of Lucile and her family. The uninvited visitor and occupier unexpectedly turns out to be a sophisticated guest with manners and musical interest. It is only through his piano playing that the unhappily married Lucile melts and understands the man behind the hated soldier. Thus, the initial enmity becomes a deep connection. From the occupiers, she hides the neighbor Benoît Labarie, who killed a German soldier out of anger. Bruno von Falk, her newfound love, is in charge of the search and rescue team. Although he suspects the hiding place, he lets the search party pass by. According to the statutes, the village head is to be executed.
When Lucile Angellier leaves with the car towards Paris, she is stopped at a road post, from the trunk Labarie shoots and kills the German soldiers. The arrival of Bruno von Falk helps to lift the wounded revolutionary back into the car and lets the two drive away.
option_4_text:
Defense attorney Richard Ramsay is working on the case of Mike Lassiter's alleged murder of his wealthy lawyer, Father Boone, a professional friend. Ramsay feels the pressure to save Mike, but Mike's complete silence makes the task difficult. Ramsay employed talented attorney Janelle Brady, the daughter of another professional friend, as a partner after leaving a career in corporate law.
The first witness, a flight attendant on a charter flight, claims to have witnessed father-son tension on a flight back from Stanford. In a flashback, Mike wants to go to Reed College, but Boone forces him to attend Stanford University. The officer who first responded to the call testifies that at the crime scene, Mike muttered "I should have done this a long time ago", and she and the lead detective claim that his fingerprints were found on the murder weapon.
The Lassiters' neighbors testify that Mike was very close to Boone but gradually drifted away over time and also report Boone's arrogant attitude toward his family and neighbors. Flashbacks show Boone's various affairs and his authoritarian and demeaning behavior toward his wife, Loretta, both in public and in private. Loretta testified that she was emotionally and physically abused for years, including on the day of her death. She testified that she went to take a shower after the fight and when she came back, she found his body. She's crying and she says that Mike confessed to her that he did it. Ramsay provides photographs of his mangled body, taken a day after Boone's death, as evidence of his cruelty.
Mike finally decides to speak up and asks to take a stand on Ramsay's objections. He corroborates his mother's and neighbors' version of his father's arrogance and cruelty, and suddenly admits that he killed his father, not to save his mother but to save himself because he was raped by his father. Mike says the abuse resumed on their flight back from Stanford and that he killed Boone when he tried again the day he died.
The prosecution calls the flight attendant, who first insists that nothing happened during the flight. When questioned by Janelle, the flight attendant admits to concealing her extramarital affair with the co-pilot and potentially spending too much time in the cockpit to confidently deny any unusual interaction between father and son. Janelle later becomes suspicious of Mike's story, meets Loretta outside the courtroom and gradually deduces that Mike is protecting Loretta. She confronts Ramsay, who says his duty is to save Mike, not to find the truth. She leaves in anger, causing Ramsay to worry about the jury's reaction to her absence, but she pursues the case.
Despite the lack of proper evidence of Boone's abuses, the jury acquits Mike. While waiting for his things in a private room, Mike confronts Ramsay, saying that he saw his mother secretly removing Ramsay's watch next to his father's corpse. Mike says he took the blame to save his mother, but he won't protect Ramsay. Ramsay denies any involvement and tells him that the case won't hold and that it will only damage Mike's credibility.
Mike doesn't believe him, but reluctantly lets him go for lack of evidence. As they all leave the courthouse, Ramsay remembers the real events. He and Loretta were having an affair. When Boone becomes suspicious of his wife's infidelity, Ramsay advises him to divorce her, but Boone insinuates that he will kill her if she leaves him. Loretta and Ramsay conspire to kill him and present the case as self-defense on Loretta's part, but Mike returns home early. Before they can organize the evidence, he confesses to the crime.

query_text: After defeating the pirate Victor Stagnetti in the previous film, Captain Edward Reynolds and his second-in-command Jules put together a new crew, which included the young pirate Olivia. Jules and the new arrival are first rivals, before entering into a lesbian relationship. Subsequently, Jules is captured by the Chinese pirate queen Xifeng, who enslaves her with a potion, then uses her to seduce and capture Edward. The latter is then forced to face a dragon, but is saved by Olivia. Stagnetti, returned from the dead, allies with Xifeng to sexually abuse Jules, and to confront Edward and Olivia who came to rescue their friend.
