Over a period of seven days, a young blogger who calls himself Michelangelo films 14 very different characters in a New York fashion house. These include the fashion designer Merlin, the model Lettuce Leaf, Minx (a supermodel), Edith Roth (the CEO and former owner of the fashion house), Tiny Diamonds (the financier/main shareholder of the fashion house), his bodyguard Jed, Anita de Los Angeles (a seamstress), Dwight Angel (an employee of the fashion house), Bradley White (the marketing consultant), Vijay Pizza (a bidder), Frank (a former war photographer), Mona Carvell (a critic) and Otto (the head of PR for the fashion house). To the interviewees, Michelangelo introduces himself as a student who needs the footage for a project at his school.
During the first show of Merlin's new collection, one of the models is killed. Detective Homer is taking over the investigation. I want him to find out if this is a murder case. While the accident is received with great concern by most of those interviewed, Tiny Diamonds and Otto soon see it as an opportunity to bring more attention to the show.
The performance must be repeated. However, there are further incidents, which is why the show has to be canceled several times and a total of five dates have been set until the end of the film. Not least because of the images Michelangelo posts on his website, there are increasing protests against the fashion show and the associated public relations. The final demonstration ends in disaster, with the protesters breaking into the building and another round of gunfire.
option_1_text:
In San Francisco in 1941, private investigators Sam Spade and Miles Archer meet prospective client Ruth Wonderly. She claims to be looking for her missing sister, who ran off from their home in New York and came to the city with a man named Floyd Thursby. Archer agrees to help get her sister back. However, later that night, the police inform Spade that Archer has been killed. Spade tries calling his client at her hotel to discover she has checked out. Back at his apartment, he is grilled by Police Detective Tom Polhaus and Lieutenant Dundy, who tell him that Thursby was murdered the same evening. Dundy suggests that Spade had the opportunity and motive to kill Thursby, who likely killed Archer.
Later that morning, Spade meets Wonderly, now calling herself Brigid O'Shaughnessy, who confesses that her story was made up. However, she convinces Spade to investigate the murders and also reveals that Thursby was her partner. He took advantage of her and probably killed Archer, but she claims to have no idea who killed Thursby. At his office, Spade meets Joel Cairo, who first offers him $5,000 to find a "black figure of a bird". When Spade is skeptical, Cairo pulls a gun on him and searches the room for it. Spade knocks Cairo out and goes through his belongings. When Cairo comes round, he hires Spade.
On his way to visit O'Shaughnessy later that evening, Spade is followed by a young man but manages to evade him. When he tells O'Shaughnessy about Cairo, her nervousness indicates she knows him. He arranges a meeting between the two at his apartment, where Cairo becomes agitated when O'Shaughnessy reveals that the "Fat Man" is in San Francisco. When Spade goes to Cairo's hotel in the morning, he spots Wilmer Cook, the young man who trailed him earlier. Wilmer works for Kasper Gutman, the "Fat Man". In his hotel suite, Gutman relates the history of the Maltese Falcon, then offers Spade his pick of $25,000 for the bird and another $25,000 after its sale, or a quarter of the proceeds from its sale.
Spade passes out because his drink is spiked. Wilmer and Cairo come in from another room and leave with Gutman. On coming round, Spade searches the suite and finds a newspaper with the arrival time of the freighter La Paloma circled. He goes to the dock, only to find the ship on fire. Later, the ship's captain Jacoby is shot several times and staggers into Spade's office before dying. The bundle he was clutching contains the Maltese Falcon. O'Shaughnessy calls the office, gives an address, then screams before the line goes dead.
Spade stashes the package at the bus terminal, then goes to the address, which turns out to be an empty lot. Spade returns home to discover O'Shaughnessy hiding in a doorway. He takes her inside and finds Gutman, Cairo, and Wilmer waiting for him, guns drawn. Gutman gives Spade $10,000 for the Falcon, but Spade tells them that part of his price is someone he can turn over to the police for the murders of Thursby and Captain Jacoby, suggesting Wilmer. After some intense negotiation, Gutman and Cairo agree and Wilmer is knocked out and disarmed.
Just after dawn, Spade calls his secretary, Effie Perine, to bring him the bundle. However, when Gutman inspects the statuette, he finds it is a fake and Wilmer escapes during the tumult. Recovering his composure, Gutman invites Cairo to return with him to Istanbul to continue their quest. After they leave, Spade calls the police and tells them where to pick up the pair. Spade then angrily confronts O'Shaughnessy, telling her he knows she killed Archer to implicate Thursby, her unwanted accomplice. She confesses, but begs Spade not to turn her over to the police. Despite his feelings for her, Spade gives O'Shaughnessy up, then submits the statuette as evidence, describing it as "the stuff that dreams are made of".
option_2_text: The young singer Gretl has a love for classical music, but finds it out of fashion in post-war Vienna where more Jazzy tunes are popular. She meets the composer Franz who has similar views to her, and is consequently out-of-work. She manages to get them jobs in a bar playing modern music, despite their distaste for it. Gretl becomes concerned when she believes Franz has fallen for American singer Gloria, and his turn towards the sort of modern music she plays threatens his hopes of a commission for a classical ballet work.
option_3_text:
Captain Edward Reynolds boasts of his victory over the feared pirate Victor Stagnetti to his faithful companion Jules; he has even assembled a new crew for his vessel, including Ai Chow and Olivia, Serena's cousin. Olivia informs the crew that the governor of Jamaica has ordered Serena's arrest and Olivia is on board to protect the crew from the enemies, and to convince Edward and Jules to apologize to Serena. When they finally arrive in Jamaica, they ask Governor Lyttelton to pardon Serena, however, he is more interested in Jules' beauty than anything else. They convince the governor to find another hidden treasure on the condition that they go on a mission first in order to defeat another group of pirates.
Olivia and Jules have a difficult beginning of friendship, but eventually end up in a lesbian experience. Later, Edward meets Takvor, the Armenian gold pirate, during a slave auction and is invited to participate in an orgy with dancers and slaves.
Meanwhile, Jules is captured by a Chinese pirate, Empress Xifeng, and given a potion that gives her control over Jules' body and mind. Xifeng uses Jules to seduce and capture Edward. He is then forced to fight a giant, monstrous creature, but Olivia saves him at the last minute.
Meanwhile, Victor Stagnetti is reborn from the sea. He and Xifeng are engaged in a threesome with his new slave, Jules. Edward and Olivia struggle against a series of living skeletons. Olivia boarded the enemy ship and fought Xifeng in a sword duel until she got him to back off. She is then forced to fight off a poisoned Jules until Stagnetti intervenes and manages to control them. Once again, Edward comes to the rescue, claiming his title as "the greatest pirate hunter who ever lived".
option_4_text: Casey, an American living in Cologne, Germany, works with his friend Matthias for a drug dealer, Geran, as money runners. He meets Juliette, another American, one night while she tends bar at one of Geran's hangouts. Though interested in him, Juliette turns him down when he asks her out, stating that she wants nothing to do with someone who runs in Geran's circles, but to look her up when he gets out. Inspired by the conversation, Casey quits his job with Geran, asks Juliette out, and the two quickly begin dating and move in together. All is well for the pair until Juliette suddenly has a seizure one evening and is rushed to the hospital. Told that her kidney is failing, and because she is not a citizen of Germany that she is unqualified for the transplant treatment, Casey proposes that they move back to America for her treatment. In order to obtain the money for the operation and save Juliette, Casey goes back to work for Geran in order to pull off a large drug theft from Germany's biggest drug dealer, Hagen Kahl.

query_text:
922: Ibn Fadlān travels north as a representative of the Caliph of Baghdad to contact the king of Saqaliba.
But before he arrives, he encounters the mighty warrior Buliwyf in a Viking village and witnesses the traditional burial of a deceased leader.
One day, a young messenger from King Rothgar comes to report that the land is being overrun by monsters. These monsters come with the fog and eat people.
A fortune teller announces that only thirteen warriors will be able to defeat the evil that comes with the fog. But the thirteenth warrior must not be a Viking. The warriors are chosen after the 12 moons, among them Buliwyf. Ibn Fadlān is reluctantly appointed the 13th warrior and travels with the twelve warriors to Scandinavia until they arrive in the kingdom of Rothgar. Soon, the thirteen warriors are faced with an uncanny superiority.
option_0_text:
Young mother Ilda raises her son in the harsh, sometimes snow-covered and sometimes heat-dried vast landscape of Trás-os-Montes. She tells him traditional stories, like bedtime stories. During the day, he moves about in the countryside, playing and doing little chores, with other children, with his little sister, or on his own. They play by streams or on old stone bridges, roam the surrounding villages, and observe nature and adults at work, such as farming or tending livestock. They also experience magical or historical scenes from local legends and fairy tales.
A father has to leave his daughter alone at home and sets off on his donkey to run errands. A young widow walks to school with her son. A river fisherman teaches his son his trade. Children read letters from their immigrant fathers to their illiterate mothers. Along a very vague plot line, the central characters interact in everyday scenes: children at play, adults at home and at work, family life in the house, residents in modern clothes and in traditional costumes reciting old verses, playing music or conversing. The scenes take place in the wilderness, the alleys of the simple villages or in the rustic homes, connected and separated by sensual images of the landscape and the people in it. Small everyday gestures and conversations, often seen through the eyes of children, give the viewer access to this world and give things a deeper meaning. Without a concrete arc of tension, the film follows the characters through a piece of their lives.
option_1_text:
'Keep crazy and behave like normal people.'
Veronika, a 24-year-old Slovenian girl, is not happy with her life: although she does not have financial problems and does not suffer from love, she simply wants to leave this life because of the monotony of everyday life. So, having swallowed a whole handful of sleeping pills, he abandons himself to his fate.
She wakes up in the private clinic for the mentally ill Villete, in Slovenia, where she learns from the doctors that following her suicide attempt her heart has been severely damaged and will only last a few more days. Veronika initially hopes that it will all be over quickly, but in that clinic it seems that time never passes. There you will meet many people, Zedka, Mari, Eduard, people who are not afraid to say what they think, because in the end they know that they are considered "crazy". With them he will establish a special relationship of sincerity, experiencing sensations that he had never known before and discovering the most secret and hidden sides of his self.
option_2_text: Two years after the murder of Count Dracula, history tells of his resurrection. To bring him back to life, three thrill-seeking nobles want to use the blood collected at the scene of death, but the three men during the ritual back off and kill their ceremonial master, Lord Courtley, Dracula's servant. Dracula's revenge (already awakened) involves the three men and their children. One of them will oppose it.
option_3_text:
The thief's trade is based on an invulnerable code: fulfill the order and cover the partner, but never cooperate with the police.
Gabriel Martin (Antonio Banderas) is a thief who has had very little luck in life. His situation changes when he accidentally meets Keith Ripley (Morgan Freeman), an old-school thief, who chooses him as a partner for his next big heist: the theft of some very valuable Faberge eggs. Ripley needs to pull off this heist to settle his debts with a powerful Russian mob boss (Rade Serbedzija). However, everything is complicated by the meddling of Alex (Radha Mitchell), Ripley's beautiful goddaughter, and Weber (Robert Forster), the police lieutenant.
option_4_text:
The novel is set in the 10th century. The Caliph of Baghdad, Al-Muqtadir, sends his ambassador, Ahmad ibn Fadlan, on a mission to assist the king of the Volga Bulgars. Ahmad ibn Fadlan never arrives, as he is conscripted by a group of Vikings, led by their chieftain Buliwyf, to take part in a hero's quest to the north; he is taken along as the 13th member of their group to comply with a soothsayer's requirement for success. They travel to Hurot Hall, the home of King Hrothgar, to defend it from the 'mist-monsters', or 'wendol', a tribe of vicious savages (suggested by the narrator to have been possibly relict Neanderthals) who go to battle wearing bearskins. After two devastating battles, Ibn Fadlan and the remaining Northmen decide to attack the Wendol village, which is located in a network of sea caves. They infiltrate the sea caves, assassinate the head of the Wendol tribe, and return to Hurot Hall. Buliwyf, however, is mortally wounded in the attempt. At Hurot, they encounter the Wendol in battle for a final time, defeating them. Ibn Fadlan is then allowed to continue on his journey.
Eaters of the Dead is narrated as a scientific commentary on an old manuscript. The narrator describes the story as a composite of extant commentaries and translations of the original storyteller's manuscript. The narration makes several references to a possible change or mistranslation of the original story by later copiers. The story is told by several different voices: the editor/narrator, the translators of the script, and the original author, Ahmad ibn Fadlan, who also relates stories told by others. A sense of authenticity is supported by occasional explanatory footnotes with references to a mixture of factual and fictitious sources.

query_text: Les (Corey Haim) is a boy who fails his driver's license exam and decides to deceive everyone by saying that he has passed so he can drive his grandfather's brand-new Cadillac and thus conquer the girl of his dreams, Mercedes Lane (Heather Graham).
option_0_text: On the California-Mexico border in the 1950s, illusionist Myra Shumway is about to marry a senator and uranium tycoon. An unwitting witness to a murder, the woman flees, followed by Ross, a journalist with post-war trauma and the senator's man. During her escape she meets Doc, a mischievous doctor who introduces her to the secrets of the shamans. By the time he's back at the altar, the cards will have been shuffled.
option_1_text: Les Anderson is a 16-year-old teenager who dreams of getting his driver's license so he can impress the beautiful Mercedes. Running the contest with his sister, he gets a large number of wrong answers, but in exasperation, he taps his computer, causing the other computers in the contest to stop. The results are unknown, he passes the driving test brilliantly, thus obtaining his license. But the results are discovered and Les loses the famous sesame for driving. His father punished him for two weeks after he tricked his family into believing he had a driver's license. Bypassing the punishment, Les decides to borrow his father's Cadillac and go on a road trip with Mercedes. But things don't always go as planned.
option_2_text:
# Meeting, parting and reuniting
Gabriel Oak is a young shepherd. With the savings of a frugal life, and a loan, he has leased and stocked a farm. He falls in love with a newcomer eight years his junior, Bathsheba Everdene, a proud beauty who arrives to live with her aunt. Over time, Bathsheba and Gabriel grow to like each other well enough, and Bathsheba even saves his life once. However, when he makes her an unadorned offer of marriage, she refuses; she values her independence too much and him too little. After a few days, she moves to Weatherbury, a village some miles off.
When next they meet, their circumstances have changed drastically. An inexperienced new sheepdog has driven Gabriel's flock over a cliff, ruining him. After selling off everything of value, he manages to settle all his debts but emerges penniless. He seeks employment at a hiring fair in the town of Casterbridge. When he finds none, he heads to another such fair in Shottsford, a town about ten miles from Weatherbury. On his way, he happens to take note of a conflagrating fire on a farm, and leads the bystanders in putting it out. When the veiled owner comes to thank him, he asks if she needs a shepherd. She uncovers her face and reveals herself to be none other than Bathsheba. She has recently inherited her uncle's estate and is now wealthy. Though somewhat uncomfortable, she employs him.
# Bathsheba's valentine to Boldwood
Meanwhile, Bathsheba gains a new admirer. William Boldwood is a prosperous farmer of about 40, whose ardour Bathsheba unwittingly awakens when she playfully sends him a valentine sealed with red wax on which she has embossed the words "Marry me". Boldwood, not realising the valentine was a jest, becomes obsessed with her and soon proposes marriage assuming she wanted the same. Although she does not love him, she toys with the idea of accepting his offer; he is the most eligible bachelor in the district. However, she avoids giving him a definite answer. When Gabriel rebukes her for her thoughtlessness regarding Boldwood, she dismisses him from his job.
When Bathsheba's sheep begin dying from bloat, she discovers to her chagrin that Gabriel is the only man who knows how to cure them. Her pride delays the inevitable, but finally she is forced to beg him for help. Afterward, she offers him back his job, and their friendship is restored.
# Sergeant Troy
At this point, the dashing Sergeant Francis "Frank" Troy returns to his native Weatherbury and by chance encounters Bathsheba one night. Her initial dislike turns to infatuation after he excites her with a private display of swordsmanship. Gabriel observes Bathsheba's interest in the young soldier and tries to discourage it, telling her she would be better off marrying Boldwood. Boldwood becomes aggressive towards Troy, and Bathsheba goes to Bath to prevent Troy returning to Weatherbury, as she fears what might happen if Troy encountered Boldwood. On their return, Boldwood offers his rival a large bribe to give up Bathsheba. Troy pretends to consider the offer, then scornfully announces they are already married. Boldwood withdraws, humiliated, and vows revenge.
Bathsheba soon discovers that her new husband is an improvident gambler with little interest in farming. Worse, she begins to suspect he does not love her. In fact, Troy's heart belongs to her former servant, Fanny Robin. Before meeting Bathsheba, Troy had promised to marry Fanny; on the wedding day, however, the luckless girl went to the wrong church. She explained her mistake, but Troy, humiliated at being left at the altar, angrily called off the wedding. When they parted, unbeknownst to Troy, Fanny was pregnant with his child.
# Fanny Robin
Some months later, Troy and Bathsheba encounter Fanny on the road, destitute, as she painfully makes her way toward the Casterbridge workhouse. Troy sends his wife onward, then gives Fanny all the money in his pocket, telling her he will give her more in a few days. Fanny uses up the last of her strength to reach her destination. A few hours later, she dies in childbirth, along with the baby. Mother and child are then placed in a coffin and sent home to Weatherbury for interment. Gabriel, who knows of Troy's relationship with Fanny, tries to conceal the child's existence – but Bathsheba agrees that the coffin can be left in her house overnight, from her sense of duty towards a former servant. Her servant and confidante, Liddy, repeats the rumour that Fanny had a child; when all the servants are in bed, Bathsheba unscrews the lid and sees the two bodies inside.
Troy then comes home from Casterbridge, where he had gone to keep his appointment with Fanny. Seeing the reason for her failure to meet him, he gently kisses the corpse and tells the anguished Bathsheba, "This woman is more to me, dead as she is, than ever you were, or are, or can be". The next day he spends all his money on a marble tombstone with the inscription: "Erected by Francis Troy in beloved memory of Fanny Robin ..." Then, loathing himself and unable to bear Bathsheba's company, he leaves. After a long walk, he bathes in the sea, leaving his clothes on the beach. A strong current carries him away, but he is rescued by a rowing boat.  He does not return home, however.
# Troy returns
A year later, with Troy presumed drowned, Boldwood renews his suit. Burdened with guilt over the pain she has caused him, Bathsheba reluctantly consents to marry him in six years, long enough to have Troy declared dead.  Boldwood begins counting the days.
Troy tires of his hand-to-mouth existence as a travelling actor and considers reclaiming his position and wife. He returns to Weatherbury on Christmas Eve and goes to Boldwood's house, where a party is under way. He orders Bathsheba to come with him; when she shrinks back in shock and dismay, he seizes her arm, and she screams. At this, Boldwood shoots Troy dead and tries unsuccessfully to turn the double-barrelled gun on himself. Although Boldwood is convicted of murder and sentenced to be hanged, his friends petition the Home Secretary for mercy, claiming insanity. This is granted, and Boldwood's sentence is commuted to "confinement during Her Majesty's pleasure". Bathsheba buries her husband in the same grave as Fanny Robin and their child.
# Gabriel triumphant
Throughout her tribulations, Bathsheba comes to rely increasingly on her oldest and, as she admits to herself, only real friend, Gabriel. When he gives notice that he is leaving her employ, she realises how important he has become to her well-being. That night, she goes alone to visit him in his cottage, to find out why he is deserting her. Pressed, he reluctantly reveals that it is because people have been gossiping that he wants to marry her. She exclaims that it is "... too absurd – too soon – to think of, by far!" He bitterly agrees that it is absurd, but when she corrects him, saying that it is only "too soon", he is emboldened to ask once again for her hand in marriage. She accepts, and the two are quietly married.
option_3_text:
It was 1847, California. The revolutionary general Don Esteban stops a carriage and arrests two passengers: Marcel, an entomologist, and Patricio, who is on his way to the governor's palace to pose as a butler. Patricio can convince the rebel leader to let him go.
Soon after, Don Esteban enters the palace and orders the shooting of the governor and his men; once again Patricio, now acting as a butler, is successful with his intervention, as he achieves that the sentences are to be executed only the next morning. That morning, only Count Martinez is led to execution, but is saved at the last moment by Zorro. The general gives the order to execute the governor instead of him, but he too is saved by Zorro, who intervenes again.
Since the general suspects that behind Zorro's mask is the butler Patricio, he has him captured, but again Zorro intervenes and frees Patricio. Under Zorro's leadership, the people take up arms and are able to defeat the rebels in the palace; Don Esteban is killed. Zorro takes off his mask, and Patricio appears. When he was captured, Marcel assumed his role to deceive the rebels.
option_4_text:
One of the highlights of the American Independence Day celebrations in the American fishing town of Southport, North Carolina, is the election of the fish queen, the Croaker Queen. In front of her watching friends Julie, Barry and Ray, high school graduate Helen has beaten her five competitors. In the evening, the two couples celebrate by driving along a coastal road. On this one, a young man was seen in the foreground sitting on a cliff holding a rotatable medallion in his hands. In a moment of recklessness, Ray, sitting behind the wheel, runs over something. On the side of the road, the friends find the body of a man with blood on his face. In their panic, the youths decide to cover up the accident and throw the apparently lifeless body into the nearby sea. In the process, Helen's crown, thought to be dead, is swept away from the beauty pageant. As Barry leaps back to rescue her, he sees the man opening his eyes. Instead of using this as an opportunity to help the injured person, the youths vow to forget the terrible incident and never speak of it again. The medallion stays on the bank.
A year later, the friends have largely disappeared from view. Julie returns home from college for the summer holidays, where she finds a letter. The content is just one sentence: "I know what you did last summer". She then reconnects with her former best friend Helen, who is also struggling to cope with last year's accident. Together, they track down Barry, who believes a joke and suspects one of Julie's friends, Max, of sending the letter. Max was distracted by Julie and Ray the night before a year ago when he drove by their car shortly after the accident. After being tracked down and threatened by Barry, unsuspecting Max is killed by a stranger in an oil jacket with a hand hook. Barry gets hit and injured by the same man. The other three are visiting him at the hospital.
Julie, who knows that two weeks after the accident a David Egan was recovered dead from a crab net, researches with Helen in a newspaper archive that on the Fourth of July two years ago Susie Willis, the fiancée of the deceased, drowned in his car after he drove it over a cliff. The two go to see Egan's sister Missy, who says that a friend of her brother's named Billy Blue has sent her condolences. In the evening, a figure in an oil cloak enters Helen's house and overhears a conversation between her and her sister. The next morning, on the Fourth of July, Helen finds herself with her hair cut and "SOON" written on her mirror, while Julie discovers Max's body in her trunk, which has disappeared when she brings Barry and Helen in. Ray arrives, and Julie decides to take the college yearbook back to Missy's to have the alleged alias Billy Blue identified from the photos of her. When Julie wants to reveal the accident to her, she speaks of her brother's suicide and shows a farewell letter "I WILL NEVER FORGET LAST SUMMER", which Julie interprets as a death threat. There is an argument because Missy insists that her brother drowned and that neither the tattoo that Julie saw, nor Susie had any tattoo at all. Julie realizes that she was mistaken in the identity of the accident victim. She returns again to the newspaper archives, where in an article by the fishermen Benjamin Willis is named as Susie's father. Now she suspects that she and her friends hit him on the country road last year shortly after he killed David Egan to avenge his daughter.
Despite the events, it is traditional for Helen, last year's winner, to participate in the election of the new Croaker Queen. Barry's watching from an emporium. Helen watches as someone in an oil coat appears behind Barry and knocks him down with his hook. Desperate, Helen tries in vain to get up through the crowd. When a policeman subsequently examines the empores, these blood traces are overlooked. As he tries to drive Helen home, a broken-down vehicle blocks their way in an alley. The figure in the oil coat kills the outgoing cop. Helen manages to escape from the police car and into her sister's store. However, the killer has already entered through the unlocked back door and kills Helen's sister Elsa. Helen initially manages to escape, but is placed in an alley a few meters from the busy street by the man and, despite fierce resistance, is also killed.
Julie hurries to the harbor and finds Ray, who became a fisherman after last summer, on his boat. It's coming out of her that she now believes that a year ago, someone other than herself and David Egan was on the street, namely Ben Willis, who first murdered Egan and then was run over by them, but not killed. Ray invites Julie onto his boat, but then she sees the boat's name is Billy Blue. Julie runs away, Ray chases after her, a fisherman knocks Ray to the ground and calls for Julie to flee to his boat. There she sees a wall with pictures of herself and her friends. The fisherman puts the medallion on it, indicating the accident. Julie realizes that she has Ben Willis in front of her and the ship is already at sea. She escapes below deck while Ray takes a motorboat to Willis's ship. In the ice cream parlor, Julie comes across the bodies of Barry and Helen. When Willis tries to hook up with Julie after a fight with Ray, his hand gets caught in a rope from the rigging. Ray releases the safety of the winches, causing Willis to be pulled up and his hand to be torn off the block of the bottle cap; Willis plunges into the sea. Ray explains to Julie that he went to see Missy out of guilt.
A year later, Julie's back at the university, on the phone with Ray. In the communal bathroom, she receives a letter addressed to her. When she opens it, she finds an invitation to a party. As Julie tries to get into the shower, she notices a message on the shower door: "I STILL KNOW". Through the door, a dark figure in an oil cloak leaps toward her, and all you hear is a scream.

query_text:
In the late 1950's, during the German economic miracle, the events of World War II were slowly being forgotten.
When the journalist Thomas Gnielka wants to denounce in the court of the city of Frankfurt am Main a former guard of the Auschwitz extermination camp, whom his acquaintance Simon Kirsch has seen as a teacher in a schoolyard, this is met with widespread rejection. However, the young prosecutor Johann Radmann deals with the case and begins with the investigation with the assistance of Attorney General Fritz Bauer.
Radmann is looking for perpetrators and witnesses who can testify to the crimes in the concentration camp. In the apartment of the painter Kirsch, Radmann and Gnielka find a list of SS men who killed prisoners in the concentration camp. He and his associates can find the listed perpetrators in telephone directories throughout the Federal Republic.
Further documentation can be obtained from the American Document Center in Frankfurt.
Despite the persistent resistance of the authorities, Radmann was able to arrest the first perpetrators, including the adjutant of the camp commandant Rudolf Höss, Robert Mulka, and the last camp commandant of Auschwitz, Richard Baer. His efforts to apprehend the SS doctor Josef Mengele, however, fail.
The difficulties Radmann encounters in his investigations get on his nerves; he begins to drink. The relationship with his girlfriend Marlene fails. He argues with his mother about his father's role during the Nazi era. He throws himself at his comrade Gnielka and resigns his post. However, when he is asked to work in his new position with the lawyer who had previously cynically approved the selection on the ramp during the interrogation of a client by Radmann, he returns to the prosecutor's office.
His efforts have borne fruit: in 1963 the first Auschwitz trial begins. To begin, Fritz Bauer sends his prosecutors on their way: "History will be written today".
option_0_text:
In 1958, Johann Radmann is a young and idealistic public prosecutor who takes an interest in the case of Charles Schulz, a former Auschwitz extermination camp commander who is now teaching at a school in Frankfurt am Main. Radmann is determined to bring Schulz to justice, but finds his efforts frustrated because of the many former Nazis who are serving in government and looking out for one another.
Radmann's boss, the prosecutor-general Fritz Bauer, puts him in charge of investigating former workers at the Auschwitz camp. The U.S. occupation forces give him access to their files, and he discovers there were 8,000 workers. He goes after Josef Mengele, who lives in Argentina, but flies back to West Germany to visit his family. After the authorities block Radmann's attempt to issue an arrest warrant, his boss warns him off and orders him to concentrate on lower-profile suspects. The department invites Mossad agents to visit, and shares its information with them. As a result, Adolf Eichmann is kidnapped and spirited away to Israel where he is tried, convicted and executed for his crimes. Having pulled off this coup, Israel declines to pursue Mengele.
Meanwhile, Radmann allows himself to be seduced by Marlene, a seamstress who, benefiting from Radmann's connections, starts a business as a dress designer. Radmann reaches a crisis when he discovers his own father was in the Nazi party. When he tells Marlene that her father too was in the party, she ends their relationship. By the end of the film, however, there is a chance she will have him back. He resigns his official post and goes to work for an industrialist. There he is again confronted with the dilemma: do what is right; or do what the system requires you to do?
When he finds this means working with a colleague who had defended a former Nazi he was investigating, Radmann walks out. His idealism has suffered from hard encounters with the real world; at every turn, the "system" wants compliance, but he wants justice. He comes to understand that the only thing that can ease the horror is not justice, but attention to the lives and stories of those who suffered. Growing out of the simplistic right/wrong moralizing, he comes to understand life as more complex, and seeks to repair all the damage, large and small, he inflicted in his zeal.
After going to Auschwitz to say kaddish, the Jewish mourning prayer, for a friend's two daughters who were killed there, he goes back to work for the West German state prosecutor. The film ends with the opening of the trial of several hundred former Auschwitz perpetrators.
option_1_text:
Opera singer Tamara is heavily addicted to cocaine. Her manager Mangol, who also acts as their coke supplier, goes in and out of her house and uses it as his drug transshipment point. Due to her addiction, Tamara has now lost both her husband and her daughter, who is growing up with her ex-husband. In order to spare his daughters' greater suffering, Mangol tells them both that their mother had died. When her daughter sits in the audience for one evening, she becomes a great admirer of Tamara's singing skills.
For Mangol, the young girl is nothing more than another potential customer whom he wants to make addicted to cocaine, but Tamara is on guard, and won't let it happen. Tamara decides to snatch her daughter from the dirty hands of the dealer and put her back in the safe hands of her ex-husband. Tamara sees no hope and commits an act of desperation. She snatches her daughter while Mangol is strangled by one of his junkie customers with bare hands.
option_2_text:
Clonus is an isolated desert compound, where clones are bred to be used as spare parts for the elite, including a future president-elect Jeff Knight. The clones are kept isolated from the real world by the workers of the colony, but are promised that they will be accepted to move to America after completing some kind of physical training. After a group of clones are selected to go to America, a farewell party is held with their fellow clones. The selected clones are then taken to a laboratory where they are sedated and placed in an airtight plastic bag and their bodies are frozen to preserve their organs for harvest.
The clone Richard begins to question the circumstances of his existence and eventually flees the colony. Chased by the guards, Richard enters a nearby town. The clone is found by a retired journalist, Jake Noble, who takes it to his sponsor Richard Knight, who appears to be Jeff Knight's brother. The two argue over what to do with the clone, which turns out to be a copy that Jeff had secretly created for himself.
After a fight, Richard's clone returns to the colony to reunite with his beloved, Lena. The clone discovers that Lena has been lobotomized by those who run the colony. Once they have him in custody, they kill him and freeze him. Meanwhile, Clonus completes his cover-up by hiring thugs to kill Richard Knight, his son, and the Nobles. Jeff Knight is stabbed in the chest in the ensuing fight with his brother, but appears to be fine the next day at a press conference, where he is stunned to discover that Noble, before his death, had managed to release a secret tape to the media, exposing Project Clonus. The final frame shows Richard's frozen corpse with his chest open and a tear coming out of his eye.
option_3_text:
In the background the struggle against progress advancing under the guise of the steam locomotive. Dawson, a stagecoach line owner, wants to stop the Tomahawk and Western Railroad's flaming new locomotive from reaching its destination.
And to do that, he hires a gunfighter named Dakota. Carrying the car to Dead Horse Point with mules and men is the job of the sheriff's young daughter, Kit. They're part of the Dakota caravan, Madame Adelaide and her girls.
Along the way, the group is joined by Johnny, a cowboy friendly to the Indians and able to enlist their help, with whom Kit naturally falls in love. Dakota tries by all means to thwart the arrival of the locomotive at Tomahawk on the day set by the company, but all her efforts are in vain.
Faced by Johnny, he plunges into a canyon. And the whole caravan under Kit's leadership makes its entrance into the city on the appointed day. Progress has won, and the railroad will cross America's prairies.
option_4_text: Young director Nick Chapman thinks his career is launched after the award he receives for a short film, but discovers that Hollywood is not so easy to reach.

query_text:
Concerned about protecting his family from outside calamities and attacks, a young Canadian man remotely follows the directions of an expert until he goes on a survival course of his own.
Reaching a remote and secret area in the snowy forests far from the cities, Antoine finally meets Alain and five other followers, some neophytes like him, others with similar experiences behind their backs.
Abandoned their cell phones and all other contact with the outside world, the students are instructed on how to survive in extreme conditions and specifically how to fight armored in this shelter that Alain has already fully equipped to withstand external attacks of all kinds.
Things go well until the exercise with explosives, at the end of which, as a result of imprudence, François is killed by the device he was packing. The incident divides the group. After the shock, in fact, the students would like to call the police, although it would be objectively difficult to justify how much was being held, being completely without any authorization. Alain, in fact, who built that complex with his own hands, is opposed, backed by David, to inform any outside person of what happened. With the idea of sleeping on it at night, the group dissolves with unresolved friction. A little later, however, Alain sets fire to François's body. The group realizes this and rebels, deciding to leave. Alain shoots Anna, who is seriously wounded in the leg, while the others flee into the woods.
During the escape, Sebastien is killed by a trap, and when, despite many difficulties, Rachel and Antoine manage to reach the cars, left far from the shelter, David catches up with them, shooting and killing the man. But Rachel, a former soldier skilled in combat, manages to engage the enemy in hand-to-hand combat and kill him.
Rachel then decides to challenge Alain in his own home, where she ran in vain to save Anna who meanwhile died of exsanguination. After a very close duel, the woman, although injured, manages to stun and immobilize her "evil master" and then drive a snowmobile to the rescue.
option_0_text: Anticipating a disaster, Antoine, a family man, attends a survivalist training given by Alain (Réal Bossé) in his self-contained lair. Fearing a natural, economic or social crisis, the group trains to deal with the various possible apocalyptic scenarios. But the catastrophe they will experience will not be the one they anticipated.
option_1_text: Today is the last day of his life. Satché is certain of this, even though he is in perfect health, and he is ready to accept his impending death. As he walks through the streets of his hometown in Senegal, he encounters places and people from his past as if he were seeing them for the first time: his parents' home, his first love, his childhood friends, his wife and children. Once again he hears the same reproach: why didn't he stay in America, where he could have had a future?
option_2_text:
# Presentation
A young girl is courted by a famous pianist. During one of their first outings together, a singer shot the pianist twice in the back. At her trial, she did not reveal the reason for her act, but something indicates that the murderer and the victim had known each other for a long time and that only tragic events could have led to this outcome.
During the hearing behind closed doors, the woman tells her story, dramatic, terrible and protective...
# Summary
Lisa is a girl of about 17 who lives with her mother, Mrs. Koslov. Although she was to be away for three days, she urged her daughter to stay focused on her piano lessons. She takes advantage of this freedom to get some rest with a friend and go for a drink. There, a handsome man they had noticed slipped them two invitations to a musical performance the next evening.
While they are sitting on the balcony of the opera house, a boy comes to them with a message; the man they have met is the artist performing on stage, Michael Michailow, and he wishes to meet Lisa after the performance.
Rejecting his advances at first, she agrees to see him again and in order to remain discreet about their relationship find themselves in a dance where the audience is less upscale and where the pianist's notoriety will go unnoticed. But as Michael kisses Lisa, the singer recognizes him and collapses. Embarrassed and evidently with a troubled conscience, he hurriedly took Lisa by the arm and told her to leave the premises quickly. As they make their way to the grand staircase, a sniper's act takes place on the stage; in the middle of the fireworks, two shots sound; the singer - Vera - shouts his name Michael Michailow and shoots him in the back.
We're going to trial. Lisa is heard as a witness but is unaware of the connection between the two people, Vera and Michael. His mother's in the audience, too.
To the president of the court who wants to know the reasons for her action, Vera says nothing. Suddenly, the clerk brings in a recently discovered suitcase that may contain clues. Threatening to open it, Vera requests a closed-door hearing to explain her action. His request is granted; another story is about to begin...
Vera had met Michael in 1912, by which time she was a singer and played pieces composed by him. She was married to Leonid and had a child. Michael made advances to her over and over again, but she always refused. But one night, after a show, Michael gets her drunk and abuses her. In the meantime, World War I broke out, and Leonidas went to war.
When he returns, the very night of the adultery, he's missing an arm. Vera wants to tell him the truth, but she doesn't have the strength.
Michael keeps writing to her, but Vera doesn't write back. One night, after another intercepted e-mail, she decides to go and find Michael to explain that she no longer wants anything to do with him. When she leaves her apartment, Leonid, who had followed her, understands everything. He leaves his wife, takes custody of the child and disappears from the scene.
Since then, Vera has lived in poverty and has only found work as a cabaret singer and in sleazy clubs. She found out that Leonid changed his name to Mr. Koslov. She's been looking for him for years. One day she finds his address and goes there.
While looking for Mr. Koslov, she bumps into his wife, who tells her that Mr. Koslov has been dead for three years. But in the moment Vera can observe her daughter, who has grown up. In fact, to the lady who tells him that she lives alone with her daughter, she replies: "Your daughter?" Mrs. Koslov understands that Vera is the biological mother of the child in the room, but begs her to please keep this secret that would ruin her future life. Vera understood, and with tears in her eyes, she walked away, satisfied that at least she had seen what her daughter looked like now.
Back at the scene of the trial, the girl Michael was kissing was his daughter, and she wanted to protect her from this pimp. So to avenge the wrong she had done and to protect Lisa, her daughter, Vera shot the man who had ruined her life and was about to do the same to a new victim.
The President of the Tribunal understands the feelings of Vera who wants this story to remain secret but in order for a judgment to be rendered he must reveal it to the members of the jury. When the judge delivers his verdict, the sentence is lenient.
But when the President speaks, Vera trembles with all her being - will her secret be revealed to the general public and to her daughter in the room? Weighing his every word, the President simply states that Vera's gesture was that of a person whose life had been shattered by Michael...
Vera leaves the court to be taken to prison. In the hallway, Lisa approaches her and wishes her good courage. Mother and daughter are face to face. Eager to take her daughter in her arms, but not making any gesture, Vera stares at her and walks between two guards to her condemnation.
option_3_text: Vince and Cesar are two often-unemployed boxers who happen to have a great opportunity: $50,000 each if they can get to Las Vegas as quickly as possible for the sideline match of a world title match. This is Húsavík, Iceland, 1974. During the live broadcast of the Eurovision Song Contest, little Lars Ericksson and Sigrit Ericksdóttir are captured by ABBA's performance and begin dancing during Waterloo. Lars, annoyed by the amused reactions of the two families, silences everyone by promising that one day he will win Eurovision.
Nowadays Lars and Sigrit, who have always remained best friends, play together in a duo called Fire Saga, despite Erick, Lars' long-time widowed father, strongly disapproving of his son's desire to pursue a musical career. Lars' ambition has remained the same since he was a child, but at the country bar where they perform the only song the audience wants to hear is the nonsense song "Ja Ja Ding Dong". Nor is Helga, Sigrit's mother, convinced of their partnership, telling her daughter that Lars is limiting her potential and that with him she will never be able to sing the "Speorg note", which can only be sung when you are yourself in the purest way.
At the Icelandic public broadcaster RÚV, the selection committee is reviewing candidates for the Söngvakeppnin, the national competition that will choose the country's representative to the next Eurovision Song Contest, and they are confident that they have found Katiana Lindsdóttir a big favourite who could even win the European competition for Iceland. Since there is still one contestant missing for the final, a final proposal is drawn up without even listening to the song, and it just so happens that the Fire Saga are chosen. When Lars receives the news, he is so thrilled that he climbs onto the bell tower of the village church and rings the bells, and ends up being arrested for setting off a false alarm. Lars tells the cops that the village is close to death and that Fire Saga's participation in the contest is the only chance he has to stay alive, and thanks to Sigrit's intervention he is released. Sigrit, who believes in ancient Icelandic traditions, asks the elves to help them participate in Eurovision, in the hope that if Fire Saga were to win, Lars would reciprocate the romantic feelings she has for him.
Arriving in Reykjavík, the duo performs at Söngvakeppnin but technical problems undermine the performance of their song "Double Trouble". Lars, heartbroken, refuses to attend the boat party reserved for the finalists and sits on the dock while Sigrit tries to console him. Suddenly the boat explodes killing all the occupants, leaving the Fire Saga as the only remaining participants. The selection committee, despite always mocking them, is forced to name them winners of their own accord and then send them to represent Iceland at Eurovision. The Fire Saga then arrives in Edinburgh, home of the event. There, Lars rejects Sigrit's attempts to kiss him, repeating that they must devote themselves to the race and not to their relationship. During rehearsals, problems arise with the new remix of their song and with Lars' elaborate stage designs, and the two make the acquaintance of Alexander Lemtov, the representative of Russia and one of the main favorites for victory.
Alexander invites them to a party at his villa, attended by many of the actual contestants from past Eurovision contests, and introduces them to several of their challengers including Greek contestant Mita Xenakis. After a "Sing Together" among all present, Alexander and Sigrit spend the night together as well as Lars and Mita, although neither couple ends up in intimacy. At the next rehearsal, Sigrit and Lars have a heated argument after Sigrit has vented her hatred towards her new costume and the new remix by asking to restore the original versions, and the two accuse each other of dating the night before. Later, back at the hotel, Lars secretly hears Sigrit writing a new song, and becomes convinced that it is a love song for Alexander and that the two have begun a romantic relationship.
It's time for the semi-final and, after Lars has satisfied Sigrit's demands and the two have cleared up, the performance of "Double Trouble" begins in the best of ways, but is then ruined by an accident: Sigrit's scarf becomes entangled in a spinning hamster wheel, part of the set design, which rolls down from the stage into the audience-occupied area, dragging them along. The two recover and conclude the performance, but the audience responds with an awkward silence and a few scattered laughs. Believing that Fire Saga has now become the laughingstock of the competition, they leave the stage, not realizing that shortly afterwards the audience erupted in great applause for the perseverance they showed in wanting to finish the song. Lars, infuriated, prepares to return to Iceland immediately, but Sigrit begs him to stay to witness the results of the race. Upon her refusal, after telling her to go and sing her love song to Alexander, Sigrit reveals to him that she wrote it for him. Lars is however too disappointed by his failure, and as he returns to Iceland alone to start working together with his father, he is unaware that at Eurovision their performance begins to receive points on points until they qualify against all odds to the final.
Becoming a fisherman, Lars confesses his love for Sigrit to his father, who reveals to him that after losing his wife he has always been in love with Helga who has never returned him, and convinces him to go back and fight for her, telling him for the first time to be proud of him for how he did not give up after the accident during the song. After learning that Iceland has qualified for the final, Lars jumps off the boat to return to Edinburgh. Meanwhile, Alexander asks Sigrit to stay with him to start an artistic collaboration, which she refuses. Sigrit realizes that Alexander is actually gay but can't come out because of homophobia in his country. Lars receives a pass from Victor Karlosson, governor of the Central Bank of Iceland and a member of the national Eurovision committee, who attempts to kill him after revealing to him that he was the one who caused the competitors' boat to explode, fearing that if Iceland won Eurovision the country could go bankrupt due to the enormous costs of hosting the event the following year. Lars is rescued by hidden elves who kill Victor with a knife thrown in his back, allowing him to return to Scotland for the final. As Lars hurries to reach the arena with the help of a group of American tourists, the broadcast has begun and Sigrit appears on stage alone to perform the song. Lars bursts into the scene and interrupts her, telling her to drop their official proposal and sing the song she had written for him, "Húsavík", which is also an ode to their hometown. Lars begins to play it on the piano and Sigrit sings it, concluding with a Speorg note, which moves the audience and the inhabitants of Húsavík. Realizing they are in love with each other, Lars and Sigrit kiss on stage to a standing ovation from the audience. Behind the scenes Alexander is also happy for them and accepts Mita's invitation to go to Greece with her to find his happiness.
Fire Saga is disqualified from the competition for altering their song, but both Lars and Sigrit lost interest in winning as they realized that their relationship was the most important thing. On their return to Húsavík, the two are greeted by a cheering crowd upon their arrival. Some time later, Fire Saga returned to play in the village bar for the wedding of Lars's father and Sigrit's mother. With their baby in their arms, they ask if anyone wants to hear their Eurovision song, but the audience again asks to play "Ja Ja Ding Dong".

Alexandre Beck and his wife Margot go to Lake Charmaine to celebrate the anniversary of their first kiss, inscribing the 19th notch in a heart carved from the bark of a tree. Night falls and the two take a bath, reaching a large raft. After a brief argument, Margot dives and reaches the dock, disappearing and shouting: Alex rushes to her aid, but once he reaches the ladder he is hit by two shots that knock him out of the fight.
Eight years later, Dr. Beck, a pediatrician at a Paris clinic, receives an anonymous e-mail on the eve of his 27th birthday requesting an appointment. For the man, now a widower, the hope of seeing his wife alive again is restored. On the date, a woman lets herself be filmed by a public camera and appears to be Margot herself.
Investigations into the woman's death had recently been reopened following the discovery of the bodies of two men buried near the scene of the crime. She's losing faith in the initial hypothesis, which attributed the murder to a serial killer, but the investigators, while returning to the husband, are basically on the high seas.
Events accelerate when a mysterious gang, also on Margot's trail, murders her best friend, Charlotte, after a futile interrogation, putting Alex in trouble, on whom all suspicion falls. This one, to go to the date given to him by e-mail by the person he hopes to be his wife, escapes arrest then, hunted by the police, relies on the protection of Bruno, a criminal whose son he had treated. Margot, actually alive, sees her husband being followed and renounces the meeting. Alex catches sight of her, chases her, but gets caught. Bruno's providential intervention saves the man, but now the wife, warned of the danger, is determined to disappear again.
The action of his lawyer, the tenacity of the skilled inspector Levkowitch and the affection of his friend Hélène allow Alex to put together the pieces of the complicated mosaic, at least as far as it is possible to get. The full involvement of Jacques Laurentin's father-in-law is a certainty so, with a microphone on and police protection, Alex goes to the key figure in this mysterious affair and, in effect, gets his confession.
Laurentin relates that Margot, having discovered that the son of the powerful Neville was abusing some minors, was beaten by them to keep silent. Called to her rescue, unbeknownst to her husband and everyone else, Laurentin, in an excess of defense of his daughter, killed the boy with his rifle and then hid the body. Neville soon became aware of Margot's responsibility for her son's death, and so he decided to seek justice by hiring two assassins who Laurentin then paid off so they wouldn't kill her. The man was then forced to eliminate the two assassins, as well as to procure a disfigured corpse to pass it off as that of his daughter, in whose recognition he was called himself. He then made his daughter run away, making her believe that her husband was dead, all to save her life. Laurentin also reveals Neville's other misdeeds including the murder of Alex's own father.
Alex delivers Laurentin's written memoir to the police, just as he commits suicide. The case is closed, but while Alex is returning to the shores of Lake Charmaine where he will find his Margot, we discover that, earlier, by evading the police hearing, Laurentin had revealed to the son-in-law that the young Neville, in fact, had been killed by his own daughter.

The king of somewhere is worried, the cupboards are empty, there's no money. The only solution proposed by his advisers Schnorr and Astropolex, to marry his daughter to the king of Persipanien, failed: his daughter refused the marriage and the king wanted to marry only a rich woman.

Cesar works as a doorman in an apartment building in Barcelona. He is a sociopath, and since his youth has never been able to experience any form of happiness; therefore, the only satisfaction he feels in life is to make those around him unhappy in every possible way. He thus spends his days studying with great cunning the tenants of the palace, whose lives he knows in detail, inflicting on them every form of anguish, and not sparing even the elderly invalid mother (to whom, taking advantage of her situation, he regularly confides all his criminal actions).
Cesar's favorite victim is Clara, a very sunny, sweet and optimistic girl, traits that make her the person Cesar hates more than anyone else.
Obsessed with the desire to destroy her happiness, Cesar decides to push himself to the extreme limit in order to "make her smile disappear". As a doorman, he has a copy of the keys to each apartment, and he uses them to break into the girl's house, hiding under her bed, drugging her into sleep with chloroform and then roaming freely in her apartment, sleeping next to her. The man's obsession and hatred for Clara also prompt him to send her numerous anonymous messages and letters, inject acid into the containers of her cosmetics (causing her numerous skin rashes) to infest her house with cockroaches, from which the girl is terrified. Following this latest action by Cesar, Clara, still unaware of Cesar's actions, asks him for help to disinfect the apartment. Cesar offers to take care of it, but Clara informs the doorman that, since the house is uninhabitable, she will be away for a few days.
Cesar doesn't take well to the news of Clara's departure, now that he'd managed to make her unhappy. Meanwhile, he himself is tormented by Ursula, a girl who lives in the apartment next to Clara's: the girl has discovered his criminal actions and blackmails him for money and pornographic films in exchange for silence.
A few days later Clara notifies the doorman that in the evening she will return to the now comfortable dwelling and Cesar, once again under the bed, prepares to resume his duties. This time the man is determined to go even further, having brought with him a bag containing, among other things, ropes, a butcher's knife and a saw. But unexpectedly, the girl is joined by her boyfriend, Marcos, and the two have sex, during which the doorman's chloroform flask hidden under the bed also opens, causing a few drops of the liquid to fall on his face. The doorman still manages to get out from under the bed without being seen, but, once he reaches the front door, he realizes that he cannot get out, having accidentally taken the keys to the apartment of another tenant of the building from the purse left under the bed. Unable to return, he hides in the shower, where he loses consciousness due to chloroform spilled all over his face and does not return until the next morning, when Clara, without moving the curtain, opens the shower water and soaks him. However, the girl does not immediately enter the shower, but returns to the bedroom, thus giving Cesar a chance to escape. The escape is unsuccessful and Cesar is discovered by Marcos: cornered, the doorman justifies himself to Clara, saying that he had just entered to retrieve the bag he had forgotten after the disinfestation work. His words, however, do not convince Marcos, who begins to suspect Cesar.
Shortly afterwards Cesar discovers that the police are on his trail because of the anonymous messages and letters he had sent to Clara. However, she manages to deflect suspicion and frame the cleaning woman's son, who is arrested along with his mother. A few days later Clara decides to spend a weekend away with Marcos, and in the meantime, due to the often late work behavior, Cesar is fired by the administrator and asked to leave the concierge within fifteen days.
From her small, dark apartment, she meditates on suicide (a premeditated act, moreover, very often, throughout her unhappy existence), going to the terrace of the building: looking from below, however, she sees Clara returning unexpectedly in advance from her vacation with her fiancé. The two are arguing heatedly; this is enough to discourage Cesar from taking his own life. He immediately goes under Clara's bed, where he discovers the reason for the disagreement between the two fiancés: Clara has discovered that she is four weeks pregnant. Marcos, who has been away for the past six years, and who is also sure that he has always taken his precautions, is convinced that he is not the father of the child and suspects the infidelity of the girl, causing his anger and triggering a furious quarrel.
One day, while Clara is not at home, Marcos, to expose Cesar, lets him into the apartment with an excuse: the boy has in fact found the tools with which Cesar tortured Clara under the bed. A scuffle ensues, in which the doorman confesses to Marcos that he had sex with the unconscious woman. When Marcos, blinded by rage, attacks him again, Cesar grabs a broken piece of mirror and strikes him in the neck, mortally wounding him. Then he moves the body into the bathtub, placing the murder weapon in the victim's own hand to fake a suicide. Since Ursula knows what she has done, Cesar one night drugges all her family, then threatens to kill the child and people close to her if she will talk to anyone and will not support his thesis to the police, for which Marcos would have killed himself due to alleged quarrels with the fiancée.
Marcos' death upsets Clara's life, who decides to move out and never return to the apartment. Seeing her emerge from the palace elevator for the last time, pale and with tears in her eyes, Cesar realizes with satisfaction that his goal has been achieved.
A few months later, Cesar decides to take the final step of his delirium: although he knows that he will face the consequences of his act, he writes a full confession to Clara, who in the meantime has recovered from grief and has given birth to the child he believes to be Marcos' son. After reading Cesar's letter, she not only discovers that she was repeatedly raped by him during the night, but that the newborn child is actually Cesar's son. The woman remains shocked, while Cesar, finally happy, waits for justice to be served.

Lee Jung-soo (Ha Jung-woo) is driving home for his daughter's birthday. While driving through a tunnel through a mountain, the tunnel collapses. When Lee Jung-Soo regains consciousness, he finds himself trapped inside his car, which is buried under tons of concrete and debris. South Korea is horrified by the news of the collapse of a large tunnel. The government urgently sets up an accident task force. In 1989, John Shaft, his wife Maya Babanikos, and their infant son JJ are the victims of an attack. Although Shaft manages to repel the attackers, there is a rift between him and Maya. She takes their son and raises him alone. The only contact is through questionable birthday gifts.
Twenty-five years later, J.J. Shaft graduated from M.I.T. and went to work for the FBI as a data analyst. When his best friend Karim, a former PTSD junkie who had just started a self-help group with friends called Brothers Watching Brothers, died of an overdose, he noticed irregularities.
