JJ gets his job back, but turns it down to work with his father and grandfather as a private investigator.
option_2_text:
Spoiled heiress Ellie Andrews escapes from her father's yacht in Miami to New York to marry aviator King Westley, disapproved of by her apprehensive parent, who considers him nothing more than an ambitious social climber. In order not to be found by the men unleashed in her search, the girl chooses to travel in a Greyhound coach, a way that does not suit her privileged life and that forces her to see the effects of the Great Depression up close. On the same bus travels the journalist Pietro Warne, just left without a job for his unreliable behavior, who recognizes her and decides to accompany and help her in exchange for an exclusive scoop.
The intimacy to which the uncomfortable journey forces them, during which they must pass for husband and wife and sleep in the same motel room (but with the "walls of Jericho", a blanket on a tightened rope, to divide them), and the sharing of the most diverse experiences, both negative (losing the bus, hitchhiking, suffering from hunger) and positive (the charm of life on the road, for Ellie who has always felt locked in a golden cage), makes them gradually approach and get to know each other, until, when the trip is now about to end, Ellie realizes that she is in love with Peter and confesses it to him. But the fact that he doesn't seem to reciprocate and then vanishes into thin air forces Ellie to call her father, who has finally decided to accept her daughter's marriage to Westley, as long as she returns home.
Peter, returning to her after getting some money and no longer finding her where he had left her, thinks he has been exploited and deceived. The unfortunate misunderstanding could be decisive if it were not for the intervention of Ellie's father who, once he met Peter and having recognized his honesty (he does not ask for the lavish reward promised by his father to find his daughter, but only a reimbursement of expenses) and the sincere affection for his daughter, urges her not to ruin her life with a wrong marriage and to let her feelings prevail. Ellie is convinced only at the last moment and abandons Westley just at the moment of the "yes", to reach Peter and bring down the "walls of Jericho" together.
option_3_text: Daniel Mantovani, a Nobel Prize for Literature laureate who has lived in Europe for decades, accepts an invitation from his hometown in Argentina to receive an award. There, he will find both similarities and irreconcilable differences with his own people.
option_4_text:
Dr. William MacLure (Edmund Gwenn) a Scottish doctor, adopts Lassie, who has an unnatural aversion to water. The Dr. tries to cure Lassie of her fears, but she remains water-shy.
Young Tammas Milton needs an operation. The doctor wants to use chloroform but the locals in the Glen are against this new idea. The doctor proves its worth by using it to put Lassie to sleep for over twenty minutes. After operating in his own house to save the young man's life, the elderly doctor in payment has extracted a promise from his father, a friend who was the previous owner of Lassie, that he will allow him to send the young man on a four-year medical course in Edinburgh so he can take over from him one day as doctor in the Glen.
The young man when recovered is sent away and the increasingly old doctor continues administering to his patients in the area, who begin to fear for his health. One snowy night the doctor is called out and sees a patient. On the way home, he dozes off on his horse and a tree branch knocks him down into the snow. Lassie rushes across a damaged bridge over a flood swollen river to get help and when she returns with two men, the bridge has been washed away.
With MacLure's life in danger, the dog is forced to dive into a raging river to get to the other side. After almost being pulled under by a whirlpool twice, Lassie makes the other side on her second attempt and seeing this, the two men wade across the waist deep flooded river. They find MacLure who is still unconscious in the snow and very cold and get him home. He eventually comes to and spends some days in bed but it has been too much for him and he dies. Shortly after his funeral, attended by all in the Glen, the new doctor arrives, having passed his exams, and takes over the practice.

query_text: Flore and Gino, two small Italian swindlers, arrive in Albania hoping to profit from the relative chaos that followed the fall of Communism. They want to acquire a shoe factory. But the government refuses to sell it to them unless they associate with an Albanian.
option_0_text:
The tribulations of a donkey in the Pyrenees in the 1960s, a pretext for painting human vices.
The early years of Balthazar the donkey are happy, in the company of Marie (Anne Wiazemsky), a little girl from the Basque Country, and Jacques (Walter Green), his vacation companion in Paris. Later, problems arise between the parents of the two children and everyone suffers, including the donkey that Mary abandons. A baker buys Balthazar to carry the bread delivered by Gérard (François Lafarge), a young thug who has no trouble seducing Marie. Balthazar is abused by Gerard, then by Arnold (Jean-Claude Guilbert), a drifter suspected of a murder in which Gerard and his gang may have been involved. The donkey escapes and takes refuge in a circus where he is trained. Back with Arnold, the abuse continued until the death of this inveterate alcoholic. Returning to Mary, his sufferings are confused with those of Mary, who disappears. Picked up by Gerard who uses him for smuggling, he is wounded in an exchange of gunfire, escapes and dies in the mountains, surrounded by a flock of sheep.
option_1_text:
The businessman Fiore and the young assistant Luigi arrive in Albania in their pick-up. Fiore is the creator of a scam, that is, to simulate an economic initiative by exploiting the Italian laws on entrepreneurship abroad, in order to pocket large state contributions. Fiore is the head of the delegation, and seeing the humanitarian catastrophe in which the country finds itself, he sharply criticizes the policy that has reduced it to this, while the Albanian official accompanying them tries to justify the miserable state in which his country finds itself.
At the end of the one-way trip, the two are introduced to a woman who is supposed to make a name for the factory property. But Fiore discovers that this woman, who was specifically requested as "no relatives", is actually close to the official. Then Fiore loses patience and asks to have an Albanian without relatives who can somehow benefit from his appointment. She asks to visit a nursing home, and here she finds a man fit for the role of society's leading man. So they pull him out of the hospice and take him with them.
Matters become complicated when the elderly "president" flees from the Mother Teresa Sisters' facility where he had been taken, forcing Louis to pursue him. The old man, arriving in a small town by train, is attacked by street children, who even steal his shoes and almost suffocate him. Luigi eventually finds him in a hospital, where he is admitted, and, despite being barely able to walk, takes him away. But a terrible doubt arose: the doctor said that the old man was not Albanian, but Italian, because he spoke Italian and said his name was Talarico Michele. Luigi reiterates that he has an Albanian passport, but the doctor tells the unknown Luigi that after World War II the Italians who remained in Albania were persecuted and shot, so many changed identities.
Little by little, what the man has been hiding for decades comes to light: his name is Michele, and he is a Sicilian, who was sent decades earlier to fight in Albania, leaving the same day his son was born. Michele is convinced that his child is now 4 years old, that there is still a family waiting for him at home, and that he himself is still 20 years old. He even thinks he's in Abruzzo. Louis treats him badly, annoyed by his rantings.
The recovery has just succeeded, when things get even more complicated: while the footwear company is discovered by the Albanian anti-fraud authorities, Luigi stops to look for food and a bathroom, tells a policeman to keep away the children who swarm everywhere, but when he returns he finds his vehicle without the wheels. At that point, the Italian is stuck, and he starts swearing at the crowd, mute.
The old man, meanwhile, gets on a bus, and Luigi follows him. The bus is stopped on a bridge by a police checkpoint. Luigi makes room with the old man, making himself recognized as Italian. Then they get on a truck headed for Tirana. There Luigi is targeted by the questions of the boys who are in turn heading to the capital to board and escape to Italy. One of them gets sick and dies in the indifference of the others, too busy with the journey to go to Italy to create a new life.
Eventually the two arrive in the capital and there, in a telephone exchange, Luigi discovers that the scam has been discovered: the old man is no longer president and he himself no longer has a job. Luigi, increasingly impressed by Michele's selflessness and naivety, begins to support him. He tries to set him up in a restaurant, giving money to the manager, then returns to the hotel, but finds the police waiting for him: without knowing the reason, he is locked in a dark and dirty cell with other men.
When questioned, he is told that the arrest was a result of the discovery of the fraud, but also that the police are actually interested in sending the corrupt official to prison. He is suggested to leave Albania, but his passport is not returned, because officially Luigi should stay in the country until the trial.
So Luigi comes up with an extreme solution: he takes a ship full of migrants, and there he also finds Michele, who is convinced that he is heading for America. Luigi gives up all reasoning: he remains there, among hundreds of Albanians traveling to the promised land, Italy.
option_2_text: Tan and Jane spend a well-watered evening with friends and then they go home. Jane is driving down a deserted country road when out of nowhere a young girl appears in the middle of the lane. The accident is inevitable. The couple leave the lifeless body there and run away. Since then remorse and guilt haunt them and they witness strange phenomena. Tan, a professional photographer, notices apparitions in his photographs and suffers from acute neck pain. With the help of his friend Jane, he tries to understand what is happening to them and torments them.
option_3_text:
Mike Kendall, an ex-cop, lives alone in a town in Utah in a beautiful house with a white picket fence that he flattened after a hard night's sleep in his muscle car. He's half-heartedly looking for work, but all he seems to be doing is drinking and fooling around with his brother-in-law Teddy.
One morning, Mike finds a badly beaten girl on the side of the road near a field where he had slept off his intoxication after another drunken night. She is a mystery and soon his possible redemption, which makes him play law enforcement again, because the young woman dies shortly after in the hospital. With a cheap business card and an equally cheap jacket and tie, he knocks on doors pretending to be a private investigator. Shortly thereafter, he chases a familiar dark tale of very young women (prostitutes) and very evil men, picking a fight with the smooth pimp and alleged murderer.
His old high school friend Randy, who now owns a bar, seems to be involved in selling young girls to pay-as-you-go suitors. Meanwhile, two more girls have been murdered. Ivy, one of the young prostitutes, and third a girl clique, is missing. Kendall tracks her down, and it turns out she's been blackmailed several times by Randal, who's been hiding her. The blackmailed defend themselves and send two professional hit men to the blackmailers. Meanwhile, the lead killer, known as "the orthopedist", kidnaps Teddy to set him free against Ivy. It brings the grandfather of the first victim and Kennall's client, Steve Wendel, and Mood to a showdown at a freight station. The killers are killed after a fierce gunfight that wounds three Saviors and Teddy.
The prosecution finds self-defense and acquits the four. His former colleagues, Detectives Crawford and Whitman, are able to pinpoint two of the three clients, the third of whom has defected to Mexico. They're giving Kendall the address they know of the last client because of the expected lengthy extradition requests between the U.S. and Mexico. In the final scene, Mood and Wendel track him down on the beach.
option_4_text: Ellen Arden returns home five years after she was lost at sea in a plane crash. But after so long searching and waiting, her husband Nick has just remarried Bianca. And it's the very day of that wedding that Ellen reappears, determined to ruin the wedding night.

query_text: Arthur Peabody, a middle-aged Bostonian, tells a skeptical doctor about his recent vacation with his wife in the Caribbean. While fishing in the bay, Mr. Peabody hears mysterious, silent songs coming from an uninhabited rock. Intrigued, he approaches with his boat, and his iron fishing rod... a mermaid! She's mischievous, childish and seductive, so much so that Mr. Peabody doesn't take long to teach her how to kiss. He hides the fantastic creature in the fish pond of the resort, near the house he rents. It's only a matter of time before there are complications...
option_0_text:
C.J. March works as a contract killer for the drug dealer Vernon Cray. She kills a man who stole $500,000 worth of drugs from her boss, but the man doesn't have the drugs with him. They're taken over by Emily Robin's pregnant boyfriend, who kills a man in the process.
March is being pressured by her boss to finish the job and get the drugs back. She finds out she's pregnant and wants to quit her job. March finds Robin, but does not kill her when she sees Robin's advanced pregnancy. She goes to an abortion clinic, but later decides to keep the child. Cray mocks her softness and threatens to take matters into his own hands. Meanwhile, flashbacks show March's mother being beaten by her partner  until little March shoots the man.
March tracks down Robin's friend and fatally wounds him during the ensuing chase. Robin takes the drugs and gives birth to the baby in the lobby of a restaurant. She dumps the kid and runs off with the drugs. March catches up with her, but she gets shot by Robin. She returns to her apartment bleeding, where she shoots Cray.
In the final scene, you see the heavily pregnant March sitting alone on a bench.
option_1_text:
The book is divided into two main sections: in the first half the characters interact together, while in the second half their individual journeys are narrated.
In the first half, Simon, a seven-year-old boy, shows up at the tower of the hermit Kerewin on a dark and stormy night. Simon is mute and therefore unable to explain his motives. When Joe, Simon's foster father, arrives to pick him up the next morning, Kerewin is made aware of their curious history. Simon was found abandoned on the beach years earlier, with no memory and few clues to his identity. Joe and his wife, Hana, are raising Simon, despite his mysterious past. However, later both Hana and her newborn son die of the flu, forcing Joe to raise the boy alone.
Kerewin develops a relationship with the boy and his father, becoming increasingly attached to their situation. Little by little it becomes clear that Simon is a severely traumatized orphan, and Joe is unable to cope with his behavior. Kerewin understands that, despite the constant and intense love between them, Simon is physically abused by his father.
Simon witnesses a violent death and seeks help from Kerewin, but she is angry with him for stealing some of her belongings and does not listen. Simon responds by kicking the side of his guitar, a very precious gift from his family, at which she yells at him to disappear. Simon goes into town and breaks a series of shop windows, and when he's brought home by the police, Joe beats him up badly. However, Simon stabs his father with a piece of glass he had hidden, and they both end up in the hospital.
In the second half of the novel, Joe is sent to prison for child abuse, Simon is still in the hospital, and Kerewin is gravely and inexplicably ill. Through a dying old man, Joe discovers the possible identity of Simon's father. Simon is sent to a children's home, and Kerewin faces the prospect of dying within a year.
Kerewin adopts Simon to keep him close to her and Joe, who's out of prison again. Meanwhile, Joe is able to contact Kerewin's family and reconcile them. The final scene of the novel describes the reunion of the three main characters, as they celebrate for some unspecified occasion.
option_2_text:
It was the '50s, Coney Island. Ginny is a thirty-nine-year-old former actress who works as a waitress at a modest restaurant, located in a playground near the coast. She has a difficult relationship with both her husband Humpty, who becomes violent when he drinks, and her son from her first marriage, who is a pyromaniac. She is also frustrated by a life without prospects and by the memory of the failure of her first marriage, for which she feels guilty. She becomes infatuated with Mickey, a younger lifeguard who aspires to be a playwright. Their relationship is disturbed by Humpty's daughter, Carolina, whom Mickey casually meets: orphaned by her mother, the young woman, on the run from a failed marriage to a gangster, knows many of her husband's secrets, and in order to escape his henchmen, decides to hide from her father, who had disowned her for years. Humpty is initially furious to have her back home, but later reconciles with her and begins to spoil her, even at the expense of caring for his wife and stepson.
After receiving a visit from two of the boss' men, the father initially warns of danger. Ginny is furious at Carolina's presence because, after learning of Mickey's attraction to the girl, she became jealous. Mickey, wracked with remorse, decides to break up with Ginny, but without telling her the whole truth, just as she gives him a watch for his birthday, stealing Humpty's savings. Disappointed, Ginny drinks again and drags Humpty back with her.
Mickey invites Carolina to dinner, who announces the news to the family as well. Ginny, who initially wants to chase after her to catch her in the act, notices on the street the presence of the same two henchmen, who have found Carolina and know where she will go to dinner. Alarmed, she calls the pizzeria, but at the last moment she hangs up the receiver, effectively handing her stepdaughter over to her tormentors. After dinner with Mickey, Carolina walks away on her own while the two hit men chase after her. The next day, all trace of her will be lost. The next day again Mickey reveals to Ginny that he has eaten the leaf, providing overwhelming evidence for something else rather easy to spot and goes to visit her at home to find her drunk in a stage dress. Mickey before leaving her forever openly accuses her, while she loses herself in theatrical quotes, without confessing but not even denying the accusations. Meanwhile, Humpty returns home, desperate for his daughter's futile searches, and aware of the tragic end he risks encountering, asks Ginny to start over, but Ginny prefers to continue with her unhappy and erratic lifestyle.
option_3_text:
Set decades in the future, Jules and George Almore have a car accident in which Jules dies. Her consciousness is stored in a device created by the company Archive, which allows him to have simulated conversations with her on the phone for up to 200 hours. At his job, George secretly begins developing a robot that will be able to hold her consciousness permanently. After learning from two initial attempts (J1 and J2), his final version (J3) is almost complete.
Archive sends a team to George's workplace to inspect the machine with his wife's consciousness. They notice he's tampered with it and built robots, and they suspect he's stealing their intellectual property.
J2 (which has the brain of a 16-year-old) becomes jealous of George's work on J3, and increasingly begins behaving unpredictably.
George finished the J3 robot.
J2, confronted with the realization that she will never be anything more or better than she already is, destroys herself by walking into a lake. Archive recovers the robot, and threaten to sue George's company. When she learns that George has been building robots, his boss fires him. He makes the final call to his wife on the Archive machine, and ends the call saying "see you soon." J3 overhears this and realizes that he intends to overwrite her consciousness with that of his wife. Though initially angry and afraid, she accepts her fate. The upload is completed as security storms George's lab.
At this point, any sign of the security team suddenly evaporates, and all is calm. The Archive starts ringing with an incoming call from Jules. J3 implores him not to answer, but George does and speaks to Jules, also hearing a child's voice on the line which is revealed to be that of his daughter. George was the one who died in the accident, while Jules survived and is now raising their daughter in the real world, and the ordeal he went through was a simulation within his own Archive, which has finally expired.
With his Archive expired, it has been prepared for burial at his official funeral. Jules and their daughter say their final goodbyes and leave.
option_4_text:
Much of the story is shown in flashback as Arthur Peabody tells a skeptical doctor about the source of his malaise.
After a bad bout of influenza, Peabody had gone on vacation with his wife Polly to the fictional Caribbean resort of St Hilda. While there, he hears singing coming from a rocky cay offshore and sails his boat to investigate and do a little fishing. To his embarrassment, he reels in a beautiful mermaid whom he names Lenore. Although mute, she is mischievous and childlike and more than a little alluring – so much so that before long Peabody has taught her to kiss. Meanwhile, he hides Lenore in the resort’s deep fish pond.
Confusion ensues as Peabody's wife Polly, who is herself attracted to suave Englishman Mike Fitzgerald, suspects her husband of infidelity with a vacationing singer. Things get more complicated after Polly storms off home without Peabody and police suspect him of murder. A search party pursues him to the cay, where Lenore nearly drowns Peabody by trying to conceal him underwater.
Back at home in Boston, as snow is falling, Peabody is talked into consulting Dr. Harvey and telling his story. In the end, Peabody seems to be persuaded by the doctor that he was hallucinating while undergoing a midlife crisis on the approach of his 50th birthday. There is only Lenore’s comb left to prove the reality of his adventure and this he gives to his wife as a homecoming gift.

query_text: In the 1980s, the rise of the glam metal band Mötley Crüe, from the youth of bassist Nikki Sixx to the periods of crisis that the band experienced in the early 1990s.
option_0_text:
Routine Detective Havenhurst and rookie Detective Vargas are interrupted while exchanging anecdotes: a murder has been reported. While the police are meticulously inspecting and cataloguing the crime scene, the murder case seems to have become a hostage situation. The swiftly identified perpetrator, college student Brad Macallam, has barricaded himself in his home after stabbing his mother to death in a neighboring house. Macallam claims he's got two hostages with him. The police order will be reinforced, and Macallam's fiancée Ingrid Gudmundson will be notified. Havenhurst tries to use Ingrid to find out more about the perpetrator and what might have led him to kill his mother. She says that Brad came back from a rafting trip in Peru completely changed. Macallam's friends had all drowned in the river at the time, and Brad was the only one who survived because an inner voice had told him not to take his kayak into the raging river. This experience marked the beginning of his visions and his gradual loss of reality. From then on, he followed his inner voice. Soon after, Brad said he called himself Farouk and claimed to hear the voice of God or see the face of God. His behaviour was manifested primarily in a kind of mystical narcissism, with Brad increasingly believing that he was the absolute anchor of space and time. He said that he had a difficult relationship with his mother because she was very attached to him and wanted to control his life. But he loved his mother no matter what. Then Lee Meyers arrives, who runs Brad's acting troupe. He says that Macallam called him this morning, desperately asking for help, but he didn't say what it was. Ingrid and Meyers tell Havenhurst about the performance of the ancient play Orestie, directed by Meyers. Macallam played Orestes's mother's murderer in the play. Ingrid also appeared in the Greek play. Brad saw himself as being in an ultimate emergency situation. He had become so absorbed in the role and identified with the tragic figure of Orestes that he believed he had to kill his own mother in order to set the fate of mankind on a good path. During rehearsals, he used a real sword, which caused great discomfort to the other actors, so Meyers eventually took his role away from him.
Ingrid testified that shortly before the crime, he once again turned to her for help and also to the game director Meyers, without them having understood what he wanted. He had also asked his neighbour, Mrs. Roberts, who was an eyewitness, to stop him by killing him so that he wouldn't have to do what he didn't want to do. Helpless and paralyzed, the coffee-table guests would have watched as Macallam stabbed his mother to death with the same sword he used during the theater rehearsals. He saw himself at that moment as an instrument of fate. The SWAT team's access and McCallum's arrest reveal that a dozen police officers and a heavily armed SWAT team had been fooled by McCallum. His so-called hostages are two flamingos. People were not in danger.
option_1_text:
In the Korean War, a distressed division of the U.S. Army is forced to retreat. To secure the retreat, the commanding officer commands a 48-man unit as a rearguard. The unit is commanded by Lieutenant Gibbs. He's joined by Sergeants Rock and Lonergan. The unit will be stationed on a pass in the mountains. During the march to the goal, the soldiers plan their course of action. Mines are to be laid and lookout posts set up.
Among the soldiers is Corporal Denno, who is unable to fire on individual soldiers. Rock informs him that in the event of the deaths of Rock, Lonergan and Gibbs, he's in command. Soon the unit is attacked, but the attack is repulsed. In the process, the men discover a cave that can accommodate the entire unit. Gibbs gets shot by a sniper. Later that night, Denno tells Rock that he gave the wrong orders twice at Officer Candidate School, injuring several of his men. Rock reassures him to trust his rifle.
The next morning, a signal trumpet is sounded. Whitey, considered by his comrades to be a know-it-all, explains that the Chinese are turning to psychological warfare. Rock sends Whitey and another man to steal one of the trumpets. Both return safely, but Whitey's comrade is wounded. While the wounded man is being cared for by paramedic Wheeler, Lonergan searches for Bigmouth, who has left his post. Lonergan finds him unconscious from the cold. When he tries to take it back, he's shot by a sniper. Wheeler's trying to reach Lonergan through the minefield. But he steps on a mine. Denno crosses the minefield and reaches the sergeant. But while Denno is carrying him back, he dies.
The next day, the Chinese attack one of the outposts, causing the men to flee into the cave. The men, who are ordered to hold out for only an hour, are afraid of the crossbowmen. Rock is killed by such a cross-bearer, Denno has to take command despite his fear. He commands endurance. When the unit is finally ready to leave, they hear a tank approaching. Denno decides to destroy the tank so that the enemy cannot follow the retreating unit. A bazooka destroys the tank, but the unit is thrown into a fierce battle with the Chinese.
Division has now successfully completed its retreat, destroying the bridge behind it. As the soldiers set up camp, they notice men trying to swim across the river. You can see Denno with the rest of his men from the rear, who won the battle.
option_2_text: The protagonist of the novel is Hank Morgan, a common citizen of Hartford, Connecticut who mysteriously (by means of the "transmigration of souls" and the "transposition of ages and bodies") finds himself transported back in time to the medieval England of the legendary King Arthur (the exact year is 528). Due to his knowledge of 19th-century technology, Morgan is mistaken for a magician.
option_3_text:
After years of abuse by the various stepfathers whose alcoholic mother changes continuously, in 1973 the young Frank Feranna Jr. leaves the family home after simulating in the eyes of the police a stabbing by his mother and moves, five years later, from Seattle to Los Angeles to try to break through in the world of music, the only passion that has allowed him to survive; after a failed attempt to reunite with his biological father, in 1980 Frank legally changes his name to Nikki Sixx. A year later, after arguing with the members of her own band (the London) after a night at the famous club Whisky a Go Go, Nikki befriends drummer Tommy Lee, her fan, and reveals to him that she is forming a new band; to it, after only one rehearsal session, is added guitarist Mick Mars, sick with ankylosing spondylitis, and later singer Vince Neil, from the cover band Rock Candy and former schoolmate of Tommy. The agreement is immediately broken and the group decides to call themselves Mötley Crüe.
Despite being involved in a brawl with some spectators, Mötley Crüe's first concert gives them a certain notoriety and they soon sell out all the night clubs in Los Angeles until producer Tom Zutaut of Elektra Records hires them with a five-album contract they sign with Doc McGhee as manager. During their first national tour the band receives advice from Ozzy Osbourne and in a short time the success becomes planetary, beginning an unbridled period of messes of all kinds. Vince marries a mud wrestler named Sharise while Tommy announces his engagement to a woman named Roxie, which is short-lived.
The Crue's excesses continually increase until on December 8, 1984, during a party at Vince's house in Redondo Beach, Tommy meets actress Heather Locklear while Vince and Hanoi Rocks drummer Razzle go to buy liquor; in the grip of the fumes of alcohol and drugs the two are involved in a car accident that kills the latter and Vince is sentenced to thirty days in jail, later reduced to nineteen. In anticipation of the singer's return to freedom, the remaining members of the group begin to work on their third album which, however, being much more commercial than the previous works, generates tensions and discord.
Nikki, dedicated to an increasingly erratic life, becomes addicted to heroin and fires Doc when he, in an attempt to help him, arranges a meeting with his mother; meanwhile Tommy announces that he wants to marry Heather and asks Nikki to be his best man, but on the wedding day the bassist is too high to perform his task and is replaced by Mick. On December 23, at the Pazadena Hotel, Nikki has an overdose from which he is saved only thanks to two injections of adrenaline in the heart: after this episode he decides to ask for help and go to rehab, convincing the other members of the band to follow him. A year later the four are in the studio recording Dr. Feelgood, which turns out to be a huge success despite the internal tensions.
After the subsequent tour, the group immediately gets back to work, but by now the disagreement between Vince and Nikki is such that the singer refuses to come to rehearsals until he decides to leave the band; despite the fans asking for his immediate return, he is replaced by John Corabi, with whom Motley Crue presents the new album, which, however, disappoints enormously. Meanwhile, Vince suffers enormous grief: his daughter Skyler, only four years old, is taken away by a stomach cancer, while Tommy is left by Heather because he cheated on her with a porn star.
After years of separation, the group decides to reunite with Vince to try to clarify and level the discussions that have undermined what was a true brotherhood; once Mick leaves the hospital after undergoing a hip replacement, the group returns to playing like the old days to the delight of the fans.
option_4_text:
Ma and Pa Snavely live in a cabin in the Yukon. Many years before, their son Chester left for the big city and became involved in crime after "the fatal glass of beer".
Pa Snavely, as portrayed by Fields, serenades a Royal Canadian Mounted Police officer with "The Fatal Glass of Beer", a mournful song detailing the evils of foul drink and bad companions in the big city. A zither accompaniment recorded for the film seldom matches the vocal, because Fields subtly changes keys when the zither does not, resulting in a humorously off-key effect.
Son Chester returns home after getting out of prison, and promises his father not to tell his Mother what he really did. He makes the same promise to his Mother. When Pa and Ma learn that Chester threw the bonds away, and intends to live off their savings, Pa and Ma hurl him out of the house.
Fields emphasizes the stagey satire by striking various poses and being overly theatrical with the dialogue. The most famous gag has Fields opening the cabin door periodically and exclaiming, "And it ain't a fit night out for man or beast!", with some obviously fake snow thrown into his face a moment later. He would reprise that gag during the "play-within-the-play" in The Old Fashioned Way (1934).

query_text: The film depicts the catastrophe of the night of February 1, 1953 from the point of view of a young farmer's daughter Julia, who is an outsider in her village and in the family due to a recently born illegitimate child, a son of baby age. When the dike broke, she had just returned from a village festival and was able to escape with her sister, child and mother to the attic of the courtyard, which turns out to be unsafe. All the family members, except the father, who rushed to the dike and was separated from the family, perish in the flood. Joe Armstrong is being held at a U.S. military base after being presented with two options after a trial: enlist in the Special Forces or go to prison. Every convoy that leaves with weapons from the base is repeatedly ambushed by local ninjas who are under the command of a paramilitary team of a leader and arms dealer, Victor Ortega, who plans to sell it to the highest bidder.
His lieutenant is a ninja named "Black Star" who runs a training camp for soldiers in Ortega's service. Having saved Patricia, the Colonel's daughter, from one of the ambushes, Joe will use his martial arts skills learned from a ninja master in his childhood to, along with his new army comrades, including Corporal Curtis Jackson, escape the traps to hold him and thus uncover the plot within the army.

Kate Dibiasky, a doctoral student in astronomy at Michigan State University, discovers a comet on a collision course with the Earth. Your professor, Dr. Randall Mindy, calculates that this global killer will destroy the Earth and the world's population in six months and fourteen days.
With the head of NASA's "Planetary Defense" organization, Dr. Teddy Oglethorpe, Dibiasky and Mindy are going to the White House to brief the President of the United States, Janie Orlean. There, they do not face the anxious reaction they had hoped for. As the midterm elections are approaching, and the president fears that the news of an approaching comet could have an unfavorable effect on her, she decides to "keep calm" and "explore". That's why Dibiasky and Mindy decide to go public. They have to navigate the media landscape, which doesn't get the attention they need. Mindy is stylized as a sex symbol, while Dibiasky is portrayed as hysterical in Internet memes. In addition, the public is reacting with denial and conspiracy theories.
A short time later, the president comes under pressure because of a sex scandal and now wants to take care of the danger from the comet. The comet is to be deflected by atomic bombs. Shortly after the rocket launches, the mission is canceled because Peter Isherwell, the CEO of a major technology company and financial backer of the president, wants to mine the limited raw materials of the comet on Earth. To do this, the comet is to be broken into smaller pieces by means of several simultaneous explosions by means of rockets and the pieces are to be collected on earth.
The public is divided by the new project. On the one hand, the dangers are seen through the comet, on the other hand, the economic opportunities through the raw materials. An attempt by other nations to distract the comet fails. This leaves entrepreneur Isherwell's mission as our only hope. However, this mission also fails due to several technical problems and the distribution does not succeed. The comet hits the Earth, wiping out almost all life. The escaped humans in the spaceship land on a populated planet after 22,740 years of cold sleep. They emerge from the spaceship naked and unarmed; President Orlean is immediately attacked and eaten by wild animals (called Bronteroc). It is implied that the remaining humans will also be killed by wild animals.
In a post-credits scene, Jason Orlean, son and Chief of Staff to the President of the United States, emerges from building debris on Earth, posts a selfie video online as "Last Man Standing" and asks people to follow and share the post.

Honorable police officer Captain James McQuigg becomes a relentless rival to powerful black marketer Nick Scarsi, though his investigation fails to expose him because Scarsi and his organization control corrupt police officers and judges. When Scarsi fails to intimidate McQuigg, he is transferred to a quiet suburban police station.
McQuigg continues his fight through a "war of words" with the help of some newspaper reporters. The fight escalates when Scarsi's younger brother Joe is arrested for a hit-and-run at McQuigg's precinct, setting in motion a complex plan to bring down the gang. McQuigg uses not only the reporters, but also a nightclub singer, the upcoming elections, and ultimately Scarsi's own organization.

Joe Armstrong is an American soldier who finds himself in the Philippines as punishment for his misdeeds. He is very grumpy and has no respect for authority, so he attracts the dislike of his fellow soldiers.
During a weapons transport mission, the military convoy is attacked by a group of rebels, aided by warriors trained in the martial art of ninjutsu and commanded by a mysterious warrior called the Black Ninja; they try to steal the weapons from the convoy, which includes a civilian girl, Patricia Hickock, the daughter of Colonel Hickock who commands the local base. The soldiers initially do not react to Sergeant Gallardo's order, but Joe intervenes showing a wide knowledge of ninjutsu even superior to the assailants; the comrades participate in the fight, but after the initial success are defeated; several lose their lives and others are seriously injured. The rebels attempt to take Patricia, and Joe frees her by dragging her into the forest with him.
The Black Ninja returns to his master, the arms dealer Ortega, who hides behind legitimate business and a respectable facade; he is entertaining future South American clients by showing them his ninja troops and his garden, tended by the taciturn Shinyuki, an old Japanese ghost soldier from World War II, found by chance by Ortega during the construction of the villa. The Black Ninja reports Joe's intervention and the fact that he was trained in his art; Shinyuki listens unseen but with interest.
Returning to the base with Patricia, Joe discovers that the majority of the soldiers have been killed and the survivors have pointed him out as the one who started it all; he is then punished by Colonel Hickock, who merely transfers him to another assignment only because he brought Patricia back to him alive; however, the other soldiers take him in dislike, especially Corporal Curtis Jackson, who first interrogated the survivors; Jackson openly provokes him until he gets a reaction, but ends up being easily defeated and is amazed by Joe's ability. The corporal, who has taught hand-to-hand combat for years, asks him where he learned all the things he knows how to do, and Joe says he doesn't know: he just knows how to do it, like he's always known how to do it. Jackson would like to convince him to set up a training school with him, which would allow him to make a decent amount of money, and tries to get him out of Colonel Hickock's dislike. He asks Sergeant Gallardo for information about Joe, discovering that his real name is unknown (the current one was given to him in the orphanage), he has been in and out of institutions for minors and finally participated in a fight as an adult; the judge has given him an ultimatum: enlistment or prison; meanwhile Patricia, after the negative reaction to the treatment suffered during the rescue, is falling in love with Joe and courts him, inviting him to go out with her.
Joe is grounded and cannot leave the base, but finds a system and goes to the appointment; here, however, he sees Sergeant Gallardo arguing with Ortega, whom Patricia recognizes because he frequents the good society with his father and has already met him. Gallardo also sees him and points to Joe as the leader of the resistance during the attack, so Ortega orders him to take care of him. The next day, Joe receives a new assignment: to take a truck to the port; here they ambush him and the truck is taken, but he gets rid of the enemies and gets on the truck, ending up in the villa-fortress of Ortega where he understands what is happening and intuits that Gallardo is playing a double game; discovered, he manages to escape with the help of Shinyuki, who claims to know him and promises to reveal everything to him later.
At the base Joe reveals everything to Jackson and Patricia, but is intercepted by Gallardo who has him put in jail; Ortega does not want to take risks, there is an important shipment coming and Joe must die; so he sends the Black Ninja in person to take care of him; the killer penetrates the base and kills several soldiers including Gallardo, but Joe manages to escape and puts him in serious trouble. To clear himself, he agrees to follow Patricia and Jackson to Colonel Hickock's house, who seems convinced but calls the military police to arrest him; Joe escapes the cops and goes into hiding; Patricia is furious and feels betrayed; Jackson begins to suspect that there is more than one traitor on the base.
Joe returns to Ortega's villa, where Shinyuki takes him by the shoulders and hides him in his house; there the young man begins to remember his childhood, when he lived in the Philippines and everyone began to die of disease; one day he was found by Shinyuki, then still hiding in the jungle as a Japanese soldier who did not surrender; the old soldier gives him the name Joe (because it is the only American name he knew) and instructs him in ninjutsu; but years later Joe was slightly hit by an explosion that took away his memory; the cause was the construction of a road, carried out by an American company, so Joe ended up crossing it. Now that he has returned, Shinyuki finishes his training and warns him that the Black Ninja has betrayed the code of conduct and must die; the two decide to attack Ortega's fortress together.
At Hickock's house, Patricia is kidnapped by the Black Ninja, while the Colonel and Ortega argue animatedly; Hickock was an accomplice from the beginning but now wants to back off; Ortega reveals to him that he has his daughter and has him in his pocket.
The next day, Ortega meets his clients again and shortly after Joe and Shinyuki attack the compound, soon joined by the U.S. Army; the colonel wants his daughter back. During the battle Shinyuki acts as a shield to Joe and is shot dead, and Colonel Hickock is wounded by Ortega who attempts to escape by helicopter; Joe finally manages to kill the Black Ninja, free Patricia with Jackson's help, and blows up the helicopter with Ortega on board.

query_text: Norma Rae (Sally Field) is a widowed mother of two who lives with her parents and works, like them, in a textile factory in a small Southern Baptist town. The working conditions of the workers in the factory are very poor, and none of them are unionized. That's why a New York unionist, Reuben Warshowsky (Ron Leibman) comes to the factory to convince the workers of the importance of forming a union in the factory. Norma Rae, more independent in spirit, was the first to engage with him and began to fight to improve the working conditions of the factory workers, which included the creation of a union (in the United States, it takes a vote of the workers for the creation of a union inside a factory). With much difficulty and Reuben's help she manages to set up a union in the factory and finds meaning in her life. The film is representative of the American social cinema of the 1970s.

In 1970, alcoholic night watchman Fritz Honka murders Gertraud Bräuer, a prostitute, in his squalid Hamburg apartment. He carves up the body, getting rid of some parts by throwing them away in a suitcase, while the rest are kept in an improvised locker in his wall. The police find the suitcase but cannot identify the culprit.
In 1974, Fritz sees schoolgirl Petra Schulz hanging out with her classmate, Willi. Despite their short encounter, Petra becomes a recurrent protagonist of Fritz's sexual fantasies. Fritz spends nearly all his free time at The Golden Glove pub, often soliciting prostitutes that reject him in disgust. One night Fritz brings home Gerda Voss, a vagrant, who is allowed to pass the night conditional on having sex with him. At Helga's birthday party, Fritz is disillusioned to learn that she is married to a man named Erich. When Erich leaves, a saddened Helga reveals to Fritz that her husband has been unemployed for months and now resorts to leech off her. One night, Willi convinces Petra to go to The Golden Glove in order to win her over. In the bathroom, Willi unintentionally provokes an older man, who urinates on him. Humiliated, he locks himself at a stall and refuses to get out when Petra comes to check on him, asking her to leave without him. Fritz notices Petra and follows her through the streets, only to discover that his apartment has caught fire. Firefighters find the corpses and Fritz is immediately arrested.

Following a grueling day of work, Long Beach, California firefighter Jeremy Thomas Coleman and his coworkers contemplate ending the day with a case of 15-year-old Scotch whisky. Jeremy enters a convenience store to buy snacks, but is interrupted by David Hagan, an Aryan Brotherhood crime boss. He accuses the store owner of refusing to sell his store which Hagan wants to further his criminal enterprise. The store owner says he buys protection from the Eastside Crips and the store is in their territory so it wouldn't be useful for Hagan's purposes.
Hagan kills the store owner's son and then the store owner. Jeremy narrowly escapes, however was shot in the leg by one of Hagan’s men. Police detective Mike Cella, whose former partner was murdered by Hagan while they pursued him in a different case, sees an opportunity to finally bring Hagan to justice. Hagan is detained and put into a police lineup. Hagan, sure that Jeremy is behind the two-way mirror, recites Jeremy's full name, address and Social Security number.
Before the trial, Jeremy agrees to enter the witness protection program, and changes his last name to Douglas. He leaves the fire department and is moved to New Orleans. Later, Hagan's attorney, Harold Gethers, arranges for him to be released from prison in the weeks leading up to the trial. As a result, Jeremy and Talia find their lives in jeopardy when two of Hagan's hitmen ambush them; though Talia is wounded, Jeremy mortally wounds one man, forcing them to retreat. Hagan calls Jeremy, threatening to kill everyone he loves whether he testifies or not. Jeremy vows to kill Hagan first and abandons the witness protection program.
Jeremy returns home to Long Beach, where he seeks out the Eastside Crips to buy an untraceable weapon. Jeremy leaves behind partial fingerprint but the police can not identify him because his identity is protected by his WITSEC status. Cella figures that Jeremy is behind the deaths. After damaging the instrument panel with medical ointment and decapitating the scientist, who turns out to be an android, Jim escapes the laboratory through a sewer. He then finds that Sara has been captured by the mysterious woman, now wearing a Snow White costume. She proceeds to tell them about her past as a costumed princess, which ended after she crushed a little girl to death whilst hugging her. She hypnotizes Jim with the necklace again, but Sara pulls it off and smashes it, freeing Jim from her spell, and allowing her and Jim to escape.

A group of shipwreck enthusiasts board a ship and stumble upon the wreckage of a ship belonging to Nazi Germany during World War II.
Due to a malfunction in their boat, the group is forced to abandon it and take refuge on a nearby island.
Exploring the initially uninhabited island, they eventually find a villa. Exploring the dilapidated building, they notice a tank for live fish and realize that someone lives there. At the same time, a German soldier comes out of the shipwreck wearing glasses and walks on the seabed without showing any trouble breathing. Finally out of the water, they head for the island. Suddenly, music begins to fill the house. A voice breaks the silence and reveals itself to be the only inhabitant. The villa's grumpy owner admonishes them to leave the island as soon as possible before it's too late. At the group's revelation that they have run aground on the wreckage of the old ship, the voice introduces a tone of terror, finally asking what the ship was called. The man finally emerges from a window to find that there is no means of communication with the mainland. Out in the open, he reaches the shore, gazing in terror at the shipwreck in the distance. The group, now exhausted, finally decides to sleep in the villa for the night, while outside a storm breaks out. With the first light of dawn, a group of Nazi soldiers armed with thick glasses and bleached, corpselike skin emerges from the sea. Upon reaching the island, they immediately kill one of the group who had gone out into the woods to gather supplies. The owner of the island warns the other survivors of a sailboat that they can use it to leave, urging them to do so as soon as possible. The group entering the forest finally finds the body of their companion, finally seeing the group of Nazi soldiers watching them from afar. Returning to the villa, the group enters the owner's private rooms and finds old relics and a flag belonging to the Nazi period. The owner berates them for not leaving when he had summoned them. One of the group shows him a Nazi rank badge revealing that their friend was killed by the mysterious German soldiers with glasses. The owner of the villa finally admits that it is too late and that soon they will all be killed finally deciding to tell the truth: he reveals that he was in the past the commander of those soldiers during the war. The commander reveals that during World War II, the German army was trying to create a perfect weapon: a super soldier capable of fighting in any type of environment and weather adversity. However, the Nazi high command was not satisfied with this and sought to create a soldier capable of fighting underwater without the need to breathe. This would have tremendously enhanced the German navy's war arsenal. The soldiers were created from the corpses of soldiers who had died during the war, selected from those who had distinguished themselves by cruelty and ferocity. The military group of that experiment was called the Undisie Corps. So a group of Nazi underwater zombies was created by Hitler's army. The Nazi zombie soldiers quickly proved to be extremely efficient and unmatched in battle. However, big problems soon arose because there was no way to control them and they killed on sight without stopping. The Undisie Corps were eventually withdrawn for further study. Near the end of the war, the commander escaped capture by the enemy with his group by fleeing to sea, awaiting further orders, which never came. Realizing that the war was now over, the commander sank the ship in hopes of destroying the platoon of zombie soldiers, remaining on the island as a guard in case they survived. This eventually proved to be true and they emerged from the waters ready to kill again. For the Nazi zombie soldiers, time has stopped: they believe that the war is not over, and there is no way to stop them. One by one, the crew members fall victim to the Aryan zombies. Between escapes to the island and the villa, the only survivor eventually finds herself in a hospital bed recounting her terrifying adventure.

Mary Lennox is a 10-year-old girl born in India to British parents, who never took care of her and never showed her even a little love, leading her to become spoiled and selfish. After losing both parents, Mary is left in the care of a wealthy widowed uncle, Mr. Archibald Craven, who lives in England.
The child is greeted coldly by Mrs. Medlock, the housekeeper of Craven House, who informs Mary that her uncle is almost never in the house and that Mary will always have to stay in her two rooms and there enjoy herself. Different towards the child is the attitude of Martha, a young waitress of peasant origins, belonging to a poor and large family, who treats Mary with kindness and kindness, pushes her to become autonomous and makes her discover the positive sides of the new environment. Initially Mary dislikes the spacious residence, the people who live there, and the surrounding moorland, which seems desolate and gloomy in winter, but Martha assures her that in spring, when the flowers are in bloom, everything will seem more cheerful.
A tragic incident involving the late Mrs. Craven deeply affects Mary: the lady loved to grow roses in a wonderful secret garden. In the garden there was also a tall tree, on which there was a huge branch where she always sat, from which she had fallen and died. Following this Mr. Craven, in desperation, closed the garden entrance door and buried the key, so as to have nothing more to do with that place. Mary tries to find out where the secret garden is and also to pinpoint the origin of a mysterious cry that she has sometimes heard in the house and that the service staff ignores or denies. Mary begins to spend more and more time in the park and the moor, at first alone, then in the company of Ben Weatherstaff, an elderly but good-natured but grumpy gardener, and a friendly robin. The outdoor life increases Mary's appetite; the child feels stronger and stronger after she begins to practice jumping rope that Martha's mother gave her.
During one of her explorations in the park, Mary finds the key to the garden in a hole and later discovers its entrance door, hidden by the ivy. The garden, overgrown by weeds over the years, is in need of care, and Mary, who has neither the expertise nor the equipment to intervene, asks Martha's twelve-year-old brother Dickon for help. Dickon is a kind boy, deeply attached to nature and able to understand the language of animals, who promises Mary not to confide in anyone the discovery concerning the garden.
One night Mary hears the mysterious cry again. Following it to try to figure out where it came from, to her great surprise Mary discovers in a room a child of her own age. The two discover that they are cousins: the child, named Colin Craven, is the son of Uncle Archibald, orphaned by his mother and confined to bed because he is believed to suffer from an unspecified problem in his spine. Colin is a spoiled, domineering and hypochondriac child, firmly convinced that he must become a hunchback like his father and die in a short time; however, he takes a liking to Mary, who visits him every day of the week and distracts him by telling stories about India, Dickon, its animals and the secret garden. Mary, convinced that her cousin is not really sick but only in need of fresh air and exercise, tries to promote his recovery by arousing in Colin the desire to leave his room and confiding in him that he has access to the mysterious secret garden. One day Mrs. Medlock discovers Mary in the room with Colin, who, however, tells her that if she throws Mary out, he, having the right as the landlord's son, will fire her immediately.
Colin then gets permission to leave his room for the first time and to be taken out into the open air in the park, in a wheelchair led by Mary and Dickon. The three children sneak into the secret garden, where they are surprised by Ben Weatherstaff. Irritated by this act, which he considers an insult to the memory of his beloved mistress, the old gardener rearranges the three boys and, in the heat, gives Colin a cripple. Furious, Colin rises from his wheelchair and for the first time stands on his legs, which he then uncovers to prove to Ben the absence of deformity. Aware that he is healthy and that he too can contribute, like Mary and Dickon, to the care of the secret garden, Colin also begins to go to the garden every day, becoming stronger and more self-confident. The three children agree to keep Colin's good health a secret, so as to give his father a nice surprise when he returns home.
Abroad Mr. Craven, who had a dream in which his late wife invited him to enter the secret garden, receives a letter from Susan Sowerby, the mother of Martha and Dickon (a very trusted friend of Mrs. Medlock as well), inviting him to return home for the sake of the boys. Archibald returns, and as soon as he arrives, he heads for the garden, where he hears children's voices beyond the outer walls, goes to see and is amazed to see not only the secret garden in full bloom, but also his son in perfect health and activity. The estate staff are surprised to see Mr Craven's festive return with Colin and the other two children.

NASA astronaut Mark Watney is one of six members of Ares 3, the third manned mission to Mars; it lands in the Martian region of Acidalia Planitia. On the sixth day on the surface, when they are forced to abort the mission due to a violent dust storm, Watney is hit by the habitat's antenna flying around in the storm, piercing his spacesuit and knocking him unconscious. With his damaged suit no longer transmitting signals, Watney is presumed dead by his comrades after a brief, desperate, unsuccessful search in the dust storm; they leave Mars without him. He survives, however, and his injuries prove to be relatively minor. But with all communication systems destroyed by the storm, Watney, the botanist and engineer of the mission, without a way to communicate with Earth, must rely on his scientific and technical skills to survive. The vital systems, such as the oxygenator, which produces oxygen from carbon dioxide, the atmospheric regulator, which maintains a healthy composition of air, and the water purifier, which turns waste water into clean water and thus creates a cycle, are still intact. He keeps a log of his activities in case his body is discovered by future astronauts.
He manages to cultivate potatoes brought along by the expedition in the habitat not destroyed by the storm and to extract water from the remaining fuel of the landing module. However, with his supplies and potatoes, he can survive only about 900 Sol (marstage). In the production of water, it fills the dwelling dome with hydrogen, but can later fill it again with air.
Reviewing satellite images of the landing zone, NASA notices that Watney is still alive, and begins to look for ways to save him. The knowledge of Watney's survival still holds her back from the rest of the Ares-3 crew, who are aboard the spaceship Hermes on their way back to Earth, so as not to distract them.
Watney plans to travel 2,000 miles (3,200 km) to the Schiaparelli crater, where the ferry is already located, which will later take the crew of Ares 4 back to the spaceship, which will arrive there in four years  he wants to be there at the same time to return with. He begins preparing one of the two remaining rovers from the Ares 3 mission for the journey by equipping it with solar cells and extra batteries. On a long test flight, he rescues the unmanned Mars Pathfinder probe and its Sojourner rover and returns them to the home dome, where he successfully repairs them and is able to make contact with Earth via a primitive hack of the rover. Mitch Henderson, the Flight Director of Ares 3, convinces NASA Manager Teddy Sanders to inform the Ares 3 crew members of Watney's survival, as they are now in contact with him. The crew is overjoyed, except for Commander Melissa Lewis, who blames herself terribly for leaving Watney behind.
When Watney's potatoes are ripe for the second harvest, the dome explodes due to material fatigue. He survives in the airlock, which has been thrown 50 meters away, and can repair the dome. But because of the cold of Mars, he lost all his potatoes and some of his water. With no way to grow food without germ-resistant potatoes, he is in danger of starving again. NASA is cancelling a Saturn mission that's ready to launch and using the rocket to deliver food to Watney. As the Jet Propulsion Laboratory is under time pressure, testing will be abandoned, and the rocket will explode after launch. The China National Space Administration approaches NASA and offers to provide one of its rockets in exchange for NASA taking a Chinese astronaut on the Ares 5 mission. However, due to the unfavorable constellation of Mars and Earth and the resulting long flight time, there is no time to construct a ground system, which is why NASA decides to dump the supplies unhindered.
Meanwhile, astrodynamicist Rich Purnell finds a flight maneuver that would allow the Hermes with the available reserves to pick up the Chinese rocket with the food in Earth flyby and return to Mars in time to rescue Watney. Teddy Sanders is opposed to this plan because it would put five other astronauts in danger. The maneuver and all the data are then sent to Hermes in an e-mail without NASA's knowledge, and the crew decides, after a consultation, to override NASA's decision. It initiates the appropriate flight maneuver, thereby forcing NASA to carry out the plan.
To save his life, Watney must reach the Schiaparelli crater and climb up to Hermes. NASA is instructing him to modify the rover so that it can make the trip to the Ares 4 landing site. He accidentally short-circuits the Pathfinder's transmitter and loses the ability to communicate with Earth. That's why Watney sends messages in Morse code with rocks that can be detected on satellite images. He's using the second rover as a trailer for the first, housing all the vital systems. During the journey, however, he must pause every five days to produce oxygen, thus taking at least 45 days to cover the distance.
The Hermes manages to pick up the food capsule during its flyby. The crew will be allowed to talk to family members over the radio, after which the ship will set a trajectory to Mars.
Watney's on his way to Schiaparelli by now. During the journey, NASA notices a dust storm on Watney's route, which would interfere with the recharging of the batteries and thus cause the rescue plan to fail. Watney, however, spotted the danger in time and was able to successfully outflank the storm.
Just before the MRM (Mars return module), Watney's rover overturns as it crashes into the Schiaparelli crater. Watney survives, sets up the rover, and can get it running again in no time. Once he reaches the MRM, he can reconnect with NASA through its radio antenna. Their instructions allow him to free the spacecraft of a great deal of excess weight in order to achieve the necessary launch speed to bring it on a parallel course with the Hermes. Watney removes an outer casing and covers the opening with a tarp. During the takeoff, the plane breaks, and due to the lack of aerodynamics and therefore too low speed, Watney threatens to miss the rendezvous point by far. His fellow missionaries are still able to reach the location by improvisation and blow a hole in an airlock of the Hermes to slow it down with the outgoing air. This is how Mark Watney can finally be rescued from Mars. He spent more than a year and a half there alone.

Unfortunately, a break in the inflatable structure of the Hab, due to the continuous cycles of pressurization/depressurization of the compensation chamber, almost killed Watney, who was in fact forced to continuous extravehicular activities (EVA) to use the impromptu communications system. The pressurization chamber is violently "shot" away from the Hab with Watney inside: during the explosion Watney's helmet breaks, and the astronaut is forced to seal it by cutting a portion of tissue from the sleeve of his suit and using it as a "stopper", as the chamber rapidly loses pressure. Again, Watney survives and manages to repair the Hab, putting it back under pressure.
Exposure to the vacuum of the equipment fortunately did not cause any major damage but it did cause some of the water supply to evaporate and the death of the second crop of potatoes that Watney had planted. Man's survival is once again in jeopardy as the potato stocks accumulated until then will not be enough to keep him alive until the arrival of the Ares 4 mission. As a matter of urgency, NASA is preparing an automated mission to send him supplies by subtracting a launcher from another departing science mission. Poor controls due to the rush to design and assemble a probe in just two months, cause the launch to fail and the rescue capsule to be lost. An agreement with the Chinese space agency procures NASA another launcher to retry, but the very little time available forces the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) to have to design a capsule without soft landing capability, with a high risk of failure and that in any case would have arrived on Mars well after the exhaustion of supplies available to Watney.
An alternative solution for rescuing man from Mars comes from an astrodynamicist, Rich Purnell, who studies a gravity-assisted trajectory with Earth that would bring the same Hermes, the crew ship of Ares 3, back to Mars, to attempt the rescue of Watney. However, the limited fuel reserves would not allow for an entry into Martian orbit and the project envisages that Watney will still go to the Schiaparelli crater, to take command of the Ares 4 MAV and make an orbital rendezvous with Hermes. The new plan is to send enough supplies to keep the Hermes crew alive for that long by launching the Chinese booster. Faced with a choice between the two options, in order not to endanger the lives of six astronauts instead of one, NASA chooses to use the Chinese launcher to send supplies to Watney and continue the journey of the Ares 3 mission to Earth. Mitch, however, is skeptical that Watney can be saved in this way, and sends the trajectory data in the form of a disguised file to the crew of Ares 3, leaving the decision to Cmdr. Lewis. All members agree to mutiny on orders and attempt the maneuver to save Watney themselves. In doing so, they force NASA to send them supplies with the Chinese booster.
Watney, having learned the developments, resumes the modifications of the rover in view of the transfer to the Schiaparelli crater, under the guidance of the engineers on Earth: in fact, more sophisticated equipment is needed than that used for the first excursion to Ares Vallis. To equip the life support systems cannibalized by the Hab, he decides to use both rovers, using the second as a trailer. Remembering also the psychological difficulties faced earlier, he also decides to arrange a small "bedroom", obtained from one of the two inflatable tents, and to dispose of the sewage (urine and feces) along the route, taking with him the entire supply of 650 liters of water in his possession. During the modifications, it inadvertently causes a static discharge that burns the Pathfinder's electronics. The astronaut is again unable to receive support from Earth but sure of being observed by satellites, he composes messages with the Martian stones using Morse code.
While Watney is finalizing preparations, NASA discovers that a low-velocity sandstorm will develop along the path from Acidalia Planitia to Schiaparelli Crater. The storm won't cause any damage to the rovers, but it will severely penalize the performance of the solar panels that Watney will be using to charge the batteries. Unable to communicate with Watney, mission control can only hope that the man realizes the danger he is encountering in time and is able to change course in a timely manner.
Watney, now experienced in navigation and equipped with a fairly comfortable vehicle, proceeds swiftly through Mawrth Vallis. Once in Arabia, Earth begins to notice a loss of performance in her vehicle's power system, but, unaware that she has entered the sandstorm that simply raises Martian dust into the atmosphere, she associates the loss of energy with the aging of the devices. Fortunately, a navigation error forces him into extravehicular activity, during which he notices the decreased visibility and therefore the ongoing sandstorm. Watney, not knowing the direction or size of the storm, improvised a system to predict its development by measuring the intensity of solar radiation at several points. In this way he senses the best route around the obstacle.
The astronaut arrives at the mouth of the Schiaparelli crater, but the rover overturns due to a hole covered with soft sand. Once again Watney survives, thanks to the spare equipment he had equipped himself with before leaving and a lever with which he straightened the convoy. With great joy Watney arrives at the Ares 4 site where he can use the radio system to communicate again with NASA, who immediately informs him that heavy modifications must be made to the new MAV. The Hermes, in fact, will not enter the Martian orbit, but will only make a flyby of Mars. The MAV will then have to reach the escape velocity of Mars itself, but is designed to simply ascend to the Martian low orbit.
Watney's modifications to the MAV are massive: the JPL orders the removal of all redundant backup systems, the seats originally intended for the five Ares 4 astronauts, and the control panel: the capsule will be remotely piloted by the Ares 3 pilot Martinez, as Watney is not qualified to fly. Watney also removes the nose of the aircraft, leaving a hole that is covered with Hab's cover residue.
Meanwhile, on the Hermes, the crew prepares to retrieve Watney. The launch is followed on Earth in worldview but the lightening of the vehicle causes a greater acceleration than that of the project (12g) and Watney loses consciousness. Martinez does his best to pilot the aircraft, but the hole cover on the nose of the MAV tears and causes greater aerodynamic friction than expected; the vehicle thus enters a lower orbit than calculated and would therefore be destined to miss the orbital rendezvous. The Hermes crew has very little time to find a solution: Commander Lewis decides to sacrifice 75% of the fuel for the control of the Hermes configuration to lower its orbit, as well as to uncardinate one of the two bulkheads of the Hermes decompression chamber to obtain a propulsive thrust from the ejected air. A rudimentary bomb is made by chemist Vogel, using sugar burned into pure oxygen and detonated against the bulkhead. The maneuver succeeds, and extravehicular activity officer Beck approaches the MAV propelled by an MMU ("Manned Maneuvering Unit") and a cable, controlled by Vogel. Beck recovers Watney, who expresses his joy, but has two broken ribs due to the high acceleration suffered during the launch and his prolonged stay in the Martian low gravity. The novel ends with Watney on board the Hermes recording a final video log in which he expresses his joy at being rescued and reflects on the human instinct to help those in need.

In a town in the southern United States, the return of a fugitive from justice (played by Robert Redford) unjustly convicted, unleashes chaos.
The sheriff, played by Marlon Brando, must deal with the town's sinister characters and their miseries.
option_2_text:
The play is divided into two acts. The plot is about Vladimir (also called Didi) and Estragon (also called Gogo), who arrive at a place beside a road, next to a tree, to wait for Godot's arrival. Vladimir and Estragon appear to be vagrants: their clothes are tattered and don't fit well; another theory[citation needed] is that they could be refugees or soldiers displaced from a conflict, such as World War II, which had just ended and which inspired much of Beckett's playwriting. They spend their time talking and sometimes arguing.
Estragon complains that his shoes don't fit and Vladimir boasts of cramped legs due to a painful bladder problem. They make vague hints about the nature of their circumstances and about the reasons for meeting Godot (but the public never gets to know who Godot is or why he is so important). They are soon interrupted by the arrival of Pozzo, a cruel but lyrical man who claims to own the land they are on, along with his servant Lucky, whom he seems to control by means of a long rope. Pozzo sits down to feast on chicken and later throws the bones at the two tramps.
He entertains them by animatedly dancing Lucky, and then gives them an impromptu sermon on the theories of George Berkeley. After Pozzo and Lucky leave, a child arrives with a message from Godot: "it seems he won't come today, but he will come tomorrow afternoon". The boy also confesses that Godot punishes his brother and that he and his brother sleep in the attic of a barn.
The second act follows a similar pattern to the first, but when Pozzo and Lucky arrive, Pozzo has inexplicably become blind, and Lucky, mute. Again the boy comes to announce that Godot will not come, although the boy claims not to be the same boy who the day before had brought the same message.
The celebrated ending of the play clearly sums up his lack of action:
Vladimir: Alors, where are you going?
Allons and.
They don't move.
What! Are we leaving?
Let's get out of here.
They don't move.[4]
option_3_text: The lonely, introverted Mason works for a telemarketing insurance company. He likes to listen to jazz music and he's also a talented painter.
