option_4_text:
Finally, Marcia Bradburn, who lives in a girls' school run by Emma Hope, has received permission from her parents to meet regularly with her boyfriend Roy Todwell. But Emma Hope reminds Marcia that she promised her parents not to rush things, and Marcia wants to keep her promises. She immediately runs to Roy, who is waiting in the school garden. But he is less patient and demands that Marcia run away with him and marry him. But when she insists on waiting a little longer, Ray takes a stone from the garden, kills his dog with it, and drives away in his parked car. The shocked Marcia tells Emma Hope about it. She calls her old friend Dr. Leonard Gillespie from Blair General Hospital in New York and asks him to examine Roy. Dr. Gillespie brings in a young physician, Dr. John Hunter Gerniede, who wants to specialize in psychiatry. After getting approval from Roy's parents, the two of them go to a party at the school. Dr. Gillespie is talking to the girls while Dr. Gerniede is in the garden talking to Marcia and Roy. He also leads them to the spot where Roy killed the dog, only to discover that Roy has no memory of the incident. Upon further examination, Dr. Gillespie and Dr. Gerniede conclude that Roy suffers from dementia praecox and therefore deserves psychiatric treatment. But Roy's parents don't believe in that diagnosis. With the support of her family physician, Dr. Ward O. Kenwood, she refuses to admit her son and to cooperate further.
While walking in the city, Marcia and Roy stop at a window displaying a toy train and a model airplane. The sounds produced are transmitted to the street by means of a loudspeaker. On a signal from the toy train, Roy smashes the window, jumps on the ledge, destroys the entire structure. And he says he's going to destroy Dr. Gillespie, too. Marcia will report this incident to Dr. Gerniede. But Dr. Kenwood still doesn't believe in the diagnosis and is trying to calm Roy down with medication. But he does not take the pill and flees the house shortly after Dr. Kenwood leaves the room. Shortly thereafter, Nurse Nosey Parker finds a Boston postcard in the mail with Roy threatening Dr. Gillespie. She reports this to Dr. Carew, the head of the hospital, who arranges a meeting with Dr. Gerniede and Molly Byrd. Dr. Gerniede even speculates on the possibility of an assassination attempt, realizing that Roy's seizures are triggered by noises like a train signal. They decide to book ambulance driver Joe Wayman for the personal protection of Dr. Gillespie, who probably won't take it seriously. Shortly thereafter, Dr. Gerniede receives another card from Roy, this time from Detroit, confirming the threat. Meanwhile, in Detroit, Roy is trying to seduce the dancer Bubbles. He wants to impress her with a sports car. To do this, he orders such a cart and has it delivered to an empty house. He kills the two suppliers there. At another meeting with Bubbles, however, he notices that the police are after him, and leaves town.
One night, from her room, Marcia sees Roy in the garden of the girls' school. When she turns to Emma, she calls Dr. Gerniede and sends Marcia to the clinic. Dr. Gerniede takes her to his apartment in the hospital and asks her to lock herself in there. Shortly thereafter, he finds traces of Roy in the hospital. Dr. Carew will call the police. Roy murders an assistant of Dr. Kenwood, who is in the clinic, and takes his identity. He's on his way to find Dr. Gillespie. Marcia, whom he had called and who subsequently met with him, wants to see him cured, and arranges by phone with Dr. Gerniede a meeting in Dr. Gillespie's office. Once there, Roy also speaks only of his recovery. When Dr. Gillespie and Dr. Gerniede ask the officers to leave the room, Roy pulls out a concealed gun and tries to kill Dr. Gillespie. Dr. Gerniede then quietly calls Joe Wayman, who knocks Roy out. A few weeks later, at their graduation ceremony, Dr. Gillespie assures Marcia that Roy didn't know what he was doing and can't be held responsible. Dr. Gerniede finally gets a job in psychiatry after getting an offer from Kansas and having Dr. Gillespie lobby for him.

query_text:
A group of shipwreck enthusiasts board a ship and stumble upon the wreckage of a ship belonging to Nazi Germany during World War II.
Due to a malfunction in their boat, the group is forced to abandon it and take refuge on a nearby island.
Exploring the initially uninhabited island, they eventually find a villa. Exploring the dilapidated building, they notice a tank for live fish and realize that someone lives there. At the same time, a German soldier comes out of the shipwreck wearing glasses and walks on the seabed without showing any trouble breathing. Finally out of the water, they head for the island. Suddenly, music begins to fill the house. A voice breaks the silence and reveals itself to be the only inhabitant. The villa's grumpy owner admonishes them to leave the island as soon as possible before it's too late. At the group's revelation that they have run aground on the wreckage of the old ship, the voice introduces a tone of terror, finally asking what the ship was called. The group claims to have read the Keiser bih on the bow.
The man finally emerges from a window to find that there is no means of communication with the mainland. Out in the open, he reaches the shore, gazing in terror at the shipwreck in the distance. Meanwhile the Nazi soldier, briefly surveyed the island, returns to the sea disappearing among its waves. The group, now exhausted, finally decides to sleep in the villa for the night, while outside a storm breaks out. With the first light of dawn, a group of Nazi soldiers armed with thick glasses and bleached, corpselike skin emerges from the sea. Upon reaching the island, they immediately kill one of the group who had gone out into the woods to gather supplies. The owner of the island warns the other survivors of a sailboat that they can use it to leave, urging them to do so as soon as possible. The group entering the forest finally finds the body of their companion, finally seeing the group of Nazi soldiers watching them from afar. Returning to the villa, the group enters the owner's private rooms and finds old relics and a flag belonging to the Nazi period. The owner berates them for not leaving when he had summoned them. One of the group shows him a Nazi rank badge revealing that their friend was killed by the mysterious German soldiers with glasses. The owner of the villa finally admits that it is too late and that soon they will all be killed finally deciding to tell the truth: he reveals that he was in the past the commander of those soldiers during the war. The commander reveals that during World War II, the German army was trying to create a perfect weapon: a super soldier capable of fighting in any type of environment and weather adversity. However, the Nazi high command was not satisfied with this and sought to create a soldier capable of fighting underwater without the need to breathe. This would have tremendously enhanced the German navy's war arsenal. The soldiers were created from the corpses of soldiers who had died during the war, selected from those who had distinguished themselves by cruelty and ferocity. The military group of that experiment was called the Undisie Corps. So a group of Nazi underwater zombies was created by Hitler's army. The Nazi zombie soldiers quickly proved to be extremely efficient and unmatched in battle. However, big problems soon arose because there was no way to control them and they killed on sight without stopping. The Undisie Corps were eventually withdrawn for further study. Near the end of the war, the commander escaped capture by the enemy with his group by fleeing to sea, awaiting further orders, which never came. Realizing that the war was now over, the commander sank the ship in hopes of destroying the platoon of zombie soldiers, remaining on the island as a guard in case they survived. This eventually proved to be true and they emerged from the waters ready to kill again. For the Nazi zombie soldiers, time has stopped: they believe that the war is not over, and there is no way to stop them. Believing that their commander has betrayed them, they intend to kill him as well.
One by one, the crew members fall victim to the Aryan zombies. Between escapes to the island and the villa, the only survivor eventually finds herself in a hospital bed recounting her terrifying adventure.

option_1_text: Somewhere in the eastern Caribbean, a small cruise ship collides with a huge cargo ship and is beached off a seemingly deserted island. Montréal, Canada: Detective Steve Carella must shed light on the brutal murder of 17-year-old Muriel Stark, who was attacked by a mysterious sex maniac in a city alley in the middle of the night. The victim was in the company of her young cousin Patricia and they were on their way home from a party when they suffered the shameful attempted rape. Patricia, wounded but still alive, after escaping her attacker takes refuge in the nearest police station. Suspects immediately fall on the sex maniacs already filed by law enforcement. Among them is the vicious pedophile Doniac who, however, during a recognition of the American occurred together with the other suspects, is not recognized by the survivor and therefore exonerated.
The first version of events, according to Patricia's confused recollections, indicates that the attacker was a young white man armed with a small knife. But Inspector Carella is not at all persuaded by that approximate reconstruction and supplied in an obvious state of shock. At Muriel's funeral, the inspector notices the young and desperate cousin Andrew wrestling and writhing over the dead relative's coffin. Struck by that scene, even more convinced of the need to solve the case as soon as possible, the policeman asks Paritricia to tell him the whole truth about the attack suffered during the night. The girl reveals to him that she lied. The assailant is her cousin Andrew who, according to the frightened girl, had long been morbidly infatuated with Muriel.
Carella's investigation starts at Muriel's place of work. At the agency where she worked as a secretary, the young woman had a clandestine relationship with her mature and seductive superior. A married man who tells the policeman about the affair but also about the obsessive presence of the accused cousin.
The discovery of the victim's diary will finally shed light on the sad story. Muriel and Andrew, who grew up together in the same house as brothers, had long had a passionate relationship. Muriel believed that she was pregnant and had even consulted a gynecologist to terminate the pregnancy. But, after discovering that she was not in a good mood, her attentions to her cousin had not been the same. Only the many attentions received from her superior had become important in the young woman's life.
option_3_text:
Attorney John J. Malone is an admirer of nightclub singer Anna Marie St. Clair. During a meeting with St. Clair, her supervisor is murdered and she herself is arrested as a suspect. She will be tried, found guilty and executed. Malone is convinced of St. Clair's innocence and sets out with his secretary Maggie Seaton to find the real killer. He also suspects that the murder may be linked to a protection racketeering case he's working on.
At the last possible moment, the scheduled execution of Anna Marie St. Clair can be cancelled due to lack of evidence. However, since the newspapers falsely report her death, she seizes the opportunity and goes into hiding. Shortly thereafter, nightclub singer Millie Dale, who had been hired as St. Clair's replacement at the club, is murdered. Eventually, Malone manages to prove the two murders to nightclub owner Eddie Britt, who is involved in the protection money business. Anna Marie St. Clair, who had a secret affair with Britt, is arrested as his accomplice and re-sentenced. The film ends with a kiss between Malone and his secretary Maggie Seaton, who had fallen in love during their investigation.
option_4_text: In May 1940, several million people fled northern France to escape the German invasion. Among them was a German who had fled his country in search of his son and narrowly escaped from Arras prison with the help of an Englishman.

query_text:
Billy Hoyle, a white former professional basketball player, often bets with African-Americans who claim that white men are incapable of playing good basketball. He usually wins those bets. One day, Hoyle meets African-American Sidney Deane, with whom he now performs as a team and accepts bets. One day, they both lose $1,700. Hoyle and his girlfriend Gloria Clemente find it odd that Deane played well below his means in this game. He and Clemente visit Deane and demand the return of the money; there Hoyle recognizes his opponents, who are also visiting. Clemente talks to Deane's wife, who refuses to return the money, but suggests that Hoyle and Deane participate in a competition together.
Hoyle insults his opponents before one of the competitive matches, which causes him to argue with Deane, who considers the insults unnecessary. The team wins $5,000 in prize money. On the way back, Hoyle bets his half that he is able to execute a slam dunk, but loses that bet and the money. He is then abandoned by the enraged Clemente. Two Mafia cashiers also demand that Hoyle repay his debts and show him pictures of blood-soaked bodies lying on the ground.
Meanwhile, Deane and his wife want to move into a better apartment. Her former home is broken into, the thieves steal cash and some belongings and vandalize the home. It's going to derail the relocation plans.
Clemente is on Jeopardy! Divide and conquer. She gives a portion of the prize money to Hoyle, with whom she reconciles. Hoyle's using the money against her will in a bet that Deane talked him into. Hoyle and Deane win the game, but Hoyle gets dumped by Clemente again. Deane tells him to listen to this woman. To the objection that he himself insisted on the bet, he replies that Hoyle is an adult and should make his own decisions. The two now face off against Duck Johnson and Eddie the King and defeat them. The final point is Billy's, where he's dunking the ball.
Hoyle's paying off his debt to the mob. Afterwards, the money collectors take a fake picture of Hoyle apparently bleeding on the floor. In the final scene, Hoyle asks Deane to get him a regular job and plays friendly against him.

option_1_text:
You know, Los Angeles. Shortly after his 50th birthday, Homicide Sergeant Roger Murtaugh is paired with Sergeant Martin Riggs, transferred from Narcotics. Riggs, a former special forces soldier who lost his wife in a car accident three years earlier, has suicidal tendencies and unleashes his aggression on suspects, leading his superiors to request his transfer. Murtaugh and Riggs quickly find themselves facing off against each other.
Murtaugh is contacted by Michael Hunsaker, a banker friend he met during the Vietnam War, but before they can meet, Murtaugh learns that Hunsaker's daughter, Amanda, has committed suicide by jumping from an apartment balcony. The autopsy shows that Amanda was poisoned with an exhaust detergent, making the case a possible homicide. Hunsaker reveals his daughter's involvement in drugs, prostitution, and pornography, and that he was seeking Murtaugh's help to remove Amanda from that life.
Murtaugh and Riggs attempt to question Amanda's protector, but they find a drug lab on the premises and the attempt leads to a shootout. Riggs kills the pimp and saves Murtaugh's life, who begins to tolerate his new partner. Although the case appears to be closed, Riggs is aware that the only witness to Amanda's apparent suicide was Dixie, another prostitute who was working away from her usual area. As they approach Dixie's house, the house explodes. Among the rubble, Riggs finds parts of a mercury switch, a sign that a professional had set a bomb; some nearby children have seen a man approach the house with a tattoo similar to Riggs's (which only green caps wear), and Murtaugh suspects Hunsaker is not telling the full picture.
As the investigation continues, Hunsaker is forced to reveal to Murtaugh that during the Vietnam War, he was part of the "Shadow Company" called Air America, a clandestine paramilitary organization working on behalf of the CIA. The team is currently run by Vietnam War veterans, and led by retired General Peter McAllister and his right-hand man, Joshua. Among their duties during the war was the destruction of drug-growing camps in Southeast Asia, they actually imported drugs into the United States; many years later the "Shadow Company" continues to traffic in drugs thanks to contacts used during the war. Hunsaker was laundering money, but he wanted out, and when General McAllister found out that he had contacted Murtaugh, he had Amanda killed in retaliation. As Murtaugh tries to convince Hunsaker to reveal everything he knows about Shadow Company, Joshua arrives by helicopter and kills Hunsaker. Riggs gets hit, too, but he survives thanks to the bulletproof vest. To make sure his opponents are discovered, Riggs is presumed dead.
The "Shadow Company" later kidnaps Murtaugh's daughter, Rianne, and demands the cop surrender to them in exchange for the girl's release. Murtaugh and Riggs plan an ambush at El Mirage Lake, where the exchange will take place. Riggs poses as a sniper, but is captured by McAllister and the trio are taken to an unknown location. Murtaugh and Riggs are tortured to extract information, but Riggs manages to overpower the kidnappers, freeing Murtaugh and Rianne, and the three escape to find themselves in a crowded nightclub, used as a front for "Shadow Company". With their cover blown, McAllister and Joshua go on the run separately. Joshua manages to escape, but McAllister's driver is killed by Murtaugh, who causes the general's car to lose control and be hit by a bus on Hollywood Boulevard. McAllister is killed when a fire causes the hand grenades in the car to explode. Murtaugh and Riggs rush to Murtaugh's house, knowing that Joshua will hunt down his family for revenge. They arrive in time to stop him and Riggs neutralizes Joshua in a violent backyard brawl. As officers arrive to take Joshua into custody, he breaks free and steals a gun from one of the officers, but Murtaugh and Riggs pull out their pistols and shoot Joshua.
After visiting his wife's grave, Riggs spends Christmas with Murtaugh, whom he has become best friends with, and his family. Riggs gives Murtaugh a symbolic gift: the hollow-point bullet he thought would kill himself with, as he no longer needs it.
option_2_text: In 1943, the US Navy ship USS Eldridge disappears, due to the Philadelphia Experiment.  In the present day (2012), researchers try to recreate the experiment, which has the unintended consequence of making the Eldridge reappear, apparently having traveled through time.  The sole survivor of the original experiment is aboard, and meets up with his now-adult granddaughter.  The Eldridge continues to drift through time and space, trapping others aboard it.  The research company attempts to cover up the incident by trying to kill everyone involved.  A struggle ensues as others try to protect the survivors, and return them to their original times and places.
option_3_text: Rocky Barnes and Dan Purvis, two childhood friends, became police officers and patrol at night. They arrest Ritchie Garris, a murderer.
option_4_text:
After three murders of elderly women, the victims being strangled and penetrated with foreign objects, the Boston police conclude that they have a serial killer to catch. As the murders stretch over several police jurisdictions, Massachusetts Attorney General Edward W. Brooke appoints John S. Bottomly as head of a "Strangler Bureau" to coordinate the investigation. Several suspects are interrogated and released.
As the body count grows, Bottomly, in desperation, calls in a psychic, Peter Hurkos, who pinpoints Eugene T. O'Rourke, a man who seems to fit the profile. The severely masochistic O'Rourke is taken in for psychiatric observation for ten days but nothing implicated him to the murders. Another murder is committed while O'Rourke is under observation, clearing him of suspicion.
While the 1963 funeral of John F. Kennedy is on television, Albert DeSalvo leaves his wife and children, under the pretext of work. He gains entry into the apartment of a woman, Dianne Cluny, by posing as a plumber sent by the building supervisor. He attacks her, tying her to her bed with rags ripped from her dress. DeSalvo is taken aback by the sight of himself in a mirror as he tries to subdue Dianne and she struggles free and bites his hand; DeSalvo flees.
He tries to enter the apartment of another woman, only to find that her husband is home. DeSalvo is apprehended by a passing police patrol. Found incompetent to stand trial for attempted breaking and entering, he is committed to a hospital for psychiatric observation. By chance, Bottomly and Detective Phil DiNatale pass by DeSalvo in an elevator, where they had been visiting Dianne, who survived the earlier attack. Observing the wound on DeSalvo's hand (Dianne, who survived his attack, could remember biting him but not his appearance), the pair make him a suspect for the Boston Strangler murders.
Conventional interrogation is ineffective because the treating physician thinks that DeSalvo suffers from a split personality: he has two identities that are unaware of each other. His "normal" personality fabricates memories in place of the memories of murder committed by the "strangler" personality. The treating physician thinks that DeSalvo could be made to confront the facts but that the shock risks putting him in a catatonic state. Bottomly expresses the opinion that catatonia would be the second-best thing to a conviction.
Under the condition, imposed by DeSalvo's defense counsel, that none of what comes to light is admissible evidence in court, Bottomly is allowed a final round of interviews with DeSalvo. After several sessions, Bottomly manages to reveal DeSalvo's hidden personality to himself. Reeling from the shock, DeSalvo slips into a catatonic state.

query_text: A young woman is left alone at her college during the Thanksgiving holidays and is attacked by a group of individuals against whom she must defend herself.
option_0_text:
Dart-In-Again, a young and poor nobleman from Gascony travels to Paris hoping to become one of the King's musketeers. When he first encounter three musketeers, Walrus, Octopus and Porpoise, he starts duelling with them but rapidly becomes their friend. Together they fight the guards of Li'l Cardinal Richie-Loo, main Minister of King Louis XIII.
Queen Ann is desperate because the Cardinal has discovered that she has given the jewels offered to her by the King to her lover Lord Duke Poussy Bunkumin. Dart-In-Again crosses the English Channel on his sailing horse to recover them and returns them to the Queen just in time to save her honour. In the course of his adventures, he falls in love with Constance Bonne-aux-Fieux. The King rewards Dart-In-Again by appointing him as a musketeer and celebrates his wedding with Constance.
option_1_text: Events taking place at the end of the 19th century in the Wild West in America. The plot — the complex vicissitudes of life of hard workers — a prospector Gabriel Conroy. Having found oil on his land, he knows happiness and disappointment, and danger, and despair.
option_2_text: After most students have gone home to their families for the holidays, Justine and one of her friends spend Thanksgiving alone on the remote campus of her university. After her friend decides on short notice to spend the holidays with her family, Justine is all alone. But as the young student prepares for a few days of comfort, she is unaware that she has already been targeted by a satanic group of killers. He hunts down young women for no apparent reason, brutally murders them, and then publishes his bloody deeds on the Internet. They always give their victims the name Kristy, since that name is derived from Jesus Christ, and they imagine that by doing so they are also killing God. When Justine becomes aware of the impending danger, her pride turns into naked panic and she flees to the campus library, where an unrelenting battle for life and death begins. But Justine develops a surprising stubbornness and kills all the members of the satanic group. At the end of the film, she leaves the campus believing that Justine no longer exists and her name is now Kristy.
option_3_text:
A killer decapitates Pendleton University student Michelle Mancini in the backseat of her car during a rainstorm. Meanwhile, at the campus coffee shop, student Parker Riley regales friends Natalie Simon and Brenda Bates by describing a massacre in the abandoned Stanley Hall dormitory, which journalism student Paul Gardner discredits as an urban legend. News of Michelle's murder spreads the following day, but Dean Adams and campus police officer Reese Wilson seem determined to bury the story. Damon Brooks, a jokester fraternity member, attempts to console the notably-disturbed Natalie, who rejects his sexual advances while in his parked car at a bluff. When Damon goes outside to urinate, an assailant in a hooded parka attacks him and hangs him from a tree. Natalie flees for help, but Damon's body and car have disappeared when she returns with Reese. Parker and his girlfriend Sasha Thomas assure Natalie that Damon has pranked her.
Later, while Natalie sleeps, the killer strangles her goth roommate Tosh Guaneri to death. She finds Tosh's body in the morning, along with a bloody message scrawled on the wall. Distraught, she tells Brenda that she and Michelle, her high school friend, had received probation for causing a fatal car accident after driving with their headlights turned off and pursuing the first driver who flashed them. Paul meanwhile investigates local urban legends, and discovers that the Stanley Hall massacre actually occurred, with William Wexler, a professor of American folklore, its sole survivor.
Dean Adams is murdered in the campus parking garage, and Reese later finds Wexler's office disorganized and covered in blood. Meanwhile, Natalie, Brenda, and Sasha attend a fraternity party coinciding with the massacre's 25th anniversary, during which the killer incapacities Parker in the bathroom and murders him by forcing pop rocks and bathroom chemicals down his throat. Sasha departs to host her late-night talkshow at the campus radio station. During the broadcast, the killer attacks her and her assistant, and her screams are played live on air; the fraternity partygoers assume it is a prank referencing the massacre, but Natalie, fearing Sasha is in danger, rushes to the station, where she witnesses the killer murder Sasha with an axe.
Natalie soon finds Paul and Brenda on campus. Paul, convinced of Wexler's complicity, escorts them away in his car. They stop at a gas station, and while Paul is inside, Natalie and Brenda find Wexler's mutilated body in the trunk. The two women flee through the woods back toward campus as Paul pursues them. They become separated, and Natalie flags down the university's janitor passing by in his truck. He picks her up, but the killer forces their car off the road, pursuing them in a separate vehicle. The crash kills the janitor, but Natalie leaves unscathed and flees on foot.
While passing Stanley Hall, Natalie hears Brenda's screams from inside. In the building, she finds her friend's corpses, along with an apparently dead Brenda outstretched on a bed; however, Brenda knocks Natalie unconscious moments later. When Natalie awakens, Brenda reveals herself as the killer, enacting revenge for her fiancé and high school sweetheart David Evans, the fatality in the road accident Natalie and Michelle caused. Brenda attempts to remove Natalie's kidney, but is thwarted when Reese arrives and holds Brenda at gunpoint. Brenda manages to stab Reese with a switchblade, and when Paul arrives, Natalie gains control of the gun and shoots Brenda, who falls out a window, before leaving with him to get help for Reese. As they drive away, the two discuss how this will later be an urban legend and all the facts will be misconstrued. Paul asks, "Well if this is an urban legend, where is the twist?" Brenda then appears in the back seat and attacks them with an axe. Paul crashes the car on a bridge, causing Brenda to go through the windshield and into the river below.
Later, a group of students at a different university have recounted the events of Brenda's killing spree, during which they say that her body was never discovered. Most of them disbelieve the tale, except for one young woman, revealed to be Brenda, who claims that the story was incorrectly told, and begins explaining "how the story really goes".
option_4_text:
In 2043, 30 years after a nuclear war has disrupted much of the Earth's climate, on Earth lives Eli, a mysterious man who is on his way, on foot, to the west coast of what used to be the United States. Along the way, Eli shows great fighting skills when he single-handedly confronts and kills the road pirates who attacked him. Needing to find water, Eli arrives in a crumbling city built under the supervision of the local crime lord, Carnegie, who aspires to be able to erect other cities and have total control using a particular book he is desperately looking for on his turf.
At a club, Eli is attacked by a motorcycle gang, but manages to defeat them on his own. Realizing that Eli is an educated man like himself, Carnegie offers to host him even though the offer is, in fact, non-negotiable. After Claudia, Carnegie's blind companion, repopulates Eli with food and water, Carnegie orders his daughter Solara to infest the guest with herself. The seduction, however, fails, and Eli offers to share his meal instead. Before eating, Eli has Solara recite a prayer with him. Solara notes that Eli carries a particular book with him. The next day, Carnegie learns from Solara about both the prayer and Eli's book, and realizes that this is the very book he is looking for. In the evening, Eli goes to retrieve the music player he had asked to be recharged and immediately afterwards is assaulted by Carnegie's henchmen. The men are surprised to see that the bullets do not kill Eli, who responds to the attack by killing Carnegie's men first and then shooting Carnegie in the leg.
Impressed by the mysterious stranger, Solara leads Eli to the city's water reservoir, hoping to follow him on his pilgrimage. Eli, on the other hand, wants to continue the journey alone, so he locks her inside the facility. Solara manages to escape but is attacked by two rapists from whom Eli saves her. As they continue to travel together, Eli explains to the girl that the book she has is actually a Bible, the last copy left on earth after the war, during which all other copies were destroyed because the survivors considered it the real cause of the conflict. That's why Carnegie is looking for it, believing he can use it to bring the people to their knees like some kind of modern Conquistador. Eli intends to take this last copy to a safe place claiming it was faith that guided him all these years.
Along the way, the couple stumble upon the home of George and Martha, two elderly cannibals who invite them for tea. Just then Carnegie and his henchmen arrive and in the ensuing firefight George, Martha and some of the criminal's men are killed. At the end of the shooting Eli and Solara are captured and Carnegie threatens to kill them if they do not give him the Bible. However, after taking possession of the book, Carnegie shoots Eli, wounding him and abandoning him there to return to the city with Solara and the rest of his men.
Solara manages to break free and take possession of a car to go to Eli's rescue and Carnegie gives up chasing her because of the little fuel left in his vehicle. Solara joins Eli, who, having regained his strength, has resumed his journey. Finally, they reach the west, cross the Golden Gate Bridge, and row to Alcatraz Island, where a group of survivors have built a fortress to preserve their culture. Meanwhile, Carnegie returns to his home and finally opens the copy of the Bible, only to find that it is a Braille edition. Carnegie asks Claudia to read it to him, but Claudia pretends she can't. At that point Carnegie is afflicted by the pain of the wound, meanwhile infected, caused by Eli's shooting. Carnegie realizes that his "empire" is collapsing due to conflicts between citizens and another criminal gang and that he is doomed to a slow and painful end.
Meanwhile, Eli, with his last remaining strength, recites to Lombardi (the leader of the survivors) all the verses of the Bible that he now knows by heart from having read it so many times. Lombardi transcribes the verses and, upon completion, archives the new King James Bible along with the Torah, the Tanakh, and the Koran. The film ends with the death of Eli, who can finally rest in peace after completing his mission. Solara is offered to stay with the civilized but the girl rejects the offer and returns to the village to her mother, bringing with her Eli's belongings.

query_text: In 2000, the Russian submarine K-141 Kursk encounters an unprecedented disaster that the government's negligence is unable to handle. As the sailors fight for their survival, the families are forced to desperately face political and bureaucratic obstacles, trying their best to save their loved ones.
option_0_text:
Under the command of Captain Shirokov, the Russian nuclear submarine Kursk is taking part in a Northern Fleet maneuver in the Barents Sea. Concerned, the torpedo team detects a rising temperature in one of the drill torpedoes and requests permission to fire this torpedo prematurely, which is denied. Moments later, the torpedo explodes, killing the crew and sinking the submarine to the bottom of the sea. The fire in the torpedo chamber causes the warheads of the other torpedoes to explode shortly thereafter. The bow section of the submarine will be completely destroyed.
Lieutenant Captain Mikhail Averin and 22 of his men were able to escape to the aft compartment and manage, under great danger, to contain the water collapse there, keep a line pump running with emergency power and ensure the oxygen supply.
The two explosions were also registered by NATO units in the North Sea, which drew the right conclusions and immediately offered their help, but the Russian Admiralty reacted very slowly to the events and, above all, tried not to reveal any details. It is only hours later that a submarine explores the sunken wreck and picks up the tapping signals of the survivors, while the only usable rescue vessel is still in port, thus arriving at the crash site even later. There it turns out that the rescue submarine can not dock to the submarine's escape hatch because the sealing unit does not work due to maintenance deficiencies. In addition, there are no replacement batteries, so the existing ones must be recharged before each new dive. Admiral Vyacheslav Grudzinsky, who initially leads the rescue operation, is deeply shaken by the poor equipment of the Russian Navy and finally calls for help the NATO officer Commodore David Russell, with whom he is privately friendly. Because of this arrogance, he's being relieved of command.
In parallel, the film focuses on the members of the submarine crew, especially Mikhail Averin's wife Tanya and her nine-year-old son Misha. They are increasingly enraged by the lack of information about the situation of their husbands, fed falsehoods and worthless phrases, and given the impression that nothing is being done. They are furiously confronting the military with the rumours and the TV reports they know about NATO's offers of help, which are rejected by the Russian side on the basis of military secrets, but they are unable to overcome the stubbornness. It is only after the third unsuccessful Russian attempt to dock that a ready-laden British rescue ship is finally given permission to dive to the submarine the next morning.
There, after days of confinement, the men slowly lose all hope and are severely exhausted. The next time you change the CO2 filter, the filter element falls into the water, the chemical reaction creates a fire that consumes the remaining oxygen. Before the fire, the men dive into the rising water, but when they emerge, they find no breathable air and suffocate. The slurry pump fails and the compartment is flooded. Hours later, the hatch is opened by NATO rescuers, who can only retrieve the men's bodies.
When Admiral Vladimir Petrenko, apparently the main person responsible for the delay in rescue operations, wants to express his condolences to the children who were left behind after the memorial service, Misha defiantly refuses to shake his hand. The children after him join in this gesture. In return, Misha gets his father's watch back, which he used to pay for the champagne for a comrade's wedding before the trip.
option_1_text:
Kim, an orphan boy in 1885 India during the British Raj, occasionally works for his friend Mahbub Ali, a roguish horse trader who is also a secret agent for the British. Mahbub Ali becomes aware of a Russian-backed plot to instigate a rebellion.
Meanwhile, Kim encounters an elderly Buddhist lama from Tibet, who is on a quest to find the "River of the Arrow", whose waters will cleanse him spiritually. Mahbub Ali has the young boy become the kindly priest's "chela" or disciple so that he can deliver a message to Colonel Creighton, Mahbub Ali's superior. On the journey along the Grand Trunk Road, the two travelers grow to love each other.
One day, British soldiers set up camp. Kim notices that their regimental flag depicts a red bull on a green field, which matches a prophecy left him by his now-deceased father, so he sneaks into the encampment and is accosted by a sentry. During a scuffle, his captors discover documents Kim possesses which show that he is actually the son of Kimball O'Hara, an Irish soldier who had served in the regiment. The lama decides that Kim should live among his own kind to be educated (despite the boy's resistance) and pays for his tuition at the finest boarding school in India. The boy chafes at the school's many restrictions, but eventually settles down.
Mahbub Ali convinces Colonel Creighton that the boy has the potential to become a wonderful spy; to that end, Kim receives extra training from the shopkeeper Lurgan during the first part of his summer vacation.
While traveling in disguise, Kim overhears a plot to assassinate Mahbub Ali and warns him, saving his life. He is then reunited with his lama and sent to help Hurree Chunder keep an eye on two Russian spies posing as surveyors. When he finds Chunder murdered, Kim talks the Russians into hiring him as their servant. He is eventually unmasked and the lama is beaten up. When news of Chunder's death reaches the British, Mahbub Ali is sent to take his place. He rescues Kim and takes charge of the interlopers' papers, but when a Russian expeditionary force approaches, the spies attempt to overpower him and he is forced to kill them; then he and Kim start a rockslide which buries the Russian force. In the end, the injured lama has a vision of his river, stumbles to it, and dies, contented. Kim and Mahbub Ali ride off together.
option_2_text:
A forester found a baby in a bird's nest and brought him back to be raised with his daughter Lenchen. They called the child Fundevogel or Foundling-Bird, and he and Lenchen loved each other.
One day Lenchen saw the cook carrying many buckets of water to the house and asked what she was doing. The cook told her that the next day, she would boil Fundevogel in it. Lenchen went and told Fundevogel, and they fled.
The cook, afraid of what the forester would say about his lost daughter, sent servants after them. Fundevogel transformed into a rosebush and Lenchen a rose on it, and the servants went back empty-handed. When they told the cook they had seen nothing but the rosebush and the rose, she scolded them for not bringing back the rose. They went again, and Fundevogel became a church, and Lenchen a chandelier in it. They returned and told the cook what they had seen, and she scolded them for not bringing back the chandelier.
The cook set out herself. Fundevogel turned into a pond and Lenchen a duck on it. The cook knelt down to drink up the pool, but Lenchen caught her head and drew her into the pond to drown.
The children went safely home again.
option_3_text:
Sam Stone has become a wealthy industrialist thanks to his wife Barbara whom he hates and whom he married only for money; in fact Sam would like to kill her to enjoy all the estate, entitled only to the consort, and the beautiful mistress Carol. One day, Sam returns home with murder intentions but does not find Barbara and discovers that she has been kidnapped by Ken and Sandy Kessler who demand a ransom to free her by threatening him not to call the police or they will kill the woman.
This does not bother Sam at all who, in fact, decides not to comply with their demands as he hopes for the woman's death and starts by calling the police. Barbara doesn't worry much about her kidnapping either, trying to put her captors away, but in vain she is imprisoned in the basement by the husbands who want revenge on Sam for stealing Sandy's fashion designer along with their savings; the two schedule meetings for Sam to pay the ransom but the man never shows up, thus making his game clear to the two kidnappers who are unable to kill the woman.
Carol, after learning of Sam's plan to kill Barbara, secretly intends to blackmail Sam, with the help of her boyfriend Earl. Knowing that Sam intends to dump his wife's body in the Hollywood Hills at night, Carol asks Earl to make a video recording of the woman's death but in the place indicated by Carol does not appear Sam, but the police commissioner Henry Benton and a prostitute, and, mistaking it for an attempted murder, also hearing the screams at the woman's desperate appearance, films their extreme sexual encounter.
Carol does not see the tape, reassured by the opinion of the companion who assures her that it is a "heinous" scene, and therefore sends an anonymous copy to Sam who, seeing the sexual act, thinks it is some kind of erotic birthday gift from Carol, and a copy to the commissioner who, interpreting it as an attempt to blackmail him (especially then by virtue of a subsequent anonymous call from Carol to instruct him to incriminate Sam), arrests the former for the murder of his wife.
In search of evidence, Benton orders a search of Sam's house but finds a bottle of chloroform that Sam intended to use to sedate his wife and pictures of Sam with Carol. With this, the police arrest Sam while no evidence leads to the Kessler spouses. Sam maintains his innocence by convincing the police that his wife was indeed kidnapped.
In the basement where she is held captive, Barbara alleviates boredom by following aerobics exercises on television, eventually losing a lot of weight, and begins to bond with the robbers by planning to enter the fashion business.
When Barbara finds out in the newspaper that Sam has a mistress, she understands her husband's game and stays with the Kesslers. Meanwhile, a serial killer arrives, known as the Bedroom Killer, intent on killing Ken and Barbara because they reminded him of his hated parents, but the killer falls down the stairs and dies.
In an attempt to prove that his wife is alive, Sam offers to pay the ransom: the Kesslers, who decide to take revenge against Sam, demand a ransom increase equal to Sam's entire net worth; the man cannot refuse, withdraws the money but begs the police to check the delivery site. Carol, not understanding this latest development of the story, wants to find out about the contents of the videotape in a video store but, unknowingly, starts it on every telescreen in the store, just as the commissioner is there with his wife, thus finding himself in a very unpleasant situation.
Taking all the money, Sam puts it in a briefcase and shows up at the appointment with Ken, but at that moment the cops arrive; Sam hands the briefcase to Ken but Earl arrives who, armed with a gun, tries to rob Sam, who tries to recover the money while Earl, in the confusion, is arrested by the police who mistakes him for one of the kidnappers. Ken gets in the car with the briefcase and, chased by the police, ends up in the sea. In the car, however, the police only find the body of the bedroom killer.
Barbara goes to the police defending her husband and the Kesslers, claiming that the murderer in the bedroom had been her kidnapper and that she had managed to escape from himself by ending the case. After that, she breaks up with her husband and decides to go into business with the Kesslers.
option_4_text:
Flamboyant Zani (Gene Raymond) is a kindly young man who grew up entirely and works in the zoo in Budapest, Hungary. His only true friends are the zoo's animals, and indeed Zani has been chastised by his boss for being too nice to them. His dad was one of the finest caretakers of the animals, but unfortunately passed away early in Zani's life, and for his mother who died at childbirth, so Zani was raised with the animals that became his only friends. You also meet the other main character Eve (Loretta Young) a young and beautiful orphan girl. Eve must somehow escape from her strict orphan school, since she is faced with the prospect of being forced to work as an indentured servant (more like a slave) until she grows up.
At the beginning you get to meet and see a lot of the different animals that live at the zoo, and how people react to them. You meet a little boy named Paul, played by Wally Albright, who is with his harsh governess and all he wants to do is interact with the animals but he never gets the chance too. As you keep wondering throughout the zoo you meet Dr. Grunbaum, who is looking at a sick monkey. A woman then comes into the office of the zoo and says that her skunk fur has been stolen, and apparently hers isn't the first to go missing. She threatens to ruin the place if it is not found. The Dr. sends for Zani, who is playing with the lion cubs, and the officers escort him through the zoo where he spots the orphan girls that had come to the zoo, and these girls are all whispering to each other that Zani is there. Zani makes it back to the Dr's. office where they end up bonding over his father and Zani admits that he stole the furs. Dr. Grunbaum tries to punish him but he can't as Zani has headed out the door toward the orphan girls that just walked by. The Dr. assures the officer that he will not do it again.
As Zani gets closer to the girls he lets out a whistle tune and the girls automatically recognize its his. The girls move along to look at the ostriches, as the head of the orphanage reads a fact booklet to them. While the girls are walking though they start talking to Eve about if she wants to escape now would be the chance, but there is one girl that is strictly advising her against it and warns her of what could happen if she went through with it and got caught. Since Eve is 18 as of yesterday this might be her only chance to leave. They keep walking around the zoo when they come across the lions and Zani is standing in between them and the cage. Zani starts talking to the lion, but it is directed at Eve telling the lion to think of all the fun you could have if you were free, and that you just have to take that chance. After missing her first window to escape the girls send a signal to the girl at the front by touching the arm of the one in front of her. Once receiving that message the girl jumps over the railing and into the pond giving Eve the distraction she needed to escape. The girls around her give Eve different clothes and she runs off into the bushes.
After all of this Zani overhears a couple talking about wanting to buy the fox at the zoo so the wife can turn it into a muff. This angers Zani greatly and the first chance he gets shortly thereafter he steals the woman's fur. The woman and the man go to the office to report that her fur has been stolen, and immediately the officers and the Dr. know who did it.
After that realization you turn your attention back to Paul the little boy with his governess who escapes while getting on the bus all the while his governess is pre-occupied. You go straight back to the head of the Orphanage who is realizing as she counts that there is one missing, and that one would be Eve. Then you go back to the governess who realizes that the boy is missing and she alerts an officer who go's to look for him. You see the boy run away and back into the zoo another way, and the officers close up the gates to get in, but the head of the Orphanage informs them that there is still someone in there that is lost, but they assure her that everyone is out. She tells the officers that if they do find anyone in there to come get her immediately so she can grab Eve herself.
Going back to the stolen fur Dr. Grunbaum realizes that he has no choice but to turn Zani in. You then see Zani offering to help search for Eve. He eventually finds her in the bushes, but informs the officer that there's no one there, so he turns around and leaves. That is when Eve changes out of her uniform into normal clothes. After leading the officer astray Zani goes back to Eve and you find out they've cared for each other this entire time and the whistles were to let the other know they were near. They sit there for a while talking and eventually they kiss before heading off in a direction Zani knows they wont be caught. He takes her to an old bear den, that has a hole in it where you can look and see a view of the city. Leaving Eve alone to gather food for her you come to find out that the officers, who have all gathered at the zoo dinner, are all looking for either Zani, Paul, or Eve. Not being able to resist Zani enter the hospital and immediately jumps into action thinking of what they're going to do save the monkey the Dr. is trying to save and without a second though Zani goes and gets the solution of bringing in Maria who is the other monkey in the cage. He ends up saving the animal and Dr. Grunbaum temporarily forgets that he's having Zani arrested.
On Zani's way back to the den he picks up Mimi the monkey and takes her with him. When he gets there Eve is upset and is wondering what is going to happen tomorrow. and Zani is trying his best to comfort her. Meanwhile Paul's parents are worried and want to know where their son is, and a lot of officers have now arrived to look for these three. Back at the den you find out that Eve ran away for Zani and that Zani wanted her to run away for him. Eve says she thought they'd get married, and this takes Zani aback but realizing that hurt Eve when he did that he asks what they would do if that happened. She says that they would get a house somewhere just like others. After having a moment of happiness Eve find Paul hiding and crying near the den, because he thinks since he ran away he's gong to jail.
One of the other zookeepers finds the three in the den and Zani runs after him, but shortly after he starts running away from the officers. Zani gets caught and you realize that the other zookeeper is trying to have his way with Eve since Zani is gone, but Zani hears Eve's screams and escapes to run after her. He fights the other zookeeper off of Eve. Paul escapes and keeps running until he gets to an area where there is a strange man locked in a cage, because he was put earlier that night by one of the zookeepers. The strange man has Paul go and get the key and get him out of the cage but Paul accidentally does the wrong cage and lets loose the tiger. All the sudden with the tiger leaping around getting mad at the other animals making them excited all of the animals break out of their cage and start fighting with one another. This makes the little boy start to sob, someone hears him and they recognize it coming from the tiger, lion, and elephant area.
In a resourceful move Zani lowers himself to where Paul is so he can snatch him up and get him out of harms way, but after grabbing him one of the animals grabs hold of Zani's leg and he is left very injured. After getting the help of some hoses and a very smart elephant the Dr. gets the animals back into their cages. As Zani is getting taken away to the hospital Paul's father comes up to him and says thank you, and if there is anything I can do let me know. Zani then replies that he doesn't want the orphanage to take Eve away.

Sophie (Sandrine Bonnaire) is hired as a maid by the Lelièvre, a middle-class couple (Jean-Pierre Cassel and Jacqueline Bisset). A shy and introverted young woman, she is illiterate, but carefully hides it because she is ashamed of it.
While also keeping her secret from him, she befriends Jeanne (Isabelle Huppert), the village postmistress, a woman with a troubled past. The latter devoted unbounded hatred and jealousy to the Lelièvre, as well as to their daughter, Melinda (Virginie Ledoyen), despite the mechanical service that the latter rendered him one day when his car broke down in the countryside. Gradually Jeanne turns Sophie against the Lilies. Gradually the criminal past of the two young women is revealed and their psychiatric flaws emerge.
One day, Melinda accidentally discovers Sophie's illiteracy and offers to help her. Ashamed and furious, Sophie threatens to tell Melinda's parents about their daughter's pregnancy so that she will keep her secret, but the girl, in tears, hurries to tell everything to her father who, not appreciating Sophie's blackmail, decides to fire her.
One evening, Sophie and Jeanne unexpectedly go to the Lelièvre's house, who cannot hear the two women because they are listening to Mozart's opera Don Giovanni on television. Jeanne, out of revenge, sets out to sack the house, while Sophie follows her in her destructive madness. They shoot Georges Lelièvre who had surprised them with his hunting rifles in hand. They also killed the rest of the family: Catherine, the mother, then her two children, Melinda and her brother Gilles. This scene of the murder of the family unfolds to the sound of Don Juan's serenade with mandolin accompaniment.
After their mischief, Jeanne bids Sophie farewell by taking Melinda's cassette player, but she immediately dies in a traffic accident near the Lelièvre's house while she tries in vain to start her car, failing to go to a garage as Melinda had advised her. The gendarmes find the stolen station: the Lelièvre had recorded the opera, and by the way, we also hear the murders. Sophie, unaware of this discovery, arrives at the scene of the accident amidst the gendarmes.

Sophie Bonhomme is hired as a maid by the Lelièvre. The family, who live in an isolated villa in the Breton countryside, consists of Catherine, her husband Georges, and a son and a daughter from previous marriages. Gilles is the son of Catherine and her ex-husband, a lonely teenager who loves reading and has a strong passion for art; Melinda is the daughter of Georges, studies at university and spends weekends at home, where she invites her boyfriend, Jérémie. Catherine  who owns an art gallery - can't take care of the house, seeks the help of a waitress and hence hires Sophie.
Sophie avoids using the dishwasher, refuses to take driving lessons (because she doesn't have a driver's license), buys fake eyeglasses, and has trouble counting the change given to her after shopping. Towards the end of the film it becomes clear that Sophie is illiterate, and that she has a history of violence, so much so that she is suspected of having killed her disabled father, or at least of not having helped him out of the fire that broke out in his own house.
Unable to drive, Sophie walks the road to the village, where she meets Jeanne, a post office clerk who also volunteers at the local parish. Jeanne, frowned upon by Georges, begins to have a bad influence on Sophie; the employee, in addition to being always indisposed and aggressive towards others, tampers with packages and letters intended for the Lelièvre. She also has a history of violence, having been accused of killing her daughter. The two friends meet regularly, both in the village and in Sophie's room at the Lelièvre house to watch television. Sophie is well treated by the two spouses, but their safe conduct and trouble-free life gives rise to feelings of envy in both Sophie and Jeanne.
One day, at Jeanne's instigation, the maid overhears a telephone conversation between Melinda and her boyfriend, and discovers that the young woman is pregnant. Shortly after, during a conversation in the kitchen, Melinda realizes that the maid is illiterate; the latter, offended, threatens to reveal the girl's pregnancy if she reveals the matter to the parents. The girl, in tears, reveals to her parents that she has been blackmailed, and also Sophie's problem: her father then decides to fire her, giving her a week to organize. Jeanne then tells her friend how she had accidentally killed her son years earlier and how justice had been reluctant to believe her, while Sophie's involvement in the fire in which her father died remains unclear.
At night, while the Lelièvre family is seated in the living room watching Mozart's Don Giovanni, the two women enter the house without being noticed. They go into the couple's bedroom, tear off their clothes, tear up family photos, sprinkle chocolate on their sheets. Then they go down to the kitchen, load Georges' hunting rifles, and lure the man into the kitchen with a loud noise. He reluctantly interrupts the viewing of the opera, and in the kitchen Sophie kills him. The two women then kill the rest of the family.
Jeanne leaves the scene of the crime in her Citroen, and is later killed in a car accident by the priest who had taken her away from her volunteer work. The film opens as Dr. Brian Cowper (Robert Coleby) takes a shower in the flat he shares with his wife Jill (Judy Morris), who is a masters student in anthropology. As he exits the building's lift on his way to work, an ominous character is seen entering and randomly choosing the button for the ninth floor. He knocks on the Cowpers' door and announces himself as Max (Ivar Kants), the building's plumber. Jill insists that they did not call for a plumber, and Max assures her that he is simply doing a mandatory check of the building's pipes.
Max maintains an affable, loquacious facade. Once inside the bathroom, he starts to chip away at the tile under the sink. When Jill rushes to the bathroom to see what he is doing, Max impishly encourages her to leave him to his work. He closes the door and then takes a very loud shower. Meanwhile, Brian has been informed that a team from the World Health Organization is coming to interview him about his work. He calls Jill to share the news, and in his glee, he dismisses her concerns about Max.
Max tells Jill that the apartment's pipes are a mess and that he will come back tomorrow to replace them. After he leaves, Jill goes to the bathroom to look at the mess that Max made, and he suddenly appears behind her. He claims that the door was unlocked and that he was just bringing in her groceries, since he had noticed they were in a heavy box. This basic pattern of Max's odd, slightly ominous behaviour recurs and expands throughout the film. He keeps finding excuses to visit the unit, and his work in the bathroom only makes a bigger mess each time. Because Brian never sees Max, he dismisses Jill's concerns out of hand. In one shot, Max patiently waits in his car for Brian to leave before heading up to the apartment.
Max eventually erects an elaborate scaffolding in the bathroom which renders it largely useless. As the Cowpers host the WHO officials for dinner, one of their guests gets himself trapped in the rigging and injures himself. During an argument with Jill, Max finally promises to finish his work, threatening that he will do a haphazard job just to get it over with. Sure enough, the plumbing explodes, pouring fetid water all over the bathroom, and prompting the return of Max to the apartment.
The film ends with the police arresting Max. They search his car and find items that belong to Jill. She looks down on the arrest from her balcony, and Max screams at her that she set him up.

It's the spring of '98. Jake Shuttlesworth has been incarcerated for more than six years in Attica Prison, near New York, serving a 20-year sentence for the manslaughter of his wife. Outside of prison, his 18-year-old son Jesus is considered the greatest prospect in high school basketball and the most prestigious universities in the United States of America are willing to do anything to have him on their teams starting next season. Jesus, whose high school team recently won the state championship, has yet to make his selection and is only one week away from the deadline. For this reason, Jake is summoned by the warden of the prison who offers him, on behalf of the governor of the state of New York, a sharp reduction in sentence if he manages to convince his son to enroll in Big State University, of which the governor is an avid supporter.
To allow the father-son reunion, Jake is forced to eat spoiled food and secretly removed from prison for health reasons. At this point, Jake has one week to convince his son Jesus to enroll at Big State University; Jake is watched over by Agents Crudup and Spivey.
Jake immediately meets his daughter Mary, who is going to middle school and is very happy to see him again. Very different is the reaction of Jesus, who refuses to entertain his father, treats him with disdain and distrust and refuses to speak to him.
So Jake goes to a hotel in Coney Island, where he lived with his family and where his children grew up, a troubled neighborhood in Brooklyn where one of the most popular activities is street basketball and young people spend hours at playgrounds. Here he meets Dakota Burns, a prostitute, constantly beaten by her protector, Sweetness. Jake soon falls in love with the woman and will do whatever he can to get her out of her predicament.
Meanwhile, Jesus is having a very difficult week. The boy is in fact pressured by almost all the people who are close to him, including the uncles with whom he grew up after the death of his mother and the conviction of his father, his coach and even his girlfriend Lala, who even accepts money to exert her influence on the boy. He is visited by controversial sports attorneys who urge him to enter directly into the NBA and universities who take him to visit their campuses to entice him in the fateful choice. Jesus remains undecided: he has a younger sister to look after, he lives in a poor neighborhood and becoming a professional player would immediately solve his economic problems, depriving him of the opportunity to have a university education and with the risk of being surrounded by parasites and falling into the thousand dangers of professional sports. Everyone smells the money that Jesus will earn: the situation disgusts him a lot and he keeps closing in on himself, postponing the decision to the last-minute press conference.
Jake tries in vain to establish a dialogue with his son, telling him among other things the reason for his particular name: Jesus in honor of his idol "Black Jesus", as basketball player Earl Monroe was called, NBA champion with the New York Knicks in 1973 and former star of the Baltimore Bullets. On the last night before the end of the week of semi-freedom, he finally confesses to his son the reason why he got out of prison, and challenges him to basketball in a one-on-one duel to force him to choose Big State University: if the father wins, Jesus will enroll in Big State; if the son wins, he will do what he believes is best. During the rehearsal, in the playground near the house, father and son will confess their deepest secrets, finally establishing a dialogue absent for years. The challenge is easily won by Jesus, who in front of Crudup and Spivey, arriving to take him back to Attica prison, throws in front of his father the papers of his enrollment at Big State.
However, moved by the sincerity and affection that his father feels for him despite his rejections, Jesus still agrees to enroll in Big State and announces it officially during the press conference at his high school, while Jake, now back in prison, finally manages to have a dialogue with his son. But in the end the warden keeps his word by denying the sentence reduction, as Jake has actually failed to get Jesus to sign the papers, making his sacrifice worthless.
Jake remains in prison, but is happy to be reunited with his son. While playing basketball on the prison court, he throws the ball over the wall, which magically ends up on the Big State court where Jesus is training. Jesus takes the ball in his hand, seeing it as a sign of hope from his father.

October of 1945. 19-year-old German prisoner of war Mark Niebuhr arrives with other prisoners at a Warsaw train station. A Polish woman waiting for her train believes she recognizes the SS officer who murdered her daughter during a raid in Lublin. Niebuhr sees her talking to one of his Polish guards, but cannot understand the content of the conversation. Shortly thereafter, he is taken away and placed in solitary confinement in a prison.
The former grenadier of an infantry unit does not know why he is being detained. When questioned by a young Polish officer, he is repeatedly asked to write down his resume and give his real name. Niebuhr does not understand the harassment he is subjected to, and keeps insisting that he is just Mark Niebuhr.
In prison, he experiences the hatred of a Polish fellow prisoner, and during work assignments, he is assigned to the most dangerous tasks. So he has to unsecured, sitting on the wall of a bombed-out Warsaw house, throwing stones and breaking his arm in an accident.
At the hospital, he learns that he's being investigated for murder. He is transferred to a new cell where other German prisoners of war are already being held. Among them there is a strict military order based on their former ranks. Corps spirit and fascist ideals are reflected in this microcosm led by General Eisensteck and Major Lundenbroich. Niebuhr is the new guy who's slowly getting to know the others. Everybody tells him he's innocent. But Niebuhr slowly realizes that he's in a cell with murderers, hangmen, and real war criminals. He begins to distance himself from them, isolates himself, and is eventually rejected by them. During the months of his imprisonment in this cell, he is persuaded that as a German soldier he has incurred personal guilt.
As the rest of the prisoners are taken one by one to be executed, Mark Niebuhr's story is finally believed. Although one of his former comrades refuses to identify him during a confrontation, the Polish woman's accusation is recognized as a mistake and he is eventually released.

Late 20th century. Huge flying saucers come from space hovering over the world's major metropolises, taking no action but to impose an end to every terrestrial conflict. For fifty years the contact with the visitors, called Superni ("Overlords" in the original English, "Superni" in various Italian editions, for example Urania, Oscar Mondadori, etc.), is limited to meetings inside one of the ships, between the Secretary General of the United Nations Rikki Stormgren, and the Controller General Karellen, without however that the terrestrial can see it.
The fateful date arrives. Aliens show up for the first time. It's no accident that we delayed it. Despite their peaceful intentions, they have the appearance of demons, with horns, tails, and bat wings.
It's the golden age. Huge capital, once squandered on military spending, is diverted for civilian use, ushering in an era of wealth, peace and well-being but progress is limited to the Earth alone because, with the complicity of the Supers, Humanity seems to be disinterested in the Cosmos, distracted by a lifestyle between ease and leisure.
A restless Ian Rodricks, an unemployed astrophysicist, manages with an ingenious ruse to clandestinely board a spaceship and visit the world of origin of the Superns, forty light years away, taking advantage of relativistic time dilation, making the journey seem to last a few months. Once he reaches his destination, however, he will be the first of all to learn a bitter truth. The Supermind has a master, called the Overmind, an entity of pure energy that roams the cosmos and without which no living thing can physically cross interstellar space.
In our world, meanwhile, children and adolescents manifest paranormal abilities, lose interest in childhood, and abandon their families to reunite in the Amazon rainforest. Adults, who have now become individual entities, are unable to develop further like children. Lacking a purpose in life, they retreat into solitude or opt for the extreme gesture. Rodricks returns to Earth 80 years later, in time to witness the mind-meld between the children of the Last Generation and the Super-mind. The planet ceases to exist. Humanity has finished its childhood. The Overlords sadly leave the Solar System, in search of new papable races, aware of their true damned nature, that is, being perfect mortals.

The novel tells the story of 24-year-old Veronika, who apparently lacks nothing and who nevertheless decides to commit suicide. The attempt fails; she is admitted to the psychiatric clinic Villete. Here the doctors predict that she will die within a week from the late effects of the pill overdose. With only a short time left, Veronika is finally allowing herself to be as she sees fit. Another central theme is madness and its paradoxical relationship to normality.
# Backgrounds
The action begins on 11 November 1997 and ends on 18 February 1998 and takes place in Slovenia. In addition to these dates, Paulo Coelho uses other references to reality. On the one hand, he mentions places in Ljubljana or the Slovenian poet Prešeren, on the other hand, the novel takes place against the background of the conflicts after the partition of Yugoslavia. There are some intertwining of the characters with the consequences of the declaration of independence of Slovenia and the crises in the neighboring countries. Moreover, Coelho does not shy away from establishing a self-reference right from the start. Later, he tells how he came across Veronica's story. All of this adds to the appeal of a true story.
In fact, according to Coelho himself, he is working through his experience of having been sent to a psychiatric clinic three times by his parents because they did not recognize his desire to be an artist. This is similar to the story of the schizophrenic Eduard, which thereby acquires a particularly autobiographical character.
# Action
The novel opens with Veronica's suicide attempt with an overdose of sleeping pills. While waiting for her death, she happens to notice a newspaper comment by the writer Coelho: "Where is Slovenia?" Veronika decides to write a reader's letter to the newspaper before her death, as she is annoyed that no one knows her home country Slovenia. While writing the letter, her first doubts about the validity of her suicide arise, but soon after, the sleeping pills begin to work. She wakes up a few days later in the notorious madhouse "Villete". During a visit to the infirmary, she is told that the sleeping pills have caused heart failure and that she has only a few days to live. For Veronika, knowing that she will die in a few days is far worse than knowing that she will die in a few minutes. Now she's doing everything she can to get medication so she doesn't have to wait so long.
In the following days, Veronika makes the acquaintance of various patients, through whose experiences she gradually learns to recognize herself and increasingly regains the will to live. Her fate of imminent death and the life-energy it awakens also inspire the other patients to reflect on their lives and even make some of them want to leave the institution. Meanwhile, shortly before her predicted death, Veronika falls in love with the schizophrenic Eduard, with whom she flees from Villete to spend the evening of her life together. But the next day, Veronika is still alive.
It turns out that the attending physician and head of the clinic, Dr. Igor, induced symptoms of heart attacks in Veronika by regular injections to make her believe that she was about to die. He hoped to obtain evidence for his own studies of mental illness, which were based on the idea of a poison, which he named Vitriol (bitterness) and which could only be fought with the awareness of life (evoked by the awareness of death). Dr. Igor's approach is thus revealed in the final part of the novel as an unorthodox therapeutic trick designed to take the bitterness and fatigue of life from his patient Veronika and thereby prevent her from repeating her suicide attempt.
