In the ancient Egyptian city of Thebes in 3067 B.C., a fierce warrior known as the Scorpion King led his army on an ambitious campaign to conquer the known world. However, after seven years of fighting, the Scorpion King and his army were defeated and exiled to the desert of Ahm Shere. One by one, they died of starvation, leaving only the Scorpion King. To survive, the latter made a pact with the evil god of the dead, Anubis: he would erect for him a magnificent temple, a golden pyramid, as well as surrender his soul in exchange for the power to defeat his enemies. Anubi spared his life, creating an oasis where he could build the Pyramid and deliver the Scorpion King the Army of Anubi (an invincible legion of anthropomorphic warriors with the head of a jackal). Anubis' army spread throughout Egypt, destroying everything in its path, and once it was done, Anubis took the soul of King Scorpion, and returned "his warriors to the sands whence they came".
5,000 years later, in 1933, Evelyn Carnahan and Rick O'Connell are exploring a lost temple with their son, Alex. Inside, they discover the mythological Bracelet of Anubis. When Rick and Evelyn risk drowning after reading a cursed inscription on their bracelet, Alex encounters three looters who flee as the walls begin to collapse. Alex then unintentionally causes a series of columns to collapse, thus helping his mother and father escape. Back in London, curious young Alex accidentally wears the Bracelet, which gives him a mystical vision of the oasis of Ahm Shere. Since that day coincides with the beginning of the year of the Scorpion, Alex has seven days to reach the oasis or the bracelet will kill him on the eighth day when the sun's rays hit the pyramid; at which point the Scorpion King and his terrible army will be awakened and move to conquer the World.
Alex is later captured by a mysterious cult that has resurrected Imhotep: their goal is to use Imhotep's unique and incomparable powers to defeat the Scorpion King, which will give him command over the Army of Anubi. The cult, led by Baltus Hafez, the curator of the British Museum, includes a psychopathic warrior named Lock-Nah and Meela Nais, the reincarnation of Imhotep's old love, Anck-su-Namun. The O'Connell's head off to rescue Alex, accompanied by Evelyn's brother Jonathan, their old friend, the Medjai Ardeth Bay, and Izzy, an old fellow adventurer of Rick's, now a helicopter pilot, who provides transportation.
Alex on Imothep's orders is kept under the watch of Lock-Nah who is repeatedly teased by the child at every opportunity so much so that the man tired of not being able to kill Alex since Imothep would kill him if he tried he promises to kill the child the moment his master no longer needs the child's help. Everywhere Alex is taken, he leaves clues about his next destination so his parents can find him. Ardeth sends messages to the army of her fellow Medjai, intent on stopping Anubi's army if it awakens. Along the way, the O'Connells learn the connection to Imhotep and the Scorpion King himself: in a past life, Evelyn was Nefertiri (vaguely inspired by the historical Queen Nefertari), daughter of Seti I and protector of the Bracelet of Anubis. Rick is therefore destined to be a Medjai, tasked with protecting Evelyn. Together with their son Alex, who is the guide for Ahm Shere, they represent the three sides of a pyramid. Meanwhile, Imhotep brings Anck-su-Namun's soul back from the realm of the dead and places it in Meela's body, bringing her back to full life.
When the two groups arrive at the oasis where the Scorpion King's tomb lies, the cultists are attacked by mummified pygmies who are also stalking Rick, Evelyn, Jonathan, and Ardeth. The cultists are almost completely exterminated, with the exception of Hafez, their leader, who lets most of his followers die. Lock-Nah after attempting to kill Alex in retaliation for the child's insults is stopped and killed by Ardeth, who leaves the group to take command of the Medjai army. Rick rescues Alex and manages to get him to the pyramid just before the sun hits it, and there Alex finally manages to remove the Bracelet. However, when Jonathan and Evelyn reach them, Anck-su-Namun enters the courtyard of the pyramid with Imhotep and kills Evelyn with a knife. The treacherous Hafez steals the bracelet and uses it to free the Scorpion King and release the Army of Anubis, but as a price for doing so, his arm is disembodied.
Imhotep's powers are taken from him by Anubi, at the entrance to the Pyramid of Ahm Shere, forcing him to fight against the Scorpion King as a mortal. Rick enters the temple when Imhotep calls back the Scorpion King, now in the form of a half-scorpion, half-human monster. Imhotep fakes an alliance with the Scorpion King, who then focuses attention on Rick, and brutally kills Hafez when he encounters him. Meanwhile, Jonathan distracts Anck-su-Namun while Alex uses the Book of the Dead to resurrect his mother; Evelyn, summoned from the Underworld and recalling the ancient martial arts of her past life, then fights against Anck-su-Namun. Meanwhile, Ardeth and the remnants of the Medjai army defeat the first wave of Anubis warriors, only to discover that what they defeated was the vanguard, and now the full strength of Anubis' Army is about to overwhelm them. Outnumbered, the Medjai prepare to fight to the death.
Rick's battle against the demigod Scorpion King is almost lost, but then he sees inscriptions on the Temple wall, depicting a man with a tattoo on his wrist that matches his own. The illustrations reveal that the Scorpion King can only be killed by the Spear of Osiris (which Jonathan has unknowingly carried with him as a trivial walking stick throughout the film). Although Jonathan's attempt to kill the Scorpion King is thwarted by Imhotep, who takes the spear and throws it himself at the Scorpion King, Rick manages to intercept it, and stab it into the Scorpion King's chest. He then commands them to return to the underworld (him and his army), turning both the Scorpion King and the Army of Anubis into sand, one second before they hit the Medjai lines.
Rick and Imhotep are now attempting to escape the collapsing temple. But a crack appears that leads to the afterlife, and both Rick and Imhotep fall inside, but they manage to hold on to the edge. Evelyn enters the room and manages to save Rick, but Anck-su-Namun lacks the courage to do the same for Imhotep. Shocked and heartbroken, Imhotep chooses to fall into the fissure, having no reason to live anymore, now that his beloved for whom he sacrificed everything has abandoned him. Meanwhile, when fleeing, Anck-su-Namun accidentally falls into a hole full of carnivorous beetles, where she is eaten to death. The O'Connells reach the top of the pyramid and Izzy arrives with a modified airship and saves the O'Connells just before the oasis and the pyramid are completely destroyed by being sucked up by the desert sands; Jonathan just before climbing onto the airship as the final act grabs the large diamond placed on top of the pyramid. The four set off for the sunset, with Ardeth Bay bidding them farewell before departing.

Her son asks to talk to her and the two get more and more scared and panicked.
The son's phone call is dropped. Marta calls the police who ask her several questions and then tell her to come in and make a report. She asks them if they can trace the call and they repeat that she must come in to make a report. Marta, now frustrated and angry, resolves to drive to France to look for her son. She leaves the apartment, but as she is going down the stairs the phone rings again.
It is her son. She asks him to describe the beach or anything he might have seen going there. She tells him to start walking down the beach, but her mother says that he should stay where he is. In the midst of this conversation, he tells her that an unknown man has arrived. He tells Marta that the man is alone and is seen relieving himself. The man is waving the boy over and her son reports being scared and that he does not want to talk to the man.
Marta tells him to run. She tells him to run and hide, which he does. He tells her that the man is looking for him, and then Marta hears the man's voice asking the son a question before the phone call is dropped again. Marta leaves the apartment. The film ends with a brief shot of a deserted beach.
option_1_text:
Maria and José Ribeiro are a Portuguese couple now perfectly integrated in the French capital, where they work without problems. Upon the death of José's brother, it is discovered that the couple can inherit a large inheritance but only if they decide to permanently return to Portugal also to safeguard the continuity of the family business.
All the people close to the couple and who have always taken advantage of their kindness try in every way to prevent them from leaving.
option_2_text:
Mary Lennox is being raised by a nanny in India. Disregarded by her parents and shunned by the servants, she grows up there. When a cholera epidemic breaks out, both Mary's parents and their nanny die. The orphan is then taken to her uncle and current guardian, Archibald Craven, on his estate Misselthwaite in England. He's been described as very evil and mean.
The journey from London to Misselthwaite she makes in the care of Mrs. Medlock, the housekeeper at Misselthwaite Castle. It becomes apparent that Mary's dislike of her is based on reciprocity.
Mary's uncle behaves much like her parents: He is rarely at home, shows no interest in her, but makes sure that she has everything she needs. Have Martha, the maid, take care of Mary.
Since there are no toys, and since Mary can't find the big library in the huge house, the only option she has is to play outside. The fresh air does her good, and gradually the girl, who was at first weak, ugly, and selfish, becomes a beautiful and kind creature.
One day, as she walks in the garden, she discovers a locked and overgrown gate in a wall. Behind it is a secret garden that has been closed for ten years. Mr. Craven had planted it with his now-deceased wife; after her death he had it locked up and made wild. But Mary secretly takes care of her secret garden with Dickon, Martha's brother.
On a stormy night, she discovers her cousin Colin, Mr. Craven's son, hidden by the employees. Because everyone believes the boy will die soon, his every wish will be granted. He's become a spoiled brat that his father doesn't want to know about because he reminds him too much of his beloved deceased wife. Mary befriends him, but she also gives him her opinion.
With Mary's help, Colin learns to walk; until now it was thought that the boy was paralyzed. Mary tells him about the secret garden and he wants to see it.
In the garden, Mary, Colin, and Dickon are playing around, tending the plants and doing gymnastics; but in the house, Colin is playing the deathly ill, wanting to surprise his father when he returns from one of his journeys by being able to walk. Finally, Mr Craven returns from his long journey to Misselthwaite because of a dream and a letter from Dickens' mother. He meets his son in the garden and the two of them go back to the mansion together.
option_3_text:
The film depicts the life of physician Patch Adams and is based on his book Good Health Is a Laughing Matter.
After a suicide attempt, Hunter "Patch" Adams volunteers to be admitted to a psychiatric hospital. There he learns that helping other people can distract him from his own problems. The highly intelligent Adams thus gains his attitude of a good quality of life as the best remedy and gets the desire to become a doctor.
After leaving the clinic prematurely at his own request, he began studying medicine. Although the study regulations forbid him to have contact with patients before his third year, he does not care about it and keeps going back to the hospital, where he manages to restore the good mood of dying patients. He is repeatedly admonished by the head of the hospital, repeatedly threatened with expulsion from the study.
After an experience with a woman who cannot witness her daughter's last moments because she has to take care of her health insurance first, Adams makes the decision to build a clinic where you do not have to pay and where everyone is both patient and doctor at the same time. This he builds together with his fellow students Carin Fisher and Truman Schiff in a cabin in the wilderness. He mostly treats patients who can't be admitted anywhere else.
A love develops between Adams and Carin Fisher, which comes to an abrupt end when Carin is killed by one of these patients with a shotgun. Adams is so angry and sad about this that he wants to end it first. Eventually, however, he regains his old optimism and his old life and helps the patient to find joy again. However, his nonconformity eventually leads to Dean Walcott excluding him from the study. Adams steals his personnel files in front of him, which is strictly forbidden, and studies them with Truman. There's a big hearing in front of the university senate where Adams explains his motives and pathetically propagates his goals. The expulsion is rejected, in the end Adams can finish his studies and make his doctorate. At the awarding of the doctorate by Dr. Eaton, Adams shows that he has retained some of his nonconformity, as he has modified his robe so that one can see his naked rear.
option_4_text: Strange disappearances predict the presence of a monster in the neighborhood where the protagonist of the film is located. As in the first episode, this is a specimen of a genetically altered insect, capable of assuming a near-human appearance by blending in with the darkness' favor.

query_text:
Dr. Michael Hfuhruhurr, a widowed brain surgeon, is renowned for inventing a method of "cranial screw-top" brain surgery. He saves the life of Dolores Benedict, a gold-digging femme fatale who is accidentally run over by Michael when fleeing the scene of her latest husband's fatal coronary, caused by her malicious mind-games and scheming. As she recovers, Michael falls in love and they marry. Dolores torments Michael by pretending to be too ill to consummate the marriage, citing a continuing headache. On a honeymoon and business trip to a medical conference in Vienna, a city living in fear of the serial "Elevator Killer", Hfuhruhurr meets mad scientist Dr. Alfred Necessiter, who has created a technique enabling him to store living brains in liquid-filled jars using the Elevator Killer's victims.
Michael discovers he can communicate telepathically with one of Necessiter's brains, that of Anne Uumellmahaye, when they both sing Under the Bamboo Tree.  Michael and Anne fall in love, with Michael taking her brain away to spend more time with her. Dolores—having learned that Michael has received a large inheritance from his step-grandmother—attempts to reignite their relationship, but catches on to his relationship with Anne when she spots him in a rowboat with the jar. She attempts to kill Anne by putting her brain in an oven, causing Michael to literally toss Dolores out of his house.
Michael consults with Necessiter, who informs him that brains in tanks do not survive long, with Anne being his longest-living one to date. Necessiter recommends transplanting Anne's brain into a body of a recently-deceased woman, revealing that he has perfected a process that could allow him to do so. Filling a syringe with window cleaner, the substance used by the Elevator Killer, Michael sees a crowd gathering around an attractive woman hit by a car, and is seen as odd for hoping she will expire, only to see her regain consciousness. Michael next selects Fran—a prostitute with an annoying voice—but his conscience prevents him from killing her. Stepping into an elevator, he finds that Dolores has just been murdered by the Elevator Killer, who turns out to be Merv Griffin. Michael takes Dolores' corpse, and Griffin promises to turn himself in to the police.
Michael hurriedly takes Dolores's body to Necessiter's lab. He is stopped by the Austrian police, who suspect him of drunk driving. After a series of unusual sobriety tests, the police permit him to leave. However, as Dolores' body flails, the police realize that she was not drunk, but dead, and pursue his car. Michael makes it to the lab, where Necessiter transfers Anne's consciousness to Dolores's body, which is viewed by the stunned policemen. In the process, Michael is electrically shocked by the equipment and falls into a coma.
Waking up six weeks later, Michael meets Anne in Dolores's body. Anne is a compulsive eater, and has gained considerable weight in her new body. Michael loves Anne for who she is, and they get married. A note in the credits reports that Merv Griffin did not turn himself in as promised and requests that the audience report the whereabouts of Griffin if they see him.
option_0_text:
Cantinflas goes to the house of his girlfriend, Paz (Dolores Camarillo) who works as a maid in a mansion, to dine for free, as she has done for a long time. While waiting, another man also arrives to enter the house, and drops his wallet in the process, which Cantinflas picks up as he enters the house. After entering, however, Cantinflas this time has to earn dinner: Paz asks him to kill the family's dog, who is sick with rabies. Seeing his hesitation, Paz stands firm: if he doesn't kill the dog, he can't eat. Cantinflas is nervous about the idea, but eventually kills the dog with a gun.
The owner of the house, Cayetano Lastre (Joaquín Pardavé), suspects the infidelity of his wife, Dolores del Paso (Sofía Álvarez), and prepares an unexpected arrival at his house, with police as witnesses, to be able to divorce. During her husband's absence, Dolores lets into the house the individual who has been prowling outside: her former youth boyfriend, Bobby Lechuga, a swindler who plans to blackmail her in exchange for not showing some undated letters to her husband that make him believe of his infidelity. Dolores wants the letters back, but the blackmailer doesn't settle for money to do so, seeking to renew his relationship with her. When they go up to the bedroom, Cayetano arrives, accompanied by the police. At the same time, the maid is frightened by the sudden arrival of the owner of the house, and hides Cantinflas in a closet. Cayetano and the police discover Cantinflas hiding in the closet, but Dolores makes her husband believe that Cantinflas is Leonardo del Paso, her lost brother. Since his father-in-law (the father of Dolores and Leonardo) needed the presence of all the heirs to read and distribute his inheritance, Cayetano (who has business problems lately) begins to treat Cantinflas like a king to gain his trust and benefit from his father-in-law's inheritance. Cantinflas is taking advantage of the situation.
After having adopted Cantinflas as his brother-in-law, Cayetano publishes an advertisement in the newspaper to gather the heirs and proceed to the distribution of his father-in-law's fortune. This announcement causes Leonardo's concubine, Clotilde Regalado (Sara García) to arrive at Cayetano's house with all her children, not caring that the supposed Leonardo del Paso is not the real one. Upon learning of the irregular civil status of Leonardo and his wife, Cayetano intends to marry them, but Cantinflas is saved by the arrival of the police, who are preparing to arrest him because, confusing him with Leonardo, he is wanted for the murder of Bobby. Confusion arises when Cantinflas admits to killing Bobby (the dog, not the gangster), exacerbated by the fact that Bobby's wallet (which Cantinflas originally picked up) is found among his clothes, for which he is arrested and prosecuted.
In a lengthy courtroom sequence, Cantinflas again confesses to killing Bobby, the rabid dog, but as almost everyone in court sees him as Leonardo brazenly confessing to the murder of Bobby the con man, he is inevitably found guilty and sentenced to the death penalty. In the end, the whole matter is cleared up when Leonardo del Paso, Dolores' real brother, appears among the assisting audience and explains about Bobby's blackmail and that he killed the extortionist in self-defense. Cantinflas is completely acquitted and returns to his old antics, waiting outside Cayetano's mansion for Paz's whistle at dinner time and then entering the kitchen to eat.
option_1_text: It's the doctor. Michel Hfuhruhurr is a luminary in brain surgery. A widower, he is seduced by the beautiful Dolores who induces him to marry her, except then immediately after revealing the anything but noble feelings that animate him. Hfuhruhurr, during one of his frequent international medical conferences, meets the quirky Dr. Needing me to secretly keep a varied collection of "still-living human brains" in the lab. It will be with one of these brains that Hfuhruhurr will discover that he is particularly attuned, that of a woman named Anne Uumellmahaye, with whom he will fall in love by exchanging their thoughts telepathically.
option_2_text: An Indian, fed up with the miserable life he and his kind are condemned to live on reservations, organizes a march to the nearest town to protest. Others will join his initiative.
option_3_text:
A king named Milluccio once saw a dead raven on stone, and fell in love with the thought of a wife as black as the raven, as red as its blood, and as white as the stone.  It affected his health until his brother Jennariello asked what was wrong with him and finally learned the story.  Jennariello set out by ship.  He bought a falcon and a splendid horse, and a beggar persuaded him to tell his story.  The beggar then begged at a magician's house, and Jennariello saw that the magician's daughter, Liviella, matched his brother's dream exactly.  Jennariello dressed as a peddler and showed Liviella hoods, handkerchiefs, and other goods, and persuaded her to come to the ship to see his better wares.  Then he sailed off with her.  Liviella lamented, but Jennariello told her why, and described his brother to her so vividly that she wanted to see this man.
On the voyages, two doves flew up.  They talked, and one told the other that the falcon would pick out Milluccio's eyes the first time it saw him, but if Jennariello warned him, or did not bring him the bird, Jennariello would turn to marble; that the horse would break Milluccio's neck the first time he rode it, but if Jennariello warned him, or did not bring him the horse, he would turn to marble; and that a dragon would eat Milluccio and Liviella on their wedding night, but if Jennariello warned him, or did not bring him Liviella, Jennariello would turn to stone.
Jennariello brought his brother the horse and the falcon and then instantly killed them.  At the wedding night, Jennariello went with a sword and fought the dragon, but when his brother woke, the dragon vanished, and he had Jennariello imprisoned as a traitor that night and sentenced to die the next.  Wishing to die known as innocent, he told Milluccio his story, and turned to stone.
Liviella had twin sons.  One day, while she was gone, an old man asked Milluccio what he would give to restore his brother.  Milluccio said his kingdom, and when told life was needed, offered his own; when the old man said his sons' lives were needed, he killed them and put the blood on the statue, which restored Jennariello.  Liviella returned and was grief-stricken, and went to the window to throw herself out.  The old man, her father, stopped her, and told her that he had punished them all for their acts against him, but the punishment had been enough.  He restored the babies to life.
option_4_text:
Debbie and Peter, who met on a one-night stand, are two twenty-somethings from Los Angeles, whose goals are to become a successful editor and a successful writer, respectively.
Twenty years later they remain great friends, however, things have changed a lot: Debbie is divorced and has a 13-year-old son named Jack full of allergies and no friends, while Peter has a great job and is a stubborn womanizer.
In addition, he moved to New York, as he was too embittered after Debbie's pregnancy (having fallen in love with her without ever revealing it), inventing the excuse of having left because of the earthquakes.
Debbie has to go to New York to take an exam so she can get a promotion, and after Jack's babysitter turns out to be unavailable, Peter, recently fired, offers to take care of him.
So the two friends move into each other's houses.
Peter (aware of the difficulties of being without a father) begins to build a relationship with Jack, helping him overcome his insecurities and make friends, while Debbie finds a manuscript of his friend in his apartment and decides to publish it without consulting him. This brings her closer to the charming writer Theo, with whom she spends a night at Peter's house, under the latter's gaze through surveillance cameras. During their time apart, the two begin to reflect on their relationship, realizing that they love each other. One day, during a hockey game, Jack crashes and ends up in the hospital. Debbie, upon discovering this, breaks off the relationship with Theo, decides to return to Los Angeles, asking Peter to leave. The two meet at the airport and, after an initial quarrel, declare to each other.
Six months later, it turns out that Peter has become a great writer, Debbie a renowned editor, and the two of them with Jack are now a family.

query_text: Thirty-year-old Brice is a son by profession and lives in his father's villa in Nice. He regularly throws large parties for supposed friends and lives, inspired by the film Dangerous Sailing, for surfing, although there are no waves in Nice. After his father is arrested for money laundering and his assets are confiscated, Brice is forced to make his own living. His attempts to work in a restaurant and rob a bank, however, fail. He meets Marius, who has only one toe. The two go to the town of Hossegor to participate in a surfing competition. With the prize money of $100,000, Brice wants to fund his living expenses, and Marius plans to use it to pay for a foot operation. Although Brice has no chance in the contest, he finally gets to surf his long-awaited "perfect wave" and meets his female double, Alice de Nice. Marius falls in love with the girl Jeanne, who has huge ears herself, and wants to travel the world with her.
option_0_text:
In San Jose, California, David Kim looks at old photographs and videos of his daughter Margot and his late wife Pamela, who died of lymphoma about two years earlier, an episode that gradually caused David and Margot to drift apart. One night Margot goes to a friend's house for her study group; while David sleeps, Margot tries to call him three times. The next morning, David is unable to contact Margot either by phone or via chat, but he doesn't care as he assumes that she left early and went to school. He later calls Margot's piano teacher, who informs him that Margot stopped going to piano lessons six months earlier. David discovers that Margot pocketed the money for the lessons and then transferred $2,500 to an account on the Venmo platform, which was deleted soon after. Realizing that Margot is missing, David calls the police; the case is assigned to Detective Rosemary Vick, who asks for information about Margot's personality and friendships. David manages to access Margot's Facebook profile and talk to her contacts, but discovers that her daughter has had no close friends since her mother's death. Vick calls to report that Margot has obtained a fake driver's license and shows him surveillance camera footage showing Margot at a highway intersection outside of town, suggesting that she may have run away voluntarily.
David, not convinced, discovers that Margot has used a vlogging site called YouCast and has often spoken to a working girl nicknamed "fish_n_chips". Vick investigates this and reports that fish_n_chips is innocent, having been spotted at work in Pittsburgh around the time Margot supposedly disappeared. From Margot's Instagram, David discovers that he has frequently visited Barbosa Lake, which is located near the highway junction, so he goes to the lake and finds Margot's keychain on the ground. The police arrive and discover Margot's car underwater with an envelope inside containing $2,500 in cash. Extensive searches are initiated around the lake with volunteers, but a storm slows the progress. Margot's body, however, is never found. David examines the crime scene photographs and notices his brother Peter's jacket in the car. Reading the chat between Peter and Margot he discovers that uncle and niece were having some kind of relationship, so he buys micro cameras and installs them in his brother's house; Peter notices this and, after a determined request for explanations from David (who had misunderstood the relationship between brother and daughter), explains that they were smoking marijuana together and accuses David of being an absent father because he did not realize that his daughter was suffering from loneliness due to the loss of her mother.
The meeting is interrupted when Vick calls David, telling him that an ex-con named Randy Cartoff confessed in an online video to raping and killing Margot. A memorial service is arranged for Margot. As David is uploading the photos to a funeral video service, he notices that the website's stock photo features the same woman as fish_n_chips' profile picture. David, after a brief search, discovers that the girl in the picture is a model who sells her image to companies online, which implies that the "fish_n_chips" account is a false identity and that therefore Detective Vick (who had said she heard the girl typing behind fish_n_chips) lied. Attempting to call her to report this, David talks to a colleague of the detective who reveals that she had volunteered to support the case, rather than being assigned to it, as she had claimed. David searches for Vick using Google and discovers that he knew Cartoff through a volunteer program for ex-convicts. He reports all this to the sheriff, who arrests Rosemary Vick while she is at the memorial service for the girl.
A few days later, Vick agrees to confess to the murder and other crimes in exchange for clemency for his son Robert, who has behavioral problems and was using the YouCast site to get close to Margot, having been attracted to her since elementary school. When Margot sent him $2,500, thinking that Robert was a working girl whose mother was hospitalized with cancer (as happened to Margot's mother), Robert felt guilty and decided to meet Margot at the lake; during the meeting Margot got scared and ran away, and Robert, trying to reach her to explain himself, inadvertently made Margot fall into a fifteen-meter deep gorge. Robert, in a panic, called his mother who tried to cover up the accident by pushing the car into the lake, creating a fake driver's license and then claiming to have verified the alibi of the girl with nick fish_n_chips in Pittsburgh. When David subsequently found the car, thus dropping the story of his daughter's escape, Vick was forced to alter the plan by putting Cartoff in the middle, making him a scapegoat and possibly killing him.
As Vick is taken to prison, David asks her where Margot's body is; Vick replies that Margot is in the ravine and that even if she had survived the fall, she could not have lived without water for five days. David tells the police to go check, pointing out that on the third day there was a thunderstorm that could have provided Margot with water. In the ravine, the rescue team finds Margot badly injured but alive. Two years later a rehabilitated Margot awaits acceptance of her application to the Conservatory to study piano. Photos and chats show that the relationship between David and Margot, now, has greatly improved.
option_1_text:
Terry Benedict locates all eleven members of Danny Ocean's crew, demanding they return the $160 million they stole from his casinos plus $38 million in interest. He gives Danny's crew a two-week deadline to return it.
Short by half the amount, the group schemes to stage a heist in Amsterdam to avoid problems with U.S. authorities. They are tipped off by an informant named Matsui about the location of the first stock certificate ever issued. After a complex series of schemes, they find the document has already been stolen by master thief the "Night Fox".
Europol detective Isabel Lahiri is called in to investigate the theft and realizes that she gave Rusty the idea of how to solve a complication of the heist with a description of a similar burglary during their earlier relationship. Surprising the group at their accommodations, she warns them they cannot beat the Night Fox or his mentor, the mysterious master thief "LeMarc", both of whom excel in the "long con", and steals Rusty's phone. She has been hunting both for years.
Danny and his crew discover that the Night Fox is François Toulour, a wealthy French baron and gentleman thief with a villa on Lake Como. Danny goes to the villa and steals Toulour's paintings. He confronts Toulour, who reveals that he had exposed their identities to Benedict (breaking the code of silence among thieves) and hired Matsui to inform the crew about the stock certificate to arrange the meeting with Danny.
Toulour is upset when LeMarc suggested Danny may be a better thief than him, so challenges Danny to steal the Imperial Coronation Fabergé Egg. If Danny and his crew win, Toulour will pay off the debt to Benedict.
The crew begin to plan an elaborate heist to swap the egg for a holographic recreation, but Toulour gives the camera recordings from his villa to Lahiri, who deduces that they want to steal the egg through an intercepted phone call to Rusty. She then captures most of the crew except Linus, Tarr, Turk, and Saul.
Linus comes up with a second plan involving Danny's wife, Tess, posing as a pregnant Julia Roberts in order to get close to the egg and swap it. They are foiled by Lahiri and a coincidentally present Bruce Willis, and the rest of the group members are captured. Lahiri is told that they are to be extradited to the U.S., while Linus is chosen first to be interrogated by the FBI agent assigned to collect them.
The agent is actually Linus's mother, who organizes the release of the whole gang. She points out to Lahiri that she will face consequences for forging a signature on a Europol form to obtain the necessary arrest warrants for Ocean's gang.
Sometime later, Danny and Tess return to Toulour's villa, where Toulour reveals his glee at their failure. He explains that he stole the egg at night using his agility and dancing skills to evade the museum's heavy security. Toulour's celebration is short-lived when Danny reveals that his group stole the real egg while it was in transit to the museum, and Toulour realizes they were tipped off by LeMarc.
A flashback reveals that Danny and Rusty had met LeMarc earlier when he revealed his confidence trick intended to humiliate Toulour and, at the same time, restore to himself the Fabergé egg that he had stolen years ago but returned following his wife's wishes. Toulour is forced to admit that Danny won the bet and gives him the money for the debt to Benedict.
As the crew pay back Benedict and promise not to perform any more heists in his casinos,  Toulour is seen in the background spying on him. Rusty takes Lahiri to a safe house that he claims has been lent to him by LeMarc. There, she is reunited with her father, who is revealed to be the man she has been pursuing for years: LeMarc.
option_2_text:
The film opens with a panicked 9-1-1 call along with visuals indicating that the four main cast members—Robbie, Angela, Scott, and Michelle—are missing. A title card explains that the subsequent footage was recovered from three memory cards found in the Mojave Desert.
Robbie is an aspiring filmmaker living in Los Angeles who has recruited his brother Scott and his friend Angela to help film a music video for his friend Michelle in the Mojave Desert. While getting ready for the expedition, he celebrates his brother's birthday, surprises his mother back home, parties with Angela, and talks to Michelle about her recently-deceased mother. Footage filmed from Robbie's apartment of two separate earthquakes is also shown.
The four friends pack their equipment and begin their journey, spending the first night at a small lake. They continue deeper into the desert the next day and encounter a pack of donkeys blocking the road. They arrive at their final location, a small hillside area near a dried-up lakebed, and begin setting up camp. At night, the four are awakened by booming sounds and frantic animal noises that appear to be getting closer. Scott and Robbie leave their tent to investigate but find no clues. Robbie continues by himself and sees a strobing light along a hillside path.
The next day, the crew discuss the uncanny events of the previous evening and begin filming the video. During a break, Robbie and Michelle investigate the area where he saw the light and record high-pitched noises coming from a nearby hole, sensing something unusual beneath the earth. Robbie remarks that his camera battery has not gone down the entire time they’ve been there. Later, Robbie sees an axe at the top of a nearby hill. The crew head to the lakebed to finish filming the video, and the sound is overtaken by noises similar to the ones heard earlier in the hole. At night, the crew once again hear the booms and animal sounds. Robbie wanders off and sees a naked man on a hill wielding the axe. As he runs away, the man attacks Robbie off screen, giving him a head injury. Robbie returns to camp, bloody and disoriented, and finds Scott asleep but the women frantic.
The camera cuts to Robbie running through the desert as the two girls scream and plead for their lives. He encounters Scott and Angela, both soaked in blood. Robbie escapes and takes shelter in a small ravine until morning. He exits, naked and disoriented, and starts wandering the desert aimlessly. He finds that the area is now infested with screaming, fleshy, worm-like creatures. That night, he returns to the campsite to find the two tents covered in viscera and sees what appears to be Michelle's body. After a number of close calls with his assailant, Robbie is transported to a pool of red liquid by the light. He is taken back to the desert, vomits blood, and removes an unknown substance from his foot. He encounters the pack of donkeys, then sees himself and his three friends walking through the desert from when they first arrived. He sees a blood-soaked Michelle running across the lakebed and chases her. He encounters a bloodied Scott and Angela, acting normally, at the campsite. Exiting the tent, he finds himself at his mother's house and then on the wing of a plane, where he sees Scott through the window.
Back in the desert, in total darkness, Robbie runs into a large monster, which closely inspects him and appears to be calling to similar creatures in the distance. He runs away and sees Angela back at camp, and the two are attacked by the worms. Robbie is carried by an unseen force that transports him back into the red liquid, and the camera is shown rapidly flying through a series of white lights before returning to the desert. Robbie finds a gas mask and an old sign indicating that he is in a government-restricted area and encounters his assailant, who appears to be his doppelgänger. The next day, Robbie finds the decomposing heads of his three companions impaled on pikes. He then finds the tooth of a large animal on the ground. He uses it to sever his penis and then disembowels himself. The film ends with a shot of a fatally wounded Robbie reaching toward the sky.
option_3_text: A sister and brother try to survive in the wilds of British Columbia after a plane crash.
option_4_text:
Brice Agostini, a cocksure and wealthy but also child-like grown man with a Point Break obsession, lives an idle life in Nice, spending his days in the sea with a surf board waiting for a wave. Even though Nice lies on a completely waveless bay on the Mediterranean Sea, Brice hopes that one day a tidal wave will hit as one did in 1979. In the evenings, he hosts massive parties in his luxury property where he defeats all challengers in "casse" (witty put-downs) competitions. He also likes to seduce women but does not appear to know what to do with them. He dreams regularly of finding love with a mermaid.
Reality hits when his father is arrested for money-laundering and all his belongings repossessed. His friends desert him and Brice - who can barely read - has to try his hand, for the first time, at making a living. He proves terrible at it, and after getting fired from a restaurant, attempts instead to rob a bank while wearing a mask of Jacques Chirac in the manner depicted in Point Break. He ends up in hospital, manacled to a bed, next to Marius, a motorcycle thief that he tried to get an escape ride from. Marius is equally child-like, struggling even to speak, and the two bond quickly. They escape in an absurd manner and steal a lorry belonging to the wife of Brice's father's lawyer.
Marius, believing Brice's endless boasts, drives him to Hossegor where a surfing competition is scheduled. Marius begs Brice to take part and share the prize money with him as he needs it for an expensive operation: instead of feet, each of his legs ends with a giant single toe. Brice agrees, touched by his plight and also too embarrassed to confess that he has never actually surfed. In the days leading to the competition, Brice makes new friends thanks to his party animal skills, and clashes with the local champion, Igor. Marius meanwhile, who has stolen a surf board for Brice to compete with, is caught by the behatted saleswoman, Jeanne, who blackmails him into working on her boat. Jeanne's attraction to Marius scares him as he is terrified of his condition coming to light, but after Brice simply explains the situation to her, she shows Marius that his feet do not bother her, and reveals that she has equally freaky giant ears, which she normally conceals.
Brice's fantasies are finally quashed on competition day: he knocks himself out with his board on the first wave and has to be rescued. In a vision, the Bodhi character from Point Break tells him that "dreaming your life is not the same as living your dream". Brice apologises to Marius for letting him down but his friend has forgotten all about getting operated on and now plans to go sailing around the world with Jeanne.
In an epilogue, Brice now works as a humble beach cleaner back in Nice, but the freak wave he hoped for does one day turn up and he manages to jump into it. Regaining consciousness on the ground, he is joined by a female wannabe surfer dressed exactly like him who has missed the wave: Alice from Nice. She is the mermaid from his dreams.

query_text: When a violinist returns to his home town after fifteen years away he strikes up a relationship with an old flame who is now working as a nurse.
option_0_text:
Professor Larry Donner and his student Owen have one thing in common: the women in their lives drive them crazy. Larry's wife, Margaret Donner, stole his novel and turned it into a bestseller.
Owen's mother, a bitter old woman, makes his life a living hell. However, Owen came up with an idea to kill two birds with one stone: he would kill Margaret and Larry would kill his mother. Two unrelated crimes. Yet when Margaret is murdered, Larry, who knew nothing of it, is left with no alibi and makes the perfect murderer. He finds himself forced to kill Owen's mother, which isn't an easy task, because the old lady is tough.
option_1_text:
The world-famous violinist Nils Ascan returns to his hometown Korby for the first time in 15 years for a concert. Here he rekindles his love for his former girlfriend Helga, who now works as a head nurse in a hospital. Ascan persuades Helga to go with him for a new life at his side. Against all the intense warnings of her friends and colleagues, she chooses Ascan over her position at the hospital.
After a short time, however, her best friend Agnes struggles with life after a suicide attempt. Helga feels partly responsible for this incident and rushes back to the hospital despite Ascan's violent protests. She assists in the successful operation. Helga realizes that her place is in the medical college and decides not to return to Ascan, but to stay in the hospital.
option_2_text:
Lieutenant Jake "Cool Hand" Grafton (Brad Johnson) and his bombardier/navigator and best friend Lieutenant Morgan "Morg" McPherson (Christopher Rich) are flying a Grumman A-6 Intruder during the Vietnam War over the Gulf of Tonkin towards North Vietnam. They hit their target, a 'suspected truck park', which actually turns out to be trees. On the return to carrier, Morg is fatally shot in the neck by an armed Vietnamese peasant. Landing on the USS Independence with Morg dead, a disturbed Jake, covered in blood, walks into a debriefing with Commander Frank Camparelli (Danny Glover) and Executive Officer, Commander "Cowboy" Parker (J. Kenneth Campbell). Camparelli tells Jake to put Morgan's death behind him and to write a letter to Sharon, Morg's wife. New pilot Jack Barlow (Jared Chandler), nicknamed "Razor" because of his youthful appearance, is then introduced.
Lieutenant Commander Virgil Cole (Willem Dafoe) arrives on board and reports to Camparelli, who later tells Jake's roommate Sammy Lundeen (Justin Williams) to take Jake, Bob "Boxman" Walkawitz (Tom Sizemore) and "Mad Jack" (Dann Florek) to fly into Subic Bay the next day and help Jake unwind. Jake goes to see Sharon, but she has already departed. He runs into a woman named Callie Troy (Rosanna Arquette), who is packing Sharon's things, and they have a small, tense encounter. After an altercation with civilian merchant sailors in the Tailhook Bar, Jake runs into Callie again. After they reconcile, dance and spend the night together, she reveals her husband was a Navy pilot himself and was killed on a solo mission over Vietnam.
Jake returns to the carrier, where Camparelli confronts him regarding the bar incident, and Cole reports in Jake's favor. Cole and Jake are paired on "Iron Hand" A-6Bs loaded with Standard and Shrike anti-radiation missiles for SAM suppression. During the mission, after a successful strike, they encounter and manage to evade a North Vietnamese MiG-17.
Jake suggests to Cole that they bomb Hanoi, which would be a violation of the restrictive rules of engagement (ROE) and could get them court-martialed. Cole initially rejects the idea. On the next raid, Boxman hits the suspected target, but is shot down by another SAM and killed. The North Vietnamese in Hanoi gloat on TV over the downing of U.S. aircraft. Cole then agrees with Jake's plan to attack Hanoi, deciding to hit "SAM City", a surface-to-air missile depot.
To secure their mission, they coercively enlist the aid of the Squadron Intelligence Officer, who has been caught urinating in the commander's coffee decanter, being the Phantom Shitter who's secretly repeated this deed throughout the first half of the film. He warns Jake and Cole that there's no chance of succeeding in their mission, but he is soundly ignored.
Sent to bomb a power plant in the vicinity of Hanoi, they drop two of their Mark 83 bombs, keeping eight for the missile depot and set a new course for Hanoi for their independent bombing mission. Arriving at SAM City, on their first pass, their armament computer malfunctions and they are forced to bomb 'by hand' (guesswork), and after barely surviving a barrage of enemy fire, their bombs fail to release. The two come back around, rerun the route, successfully drop their bombs and manage to obliterate the missile depot in a spectacular display of secondary explosions. Upon returning to the carrier, Camparelli angrily chastises the pair for their independent mission and informs them of their impending court martial at the U.S. Naval Base Subic Bay. During the preliminary hearing, Cole and Grafton are criticized for their actions, and informed that their naval careers are essentially over.
The charges are dropped the next day when Operation Linebacker II is ordered by President Richard M. Nixon, and the unauthorized mission is covered up. The next day, Camparelli grounds Jake and Cole while the rest of the carrier's A-6 and A-7 crews conduct a daylight raid to destroy anti-aircraft emplacements: the tangible, lucrative targets they've longed to attack. Camparelli is hit by a ZSU-23-4 Shilka AA tank and crash lands, his bombardier dead. Sammy Lundeen is hit and has to head for the ocean. Razor is ordered by Camparelli to disengage and obeys. Jake and Cole, defying orders, man their Intruder, launch and fly one more time to assist Camparelli. They destroy the ZSU, but are forced to eject from their heavily damaged aircraft. After bailing out, Jake lands near Camparelli's crashed Intruder and runs to cover with Camparelli. Separated from Jake, Cole is mortally wounded in hand-to-hand combat with an enemy soldier. On the radio, he lies to Jake, telling him he has already gotten away. Moments later, a pair of U.S. Air Force A-1 Skyraiders ("Sandy") appear and provide cover.
Cole instructs the lead Sandy to drop ordnance on the spot he has marked with smoke. He is killed along with a few dozen NVA soldiers. Cole's final voice transmission to Sandy is: "Alpha Mike Foxtrot"! (meaning "Adios, mother f___!") Jake and Camparelli retreat into the woods, pursued by a sniper. A "Jolly Green Giant" helicopter picks up the two men, and the Skyraiders make one final napalm run to finish the job.
Later, recovering from his injuries, Jake joins his crew and Camparelli, all in their Navy whites, on deck to prepare for entry at a port of call. Jake and Camparelli reconcile their differences, and the movie ends in rolling credits.
option_3_text: In the future, scientists based in a laboratory located on the desert and inhospitable planet Xarbia, have succeeded in creating a form of life, called "Subject 20", by operating crosses between human cells and bacteria, and which should help fight against a famine that is currently hitting the galaxy. But once this creature comes out of its cocoon, it starts killing the lab staff...
option_4_text:
Framed by numerous (from the archives) flying scenes from the Western Front (eastern and northern France), the film tells a love and espionage story: the German Werner Dewall, who belongs to the flying squadron Manfred von Richthofens, has been quartered in a castle in Champagne. Here he meets the lovely Suzanne de Val, whose father, the lord of the castle, is a bitter enemy of the Germans. Both young people fall in love with each other, which calls for a sidekick to curry Suzanne's favor. To incriminate Dewall as a spy and traitor, he steals important war plans from the Germans and passes them on to the French.
Squadron leader von Richthofen then sees himself forced to intervene and sends Dewall back to the position of his unit. This separates the two lovers for the time being. The second-in-command takes advantage of the hour to smear Werner Dewall with slander at Suzanne, whereupon she actually distances herself internally from fellow pilot Richthofens. Dewall is even said to have caused her brother's alleged death. Manfred von Richthofen, however, brings the truth to light, for Dewall has even saved Brother Charles' life and can thus reunite the Franco-German couple in peace. The last scene of the film shows the solemn burial of Richthofens.

query_text:
Italy shortly after the outbreak of the First World War. Giovanni Busacca must enlist in the Italian army to escape from prison. He bribes Oreste Jacovacci to give him a reprieve, but Oreste still doesn't help him. The two men will be taken to the front by train in the same wagon. In an effort to avoid mind-numbing assignments, they add to their differences.
On the eve of the expected battle, the company moves illegally. Giovanni spends the night with the prostitute Constantina, who steals his wallet. The next day, Giovanni participates in the bloody battle, which ends with the capture of Austrian equipment. With Oreste, Giovanni is sent to the city to get supplies. He can get his wallet back from Constantina with some difficulty. He realizes that he loves the woman. Oreste and Giovanni remain in the city to escape the battle that is now taking place in their camp.
The next morning, they find out their company's been decimated. The locals welcome them, believing the two to be survivors of the battle. Giovanni and Oreste decide to defect. However, a conversation with the widow of a fallen comrade causes her to return to the company. They are sent on a special mission as messengers, but they are captured by the Austrians. They are being asked to provide information on a relief platform built by the Italians to bring in reinforcements. Giovanni, who knows where the bridge is, does not want to betray his comrades and is shot. Oreste, unaware of the bridge, is shot in a hysterical escape attempt. The Italian commander believes the two men have again tried to escape the fighting by fleeing.
option_0_text:
When Ted arrives at the museum, he prepares the reasons why he would be a good candidate to take over the museum for Mr. Bloomsberry who is retiring. However, Mr. Bloomsberry stated that Ted was the only candidate because he could not imagine not leaving Junior (the main antagonist of the first film) in possession of the museum (he is now a cashier on a parking lot). The only stipulation is that Ted has to write a presentation about his vision of what the museum would look like to be submitted to the board of directors within a week. However, Ted is afraid of the board of directors.
While Ted is in his office writing his cards, Maggie tells him that her loved ones need more attention: her, George, etc. George comes in and tries to show Ted the poster with Kayla (indicating the Piccadilly act). Ted says he understands what Maggie's saying and has decided to take George to the magic show. During one of Piccadilly's magic tricks, Kayla disappears and George goes looking for her. He finds Kayla in the basement of the theater, starts playing with her and they stumble onto the building's exit.
Piccadilly arrives and can't find Kayla, so he calls security. Danno Wolfe is in charge, assisted by Mrs. Fisher. Danno interrogates Ted and becomes suspicious of him and George. Meanwhile, George and Kayla head to Ted's apartment where they see a cover of Kayla's original home in California with her brother Tonga and sister Layla.
Ted comes home and finds George and Kayla in their apartment. He decides to return to the theater with George and Kayla, but loses them on the way when George sees an advertisement on the train for the "California Express". Ted joins them on the train, but fails to get them out of the carriage before he leaves the station. They head west and Ted gets nervous when the train doesn't even stop in St. Louis and his cell phone battery dies. Meanwhile, a mysterious message from a monkey that Danno thinks speaks Chinese leads him to believe that George and Ted have kidnapped the elephant. He starts trying to find them.
Back on the train, George opens the carriage door, but Ted falls trying to catch the pages of his paper in the wind. Ted goes to a small train station with a station manager who offers to charge the mobile phone (which broke after his fall). Ted uses the little change he called to call Piccadilly, but fails to complete the call, making Danno even more certain that Ted and George abducted Kayla. Ted uses the stationmaster's motorcycle to catch up with George and Kayla and gets back on the train. He leaves his cell phone in Humbleton with the station master who tries to use the phone to tell Piccadilly that Kayla is fine, but the phone breaks. Mrs. Fisher traced the call that allowed Danno to make his way to Humbleton Station.
Ted, George and Kayla continue on the train to the next stop in Grand Junction with Danno on their heels. Kayla's movement, however, causes the covered carriage to separate from the rest of the train, which moves away from the rest of the train. It finally stops and they go looking for a way to get help. A man in a flatbed truck pulls up and picks them up. Ted thinks they're going east, but they keep traveling west again. Meanwhile, Piccadilly is interviewed by Hark Hanson and he reveals footage of George and Ted as Kayla's kidnappers. Ted wakes up after a night of sleeping in the back of the truck and realizes they're headed in the wrong direction. He gets them off the truck and tries to make his way back east.
They meet a farmer named Dan and his daughter Anna, with whom they spend the night. The next morning, Ted picks up the newspaper and finds out that New York thinks they're kidnappers. He also reads about Kayla's family. Ted wants to take Kayla back to Piccadilly, but George and Anna disagree. Ted changes his mind the next morning, but before they leave for Kayla's house, Danno shows up in a helicopter. After the pig throws Danno into a rain barrel, Kayla chases the pilot away.
While distracted, George and his company escape by boarding a dug-out school bus and eventually make their way to the park where Tango and Layla are happy to see her. Danno shows up again and arrests George and Ted and captures Kayla. They return to the city, but after George receives the keys to Danno's handcuffs, they all escape by jumping out of the plane. They return to Piccadilly and all is well, except that Danno has followed them again. Kayla subdues him and throws him onto the stage door that Piccadilly opens, dropping Danno onto the mattress below.
George and Maggie watch Ted give his report to the board of directors. At first he is troubled by the adventures of the past week which have prevented him from preparing his presentation. Once George enters the room, Ted improvises a speech saying that friends are more important than work and proposes several ideas for the museum based on that idea (e.g., Father/Son Day). The board is impressed and approves his appointment.
option_1_text: Boris and Jonathan have been a couple for many years. As writer Jonathan loses himself more and more in the work of a new novel and actor Boris approaches his younger colleague Tim at film rehearsals, they unexpectedly find themselves at a turning point in their relationship and begin to question their love. Meanwhile, Jonathan's single-parent sister, Natasha, struggles to find stability for herself and her young daughter, Josie, who is finding her own way of coping with the impending end of her childhood.
option_2_text:
Nome, Alaska, 1900: Flapjack and Banty come to town to check on their gold mine claim. Saloon owner Cherry Malotte is aware of the corruption all around, including that Bennett and Clark are out to steal the men's claim.
In on the crooked scheme is the new gold commissioner, Alexander McNamara, as well as the last word of law and order in the territory, Judge Stillman. So, the bad guys usually get their way.
Cherry's old beau, Roy Glennister, returns from a trip to Europe. He is attracted to Helen Chester, the judge's niece. Roy makes the mistake of siding with McNamara, damaging his relationship with his longtime partner, Al Dextry.
Roy realizes he's been deceived as McNamara and Stillman prepare to steal at least $250,000 while the mine's case awaits appeal. Helen is now in love with Roy, who begs Dextry's forgiveness and persuades him to rob a bank to take back the wealth stolen from them. Both Glennister and Dextry don blackface to disguise themselves.
The Bronco Kid kills the marshall, but Roy gets the blame. He is arrested and a plot forms to kill him, but Cherry comes to his rescue by breaking Roy out of jail. A fierce fistfight with McNamara results in Roy getting back his mine and his girl.
option_3_text:
Werner, Hans-Jörg and Agnes, who lived under the name Martin before their gender equality, are siblings. The eldest brother, Werner, is a green state secretary in the Federal Ministry for the Environment and has as a major political goal the introduction of the Europe-wide can storage. His marriage with Signe is in crisis, his son Ralf films him in the most embarrassing situations. Hans-Jörg is a librarian at a university library. His biggest problem is his sex addiction. He impersonates female students, watches them and masturbates in the ladies' room. Agnes lives with a proletarian lover, but he constantly insults her and eventually throws her out of the apartment. The relationship of the three siblings to the egocentric father Günther is different. Werner considers the visits to him more than a duty, Hans-Jörg has a real hatred against his father, as he suspects that he abused his youngest child as a child, which then led to transsexuality. Only Agnes' relationship with her father seems to be half intact.
Hans-Jörg's voyeuristic activities at work are discovered, and he loses his job. After observing another visit to Agnes's father, he comes to the wrong conclusion that he is correct in his suspicions of abuse, and shoots the father at night. So he turns to Manni Moneto, a porn producer he met at his sex addiction support group. During the shooting, he meets the attractive Desirée, with whom he falls in love and tells her about his deed. She suggests that they go abroad together. He says goodbye to Agnes without revealing to her that he murdered her father. Eventually, Agnes dies of her illness, but happily remembers her childhood as Martin in the hour of death.
option_4_text:
At the beginning of World War I, two young Italian recruits, Oreste Jacovacci (Alberto Sordi), from Rome; and Giovanni Busacca (Vittorio Gassman), from Milan, meet at the recruiting offices. Oreste, a swindler, deceives the naive Giovanni, an idealist and social rebel, and manages to escape with some of his money. But they meet again on the train that will take them to the regiment to which they are assigned. Giovanni travels completely shaved. After a fight, they realize that despite having very different personalities, they have something in common: an absolute lack of patriotism and courage, and a friendship begins between them.
They begin their military training, and soon are classified as "inefficient" in the midst of grotesque and comic situations. Oreste and Giovanni volunteer as couriers to escape from the trenches and go to the nearby village to have fun, but when they return to the company they find that in the meantime there has been a major attack by the enemy that has caused numerous casualties, with which they feel lucky.
Time, months and years, begin to pass between battles, missions and periods of rest. All against a backdrop of slaughter, death, hunger and cold. Giovanni befriends Costantina (Silvana Mangano), a prostitute, and the war does not seem so hard to the protagonists, between comrades in arms and peasants, while Oreste and Giovanni strive to avoid all risks, get out of the war unharmed, and spend their service in the army in the most comfortable way possible.
The war front changes permanently, the two friends are witnesses of the serious defeat of Caporetto and shortly after, already in 1918, they are tasked with a mission as messengers. True to their desire to avoid danger and fatigue, Oreste and Giovanni stay overnight at a farm near the front but are isolated when they notice that the Austrian army has advanced to that position while they sleep. They try to escape but are discovered by enemy soldiers and brought before an Austrian officer to be shot as spies. There they confess that they are messengers and that they want to surrender, even offering information about an Italian offensive in the Piave, but the Austrian officer does not believe them and rather mocks the lack of courage of the Italians. Giovanni, offended, insults the Austrian and ends up being shot to Oreste's consternation. The officer presses Oreste to know the situation of a bridge of boats that has been built by the Italian army, but Oreste refuses to give the information claiming not to know about it and is shot.
The film ends by showing the Austrian retreat at the Battle of the Piave and the Italian advance, which reaches the farm where Oreste and Giovanni have been shot. The Italian soldiers advance through the newly taken farm, and the camera shows the lying bodies of the two protagonists, hearing the comments of their comrades who consider them fugitives, unaware of their shootings.

query_text: King Louis XIII of France has twin sons. The reason of the State requires him to give up one of the two, who is entrusted to the care of the Musketeer D'Artagnan. Little Philip is thus kept secret and raised in the fief that his father has given him. On the occasion of the succession to the throne, while the Dauphin of France is preparing to become king, Philip is arrested and, imprisoned in a secret cell, an iron mask is imposed on him to completely hide his face. D'Artagnan and the Three Musketeers will try to free him.
option_0_text:
Written in Birmingham, England, the novel tells the story of a young man named Ichabod Crane, a native of Connecticut. He settled as a teacher in the Sleepy Hollow in Greensburgh (nicknamed Tarrytown by the wives of the surrounding villages because of their husbands' habit of hanging out in taverns), near Tappan Zee. Ichabod Crane leads a nomadic life, housed and fed by the farmers of Tarrytown. He is drawn to the fantastic tales of ghosts, witches, and ghosts that abound in Tarrytown. According to Washington Irving, a German doctor or a Native American chief may have cast a spell on Sleepy Hollow, causing its inhabitants to have all sorts of hallucinations.
Ichabod Crane wishes to marry Katrina Van Tassel, the daughter of a wealthy farmer. However, he has to face a formidable rival: Brom Van Brunt, nicknamed  Brom Bones. Following a reception given by Baltus Van Tassel, Katrina's father, Ichabod attempts to have a conversation with Katrina. The story is very vague as to the content of their discussion and does not record any words; we only know that the young Ichabod went away, looking distressed. On the way home, the Headless Horseman (Dullahan), believed to be the ghost of a Hessian mercenary decapitated by a cannonball during the American Revolutionary War, appears to him. Ichabod Crane is pursued by the Headless Horseman until he reaches a small church not far away. The Horseman then uses his head as a projectile and hits Ichabod Crane in the head. The next day, the people of Greensburg went looking for him, but found only the saddle of Ichabod's horse, his hat, and further away, a pumpkin. As for Ichabod Crane, he's missing, so it's not clear whether he's dead or alive. The story nevertheless suggests that it was in fact his rival,  Brom Bones, who disguised himself to frighten the young teacher, and threw a pumpkin at him, forcing him to leave the village, and then set off for new prey.
option_1_text:
In 1638, King Louis XIII was delighted when his wife gave him a son, Louis, the heir to the throne. However, a few minutes later a second son was born. Colbert, the king's trusted advisor, persuaded the king to secretly send the second child, Philip, to Gascony to be raised by a friend of His Majesty, d'Artagnan, in order to avoid a possible civil war later. Fouquet, a simple messenger of the cardinal at the time, discovers the existence of the twin and uses it to advance his career. Twenty years later, he was Minister of Finance under Louis XIV. The king is hated by the commoners for raising oppressive taxes and executing them for not paying them.
Fouquet sent soldiers to force d'Artagnan and his loyalists to pay the taxes, although the old king had exempted him and his village. They were driven out, but returned in much larger numbers and, with great difficulty, captured D'Artagnan, the Three Musketeers and Philip. Louis is about to order their executions when Colbert tells him of Philip's strange resemblance to him. As Louis was aware of an assassination attempt that was to take place that day (but not where or when), he made Philip appear to be him in exchange for the lives of his friends. Philip not only survives the ambush, he shows mercy to his would-be assassins and is acclaimed by the people. Princess Marie-Thérèse, whom Louis must marry to seal an alliance with Spain, finds this new Louis much more attractive than the real one. However, when she discovers that Louis is having an affair with Mademoiselle de la Vallière she returns to Spain.
When the truth was discovered, Louis had Philip imprisoned with an iron mask placed over his face, hoping that Philip's beard would grow inside the mask and eventually suffocate him. Philippe is rescued by the Musketeers, who break into Louis's bedroom and imprison him in the mask. The Musketeers dragged him away and locked him in the Bastille, where the prison guards mistook him for Philip, and whipped him.
When Louis succeeded in getting a message to Fouquet, he was released, and a lawsuit ensued to prevent Philip from marrying Marie-Thérèse and taking Louis' place on the throne. The stagecoach is spotted by the Musketeers, who all die heroically, but Fouquet and the real Louis XIV are also killed when the driverless stagecoach plunges off a cliff. The mortally wounded d'Artagnan survives long enough to exclaim "God Save the King!" at Philip's wedding, then falls dead. Philip finally takes the throne.
option_2_text:
A small English village in Cornwall at the turn of the century. Harry George Spalding inherits from his late brother Charles a house in a small village. Bartender Tom Bailey tells him of a grisly series of murders that will soon be known simply as the "Black Death" because the victims all share the same characteristic: bite marks on their necks that point to a large snake and a peculiar skin discoloration. The dead brother also fell victim to this mysterious creature. Harry now tries to get to the bottom of these strange recent events, but no one in the village seems to really want to help him, there is too much fear that he himself could be the next victim.
In this world of small people and quirky types there seems to be only one man of high intelligence: the equally dismissive and educated Dr. Franklyn, a man who, as an explorer, is considered a capacity in all things having to do with India and adjoining areas, where he has often set off on exploratory journeys. Franklyn lives in seclusion in a country house on the other side of the moor, largely staying away from the villagers. Even Spalding's visit to Well House, the name of his residence, seems anything but enthusiastic. Franklin's daughter Anna is punished by her cold and hard-hearted father with outright contempt, and even the house servant, called "Malaie" for short, whom Dr. Franklin once brought with him from one of his travels, is anything but talkative. More help in his investigations comes from the deranged villager Peter, whom everyone calls "mad Peter". He warns the Spaldings not to investigate further and advises them to leave the area as soon as possible. A short time later, he too is dead, with the same skin discoloration and bite marks that had marked the other recent deaths, as Harry and Tom, who examined Peter more closely and then excavated Charles' body, must find.
Shortly afterwards, Harry receives a message from Dr. Franklyn and rushes there. There he is attacked and bitten in the throat by a giant reptilian creature with a serpentlike head. With the last of his strength, Harry can save himself. Meanwhile, his wife, Valerie, witnesses a grisly event as Dr. Franklyn attempts to murder his apparently cursed daughter. What no one knew until now was that Anna had once fallen into the clutches of a snake-worshipping sect, a cobra cult from the Far East. As a punishment for Franklin's involvement with the Malayan-Indian cult, his daughter was sentenced to regularly transform into a man-sized king cobra, whose bites brought death and destruction to the inhabitants of the small town. A life-and-death struggle ensues between Dr. Franklyn and his mute servant, the Malay, also a member of the snake cult. In the scuffle, a lamp is knocked over, and the property catches fire. Dr. Franklyn is finally bitten by his own daughter, and father and daughter perish in the flames. Harry and Valerie can escape this hell at the last moment.
option_3_text:
Young farmer Gabriel Oak, leading a frugal life and saving and borrowing, runs a sheep farm. He falls in love with the beautiful, but poor, Bathsheba Everdene, newly arrived to live with his aunt, and asks for her hand in marriage. Bathsheba refuses him. After a few months, the social status between the two was reversed: Bathsheba inherited her uncle's farm, and Oak lost all his possessions in a stormy night. Oak then finds himself in Bathsheba's employ, first as a shepherd and then as a farmer; and he is thus able to observe from her and her other employees, the colorful inhabitants of the country. Bathsheba wins the hearts of all the men she meets, but only one, at first, seems indifferent to her charm: her neighbour on the farm, William Boldwood. Bathsheba jokingly sends him a Valentine's card.
The man becomes inflamed and begins to burn with love for her. Bathsheba barely manages to prevent an engagement between them, taking time; meanwhile a new sergeant arrives in the village, the bald Francis Troy. For the first time in her life, the contemptuous Bathsheba falls in love, yields to Troy's flattery, and marries him after a few days. Troy begins to squander Bathsheba's wealth, but that's not all: his previous relationship with a waitress, Fanny Robin, whom he had seduced and abandoned, also comes to light. When Fanny dies in childbirth, Troy suddenly rediscovers all his love for her, has her build a monumental tomb and runs away from home.
He is believed to have drowned at sea and Bathsheba is recognized by all as a widow; Boldwood begins courting her again, obtaining a promise of marriage from her at the age of six. However, when Troy suddenly responds and claims his wife, Boldwood, who had already shown signs of mental imbalance, kills him and is sentenced to death (he will later be pardoned and deported to Australia). A true widow, Bath-sheba eventually marries her first suitor, Gabriel Oak, who had not stopped watching over her and loving her all those years.
option_4_text:
Deeply depressed at his dead-end job in the mail room of a New York City newspaper, Lemuel Gulliver decides to impress journalist Darcy Silverman. He convinces her he could write a report about his (false) extensive world "travels" saying his dream is to become a writer. After suffering writer's block and thinking that Darcy will not want to hang out with a "guy from the mailroom", Gulliver plagiarises a report from other publications on the internet. The next day, Darcy, impressed by his writing, presents Gulliver with a new task – to travel to the Bermuda Triangle and write an article about the legends of ships mysteriously disappearing there.
Upon arriving in Bermuda, Gulliver rents a ship and travels into the triangle. After falling asleep at the helm of his ship, Gulliver is accidentally caught in a freak storm and the ship is overwhelmed by a waterspout in the process,. Gulliver washes up unconscious on the shore of Lilliput, where he is immediately confirmed as a "beast" by the town's tiny people. After the citizens claim him to be dangerous because of his size, Gulliver is captured and imprisoned in a cave. There, he meets another prisoner named Horatio who was jailed by General Edward because he loves Princess Mary of Lilliput, despite Edward also pursuing her. After the island across from Lilliput, Blefuscia, orders some commandos to kidnap Princess Mary, Gulliver manages to break free of the plough-machine he is forced to work and then rescues the princess from being kidnapped. Gulliver also saves her father, King Theodore, from a fire by urinating on it.
Gulliver is declared a hero by Lilliput's citizens and lies that he is the President of Manhattan, says Yoda is his vice-president and a living legend in his homeland. Edward, however, becomes enraged due to the luxurious accommodations that have been built for Gulliver, and for being presented as an honorary general of the Lilliputian Army complete with uniform. The townspeople find Gulliver's boat and his things, when Gulliver receives angry voicemails from Darcy, who has to take his place and travel to Bermuda now, and she has found out about his plagiarism and now hates him. The next day, chaos ensues as the Blefuscian Navy lays siege to the city when Edward shuts down its defense system as an act of revenge for Gulliver's treatment. Gulliver defeats the armada, invulnerable to the cannonballs being fired at him (although he receives numerous welts on his stomach). Embarrassed once more, and with Mary no longer wanting to have anything to do with him, Edward defects to the Blefuscians and brings with him blueprints of a robot he had made from a page he'd seen from Gulliver's Guitar Hero III game manual. The Blefuscians secretly build the robot, with Edward as the pilot.
The Blefuscians invade Lilliput and the robot-wielding Edward makes Gulliver admit to the people that he is "just the guy from the mail-room" and nothing more. Edward banishes Gulliver to the shores of "the island where we dare not go" (Brobdingnag). There, he is snatched up by a "little" girl (Glumdalclitch) who towers over him. She captures him easily by trapping him inside a glass cup. When Gulliver wakes up, he finds himself in a pink dress in a bedroom of a doll house which begins to shake when the "little girl" pulls apart the wall of the bedroom who begins to stare emotionlessly and ominously at a tiny defenseless Gulliver. He then screams fearfully at the sight of the quiet giant "little" girl, she shoves a milk bottle in his mouth and forcefully feeds him excess milk. The girl treats him as a doll, playing with him roughly. Horatio, who has gone to find Gulliver after being spurned by Mary, reveals to Gulliver that Darcy was imprisoned by the Blefuscians after she was lost in the Bermuda Triangle in the same manner as Gulliver. Gulliver narrowly escapes with him, using a parachute that he took from the skeleton of a dead U.S. Air Force pilot sitting in the dollhouse.
Once again accepting a duel from Edward, this time not only for Lilliput's freedom but for its fate as well – as Edward threatens to destroy it should Gulliver fail – Gulliver ultimately defeats him with the assistance of Horatio, who disables the machine's electrocuting weapon. Horatio is hailed a hero and gets King Theodore's permission to court the princess. Edward, reaching the point of insanity, threatens to kill the princess, but the princess, finally having enough of Edward, punches the traitor in the face in frustration. When King Theodore decides to sentence all Blefuscians to the gallows or to prepare for war, Gulliver then helps to make peace between the rival island-nations by reciting Edwin Starr's "War" and he, along with Darcy, return to New York City on their repaired ship. The film ends with Gulliver, now a legitimate travel writer, taking Darcy to lunch while holding hands, after returning from another travel assignment.
